author: Ravenstone
subject: Rework Judgement and Restore JotC
content_md:
**Rework Judgement**
My Judgement proposal is simple. Take the damage from Judgement of Righteousness, and apply it to the Judgement spell so that every time you judge, regardless of your Seal, you deal Holy damage. JoR and JoC would need to be reworked, but I'll get to that in a bit.

 **Restore Judgement of the Crusader**
My second proposal is to restore Judgement of the Crusader and it stems from the fact that Paladins now feel completely unvanilla. The new Judgement of the Crusader is increadibly unthematic and has had its original purpose entirely been replaced by an awful spell in Crusader Strike. The new JotC currently makes me feel like some rare weapons collector, carrying around different weapons just for their special effects, and has already led to a whole exercise of nerfing specific weapon interactions just to force the change to work in a more balanced way. It also pidgeonholed Paladins into becoming Nightfall bots which I think is a terrible direction to take them.

Crusader Strike is OP in PvP. Its spammable, which means it can be abused in AV/AB to prevent anyone from capping a flag in conjunction with Divine Shield for a full 12 seconds. It also provides 5 quick, separate instances in which you can proc Vengence, which in conjuction with Holy Strike double dips to deal insane damage bypassing armor entirely, which means you can run at a flag carrier surrounded by his team in WSG, Divine Shield, spam Crusader Strikes and then blow him up with a Holy Strike/Judgement combo. The only area Crusader Strike works for is PvE, but at the expense of the vanilla JotC, and PvP as described above. Crusader Strike was a mistake and should be removed.

 **Tying them both together**
With my first proposed change, it shouldn't feel as bad to use SotC as you will be dealing Holy damage each time you Judge. This will be a massive improvement already from how it was in Vanilla. Part of the problem around vanilla SotC is that it looks like a DPS seal, but its Judgement is only usable once, so it was much like the other Judgements just applied once and forgotten about. This led to the Seals feeling inconsistent and basically split into two categories, the two damage ones, SoR and SoC, and the rest being utility ones. With this change, it shouldn't feel so punishing to switch to a different Seal during battle as you can still maintain Judgement damage.

I think it still has some drawbacks, notably that only one person would be able to really use SotC/JotC, but I believe it is a step in a better direction than what we currently have. SotC could still do with a rework IMO but I don't really want to discuss that here if possible.

 **Judgement of Command and Righteousness reworks**
Back to the judgements, obviously, we don't want SoR and SoC to be doing double damage, so they'll need to be modified. SoC is simple and can just deal its extra damage when the target is stunned so that its basically the same damage it is now. For SoR I'd propose the Judgement deals extra threat if to help Paladin Tanks maintain single target threat a bit more reliably. I don't think this is anything too drastic and SoR is the tanking Seal anyway.

I don't think the Judgement change really impacts PvP all that drastically from what we already have, although I acknowledge it is a buff. I think the benefits out weigh the negatives there though. I believe removing Crusader Strike is a well deserved nerf to the current Paladin in PvP, though Holy Strike still needs to be fixed from one-shotting everything, however, I'd like it if this thread didn't get derailed too much from Holy Strike discussion though.

Thoughts?

author: Bob022
subject: Re: Rework Judgement and Restore JotC
content_md:
My first thought is, after near enough to two decades, I am thoroughly tired of PvP acting like an anchor holding back PvE.

My second thought is, easier way to fix Crusader Strike without taking away (most) its good, and without deleting it outright:  Triple its cooldown (to three globals or so), increase debuff effect to 5% per, max 3 stack, problem largely solved.  Can't be rapidly spammed anymore, but retains the positive of allowing individual paladins to actually use the Crusader debuff in PvE.  Wisdom pretty much always has to be judged for mana reasons, save for using Justice to taunt or stop critical runners, so reverting to the old Judgement of Crusader effect simply means it goes back to being largely un-used like before.  Don't want to go back there.  That's the problem with "Here's several judgement effects--pick one" ability design when one is much more important than the others.

Abilities like Holy Strike double-dipping from Vengeance should be regarded as a glitch and altered, if that's possible.

The above being said, I don't much like the new Judgement effect associated with Seal of Crusader, either.  The game and its items weren't designed for proc-on-demand--in PvE, PvP, anywhere.  As such this one causes more trouble than it's worth.  Give Judgement of Crusader a Holy damage-over-time effect (undead only even!), the Vindication debuff (freeing up those talent tree slots for other ideas), a Thunderclap-style speed debuff, almost anything else is less problematic.

Tying damage to Judgement and adding threat to Judgement of Righteous, I'm neutral there, there are too many possible interactions (such as with the talented Justice taunt) to be able to form a hard stance without seeing the specific implementation in operation.

author: Borzy
subject: Re: Rework Judgement and Restore JotC
content_md:
Haven't quite made to 60 yet, but some thoughts.

- I too don't understand the new JotC.  It's like a brand new mechanic that, if true that weapons have had to be re-balanced to not make this ability too OP, just sounds like more work than was required.  It may be a fun thing, but it's a complete break from Vanilla.

- I don't understand how SoC was fixed in any way.  It's still the same random proc based ability.  The extra-talent to gain mana back seem insignificant, and does not fix the pally's mana hungry playstyle.

- Crusader strike likewise just requires more mana.  I think there need to be a break from some of the nonsense Vanilla designs:  why is it that pallys need to have this "extra holy dmg" debuff thing to just do damage?  Especially considering pallys are the only one who do holy dmg? (I assume holy priest isn't a viable dps build mostly)  Why not just get rid of it and balance our dmg outright more like the other classes?  I can't think of another class that expends resource to apply a debuff that is used to increase "a portion" of your damage.

- Divine Intellect and Divine strength are still 2 separate talents, in the HOLY tree.  This really needed to be fixed.  A simple fix to the pally's mana issue would have been to roll the two into one, and make it so that there's a talent... in the RETRIBUTION tree, called Divine Intellect, that basically gives you intellect based on a % of strength.  That allows the pally to just stack strength for AP, and at the same time reward us with the mana pool to deal the damage.  This will also fix itemization issues, because now you can just give pallys and warrior essentially same gear, without having to have a separate pool of plate with intellect.

- And many things still missing after all these fixes:
 - direct taunt
 - cleave ability (on demand multi target strike)
 - ranged pull
 - final Retribution talent is still a sub-par CC with a 1 minute cooldown
And I will parrot another point raised above:  I detest PVP in WoW.   It is the root of so many problems that RPGs have to deal with "balance", that it removes pretty much all aspect of an "RPG" (where each class is just unique in their problem solving ability) and instead balance all classes so they pretty much all do the same thing.

subject: Re: Does Ret Paladins have huge mana issues?
content_md: I wanted to give my impressions as someone who’s been leveling ret and is level 34 now, so take this with a grain of salt because I haven’t been leveling too long. But after some trial and error, I’ve found a solution that works for me: just don’t level in the meta way (auto attacking, never using crusader and holy strike, and rarely judging to keep mana) instead, try and stack up on intelligence when you can along with strength and stam, spec into heart of the crusader as well, during rotation actually use crusader strike 1-3 times depending on mob health, and use judgement and holy strike when you can and when mana allows. Is it gonna be the most efficient best leveling spec? Nah. You will have to stop and drink every 4 mobs or so as well, but it’s actually fun to level, it’s actually an interesting somewhat engaging rotation that doesn’t just have you auto attacking and spacing out. To be clear, it’s NOT meta, but to me it’s much more worth it for the leveling to actually be fun, keeps me playing for longer and makes me not regret playing paladin. Plus with heart of the crusader and 1-3 crusader strikes on a mob, it’s fun to see the extra damage, even if small, and holy strike hits for big numbers, and big numbers feel good. And IMO it feeling good is more important than it being 100% optimized and efficient. Just my two cents though.

author: Portholes
subject: Re: Ret and Prot in raids?
content_md:
The answer is yes Prot Paladins can tank.
Do they have their weaknessess? yes.
Do they still need more work? yes.
Are they better than they were in vanilla/classic? yes.
Would most still prefer a geared warrior or bear tank on most fights? yes.

Paladin is good for fights like Nefarian because he will do a "class call" and affect classes differently:
Druids are forced into  Cat Form for 30 seconds by  Involuntary Transformation.
Hunters have their equipped ranged weapons instantly broken. You can counter this by equipping a different weapon right before a Class Call comes out, then equipping your real weapon after the call passes.
Mages will polymorph raid members into animals like giraffes, cows and worms with  Wild Polymorph.
Priests are afflicted with  Corrupted Healing, causing the targets of any direct heals they cast to be debuffed by  Corrupted Healing, dealing 44 to 56 damage every 1 sec, stacking up to 50 times.
Paladins receive  Siphon Blessing, forcing them to continuously cast  Blessing of Protection on Nefarian.
Rogues are teleported in front of Nefarian and immobilized, leaving them open to his Cleave and breath attacks. Tank repositioning usually saves Rogues from this call.
Shaman will be under the effect of  Corrupted Totems, summoning powerful versions of the Shaman's various totems that will buff Nefarian and damage the raid.
Warlocks will be forced to  Summon Infernals, summoning two Corrupted Infernals per warlock to start attacking the raid.
Warriors will  Berserk, forcing them into a modified  Berserker Stance, increasing damage taken. After the call is over, Warriors must manually return to their desired stance.

So Paladin tanks don't really get much of a debuff on this fight like Druids (forced cat form) and Warriors (Berserker Stance)

And just as a note. Most things on this server are viable, but thats a very subjective opinion.  Some think that optimal and viable are synonymous so they'd disagree.  Something like ret, are you going to be at the top of the meters? most likely not but that depends on the player, gear, consumables, and who you're competing against.  Just remember that your strength as a pally mostly comes from your buffs.

author: Kairion
subject: Re: Ret and Prot in raids?
content_md:
First things first.
The Video of Tanking Chromaggus has to be taken with a big pinch of salt. Worldbuffs are gone as is the weapon that is likely used to tank him in this footage. This weapon was essential to tanking mobs with damage reduction against holy spells. As it dealt your physical damage as holy.
Since this can no longer be done, the Threat generation for paladin in this fight is atrocious and you REALLY want a druid/warrior tank for chromaggus.

Mana sustain i'm a bit of split opinion. On one hand you are prone to going oom mid bossfight without support. But you are in a 40 man Raid. Getting BoW, JoW on the target and WF support as a tank is not too much to ask for. A Shadowpriest or a Arcane mage are also possible solutions for the manaproblems. As is using Innervate or tea with sugar.

For 5 mans mana sustain via blocking and jow is totally sufficient.

Reploidrocsa surely raids in a different guild than i do. We successfully employ multiple paladin tanks in all raids. Sure we can't tank Fear bosses or Chromaggus but otherwise our threat is sufficient for all encounters.

TLDR: Paladin surely ain't as good as warrior for raid tanking, but i'd take a good paladin over a bad warrior any day of the week.

author: Geojak
subject: Re: Ret and Prot in raids?
content_md:
Prot pala needs gear from the next higher raid to perform well.

For mc you need zg gear
For bwl you need aq40 hear.

What I mean with need here is, to be equal to a warrior or druid tank with one lvl lower gear.
So a aq40 prot pala is as good as a bwl t2 warrior.

For progression coming from mc first time into bwl, the prot pala is a liability to the raid. It's just how it is.
They oom, they are squishier, they have worse Single tsrget threat, they have worse taunt.

Yes prot pala can tank raids. But is it good?
Moonkins can dps in raids too but they ain't mages.
You end up with slower clear times and more wipes when a tank gets nuked or DD pulls aggro that coild have been avoided with a warrior shield wall or aoe taunt.

This wasnt meant as a rant, just to clear up how it is. I am mostly OK with this as a paladin myself.

Regarding rets, They are great. With sp flask you csn top the dps Meter against non flasking raid. Generally not a liability, as you are needed for judgement, Decurse, not too bad dps anymore provided you have wf or shadow oil.

I'm pleased I'm not the only person who remembers using Seal of Fury.  I also regarded Righteous Fury as a gigantic nerf to the class--by design, since that was the period where Blizzard had grown hostile towards paladins doing the tank job in general.  Heck I liked the way the talent trees were laid out back then better, too.  21 prot for holy shield and 21 ret for consecrate left a decent amount of points left over for personal preference.  Think we probably all miss pre-nerf defense gear.  Add everything together I'm not sure the T-wow paladin is actually better as a tank than that version was...different set of strengths and weaknesses.  1.12 is such a rough spot to start from.

Pre-RF Consecrate wouldn't necessarily keep aggro off AE damage dealers, but I could keep the healers reliably safe.  There was something going on, maybe with Seal of Fury, maybe with Consecrate itself, that made the effects work better than might be expected for holding threat.

author: Whoopie
subject: How to fix Paladin in PvP
content_md:
The headache for most is how powerful and unstoppable Paladins are in PvP currently. Paladins are able to get complete immunity and then oneshot people. Their immensly strong Divine Shield and Holy Shock spells need some adjustments to make PvP and faction balance a little more leveled.

How to fix it?
 **1. Divine Shield** - Reduce Paladin's damage by 50% for the duration of the Divine Shield. This has been part of the game since TBC and it makes a lot of sense.

 **2. Holy Shock** - Reduce it's damage by 20% and make cooldown longer when used offsensively, lower when used deffensively - For example if you heal an ally, make it 15 seconds cooldown, if you hit en enemy, make it 25 seconds cooldown. This will actually make "the last talent in Holy tree" be a Healing spell, rather than damaging one, while still offering good damage output if needed.

Holy Shock** - Reduce it's damage by 20% and make cooldown longer when used offsensively, lower when used deffensively - For example if you heal an ally, make it 15 seconds cooldown, if you hit en enemy, make it 25 seconds cooldown. Holy shock doesn't need to be messed with, I have 160 spell power and with a full 5 stacks Crusader Strike (with pvp gloves bonus) I crit for 1200 dmg, without building stacks its closer to 1k.  Not exactly game breaking on a non-spammable CD.  Pales in comparison to an ele shaman's burst.

content_html:
The headache for most is how powerful and unstoppable Paladins are in PvP currently. Paladins are able to get complete immunity and then oneshot people. Their immensly strong Divine Shield and Holy Shock spells need some adjustments to make PvP and faction balance a little more leveled.

How to fix it?
1. Divine Shield - Reduce Paladin's damage by 50% for the duration of the Divine Shield. This has been part of the game since TBC and it makes a lot of sense.

2. Holy Shock - Reduce it's damage by 20% and make cooldown longer when used offsensively, lower when used deffensively - For example if you heal an ally, make it 15 seconds cooldown, if you hit en enemy, make it 25 seconds cooldown. This will actually make "the last talent in Holy tree" be a Healing spell, rather than damaging one, while still offering good damage output if needed.
Holy shock doesn't need to be messed with, I have 160 spell power and with a full 5 stacks Crusader Strike (with pvp gloves bonus) I crit for 1200 dmg, without building stacks its closer to 1k. Not exactly game breaking on a non-spammable CD. Pales in comparison to an ele shaman's burst.

I would be fine with a Divine Shield dmg penalty.

author: Ravenstone
subject: Extra Threat for Seal/Judge of Righteousness
content_md:
One of the problems Paladin's have when tanking is smooth threat gen, particularly when beginning a fight. Having your first Holy Strike and Judgement miss/resist can really mess things up. I've [suggested it before briefly](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=6294), but my proposal is to give the Seal and Judgement on Righteousness an additional threat component, akin to Shield Slam or the plethora of other Warrior abilities with inbuilt "causes a high amount of threat". This harkens back to the pre 1.9 Seal of Fury that Paladin's had as Darg727 and Bob022 elaborated on [here and further on in the thread](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=42651#p42651).

> **Darg727 wrote: Sat Apr 22, 2023 11:08 pm**
> Seal of Fury was the original iteration of a tanking seal for paladin. It added 90 base TPS per swing along with 4 phantom swings to proc weapon procs and judgements. The judgement gave 337 base threat every time it was hit with a holy damage effect: SoR, holy shield, JoR, holy shock, consecration, smite, etc.

I believe part of the problem with the Paladin design is that you are reliant on Holy Damage to achieve your threat. Now inherently there is nothing too problematic about this if there were properly statted items for this style of play, but currently these do not exist to the extent that Paladin's would need them. I also think it would be harder to balance since I feel that Paladins need far more from their gear stats wise than Warriors do and could introduce more problems. Giving Paladins extra inbuilt threat on SoR/JoR would lessen the impact of lack of proper itemisation (though this should definitely still be looked at).

This change could also serve as the start to diversifying the Seals a bit more as currently SoR is better for DPS than both SoC and SotC. Having SoR as the Seal of choice 95% of the time is just not good from a design perspective. SotC and SoC can't be brought back into play unless SoR is toned down.

I should say that this would probably have a knock on impact to the current SoR MCP spellret DPS builds that are out there. Now, I'm not too familiar with the actual threat they output, but in my opinion this style of play isn't particularly appealing from either a gameplay or thematic point of views and I'd prefer Retadins to DPS without having to rely on such a gimmicky style, and therefore would be a necessary casuality for the sake of a better Paladin.

Thank you for reading, please let me know what you think.

author: Darg727
subject: Re: Extra Threat for Seal/Judge of Righteousness
content_md:
Paladin dungeon threat is just fine. I think the biggest point people have a hard time wrapping their heads around is that threat is like a pool. You only need enough to swim. Too little and you trudge extra slow, too much and you might not have enough in other pools when people jump in. A mistake I see a lot is paladins not using  BoSalvation. This is our D-stance or bear form. In layman's terms it, for all tense and purposes, gives ~43% more threat on everything we do. Righteous fury is like the extra threat on heroic strike, it's just extra. It's the reason shaman aren't designed to be tanks. They don't have an d-stance equivalent of their own. Though, like any class, they can make use of BoSalv on turtle.

If a target has 5000 hp, your group is the standard 1/3/1 comp, you should only need to do ~700 threat to keep aggro until it's dead. At 20,000 hp you should only need to do about 3,500 threat. Of course, these are minimum values based on evenly distributed threat between the dps in the group. If there is only one target to beat up on, you'll be able to bring the full force of your single target threat generation to bare which makes 1 dps doing the work of 2 not much of a problem.

One thing I haven't checked is whether seal buff threat is a thing on this server (equal to the level at which you trained it × RF bonus)

Where paladin threat gets wonky is raiding. The poor scaling and cooldown/mana constraints means that while warrior and druid threat generation grows by leaps and bounds, paladin threat generation practically stagnates without greater blessing usage. That said, it is a paladin unique way to scale threat generation. Though I think I can speak for all paladins in this regard, the spell component cost is quite annoying. Though much less than farming MCPs.

> To be honest this feels more like an attempt to nerf spellret by a player who hates spellret, than an attempt to buff protpally by a player who loves protpally. There are many approaches they can make to this that don't involve killing another spec, especially one as unique and fresh as spellret. What that spec needs is to fix all the jank with it and keep the good core (the reliance on very weird items, the threat capping). Spellret is the way to go if they want paladins to be viable pve dps and not broken in pvp.

I will admit I don't like the current Spellret that relies on MCP or Dragonbreathe Chili, but this isn't my main driver behind this.

I believe that Prot Pallys require too much itemwise to be good, and that there will be an overreliance on SP to generate threat. It can work in the first place because Righteous Fury provides a huge boost to threat Holy damage does, but if you have to trade a lot of survivability for it then it forces Paladin too tightly into a corner. Prot Warrior tanks only really need Stamina, Strength and some defence stats, but Prot Pallys would require SP and potentially Int as well.

I also wish to see the return of JotC rather than the awful current implementations of CS and JotC, which iv made abundantly clear in other threads. The only way I can see the old JotC returning though is if it is buffed to also do holy damage. This change is simply to help cement SoR as the tanking Seal, and allow SotC and SoC to be used as DPS Seals, rather than the current situation where SoR is the best Seal for tanking and DPS.

Regarding Spellret, I believe that Spellret can't realistically work without completely reworking Ret in a way that will make them unvanilla. SP coefficients and SP itemisation budgets will always mean that you get less than investing in AP. Spellret really only currently works because Dragonbreath Chili has a 100% SP coefficient. I'm not against Spellret in general but I can't see how it would ever work without a massive overhaul.

author: Darg727
subject: Re: Extra Threat for Seal/Judge of Righteousness
content_md:
> **Ravenstone wrote: Sun May 14, 2023 7:16 pm**
> I have to disagree with you here. I'd argue that RF is like Defensive Stance extra threat, and that Paladins don't have the equivalent inbuilt extra threat abilities that Warrior has, because when it comes to raiding, regardless of which tank you have, you will always have Salvation up. Therefore Warriors have the extra threat whilst Paladins don't. Sunder Armor as an example gives 261 threat by default, with an additional 45% coming from Defensive Stance + Defiance modifier. The ability itself still inherently generates decent threat at a quick pace which Paladins don't have. Paladins have either this trickle of threat, or high burst threat, nothing in between like Sunder.
>
>  In dungeons I can see your reasoning, and yes they are fine, up until ZF from my experience. Even with BoSalvation, I found I couldn't hold threat on well geared people, and I suspect it is largely due to the fact Paladins don't have the gear to boost their Holy damage quite like the other classes do to boost their DPS stats. But then I feel like Paladins will be too dependant overall on getting SP gear to boost threat gen.

First off, of course you aren't going to hold threat on people that out gear you and don't let you build a lead. That's literally how the system is designed: for people to pay attention to threat. Warriors and druids have the exact same issues while leveling, they just have taunt as a base ability for a crutch. The reason dps should let you build a lead is not because you don't generate enough threat, it's because there are random elements baked into tanking like miss/dodge/parry.

As for why you specifically aren't holding threat there are a multitude of reasons beyond just what your party member is wearing. Warrior heroic strike does additional threat, a rogue ambush/backstab crit is a huge amount of damage, etc. What kind of rotation are you doing? Using a slow weapon with holy strike and dropping a consecrate I'm pretty much able to keep threat on just about anything.

Now to the equivalence argument. RF is definitely not like defensive stance. It might have once been when fishbringer did 100% holy damage, if you even had it. However, it just doesn't provide enough global threat to be treated as such. Mathematically speaking, all it does is let you catch up with the base threat warrior abilities provide like how druid's maul/swipe have a 75% built in multiplier. It doesn't seem like that because of the existence of HS and how well a paladin can spread threat to a group. For RF to actually be considered equivalent, the threat multiplier needs to be increased, ignoring consecration. And it's not about the gear, you get new ranks increasing your damage and threat as you level. Sunder doesn't scale with AP or weapon damage for example.

Paladin was never designed to be a raid tank in vanilla. It's as simple as that. BoSalv not counting as a self only d-stance in large groups was the point from the beginning. It wasn't any different from the beta Seal of Salvation spell which was castable on others.

> **Ravenstone wrote: Sun May 14, 2023 7:16 pm**
> Yes, it is in raiding in particular that the problems really show. Are you referring to GBoK spam to generate threat here?

I did mention greater blessings. Might is a slightly more expensive alternative to kings but it does generate the same amount of threat.

The point I was trying to make here is that a paladin's base threat doesn't scale well in a raid setting if we ignore the threat from greater blessings. GB spam is what is what makes up the difference in classic wow and HS slightly helps bridge the gap here on turtle despite the fact it unfairly suffers partial resistance. If I were to try changing anything, I'd probably lean into what we already do and I've already made a suggestion in that vein already: [The Case for Seal of the Crusader](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?f=41&t=4177). From there, it would only be a matter of whether we would want GB threat to remain or not. If so, there wouldn't be much else to do. If it were removed, the threat reduction on SotC could be removed with RF; Holy shield could be given a 100% threat multiplier, 25% spell coefficient, and a guaranteed proc of redoubt; and reckoning could have a 10% chance on a normal hit to proc (adding 10% to x% crit chance in pvp isn't going to break the talent what so ever); and/or the cast time of HoW could be removed conditionally. So many options, but it's not like we'll ever have insight for what the devs have planned or even what their goals are. For all we know, they want paladins to be subpar in everything but healing, want warriors to be 500 dps ahead of any other dps and be the optimal tank in 99% of situations. It's not like they've ever expressed where they want the game to be. That will likely never change because it means they can do nothing and people can't latch on to something and swing it back into their faces.

Point being:  The paladin plays different for good reason, and not every class's mechanics are supposed to appeal to all players.  In this sense, different is good.

author: Kwayver
subject: Re: Ret Paladin need rework
content_md:
Have said this many times across the several threads calling for/suggesting changes to ret, so i'll say it again here:

in a single moment a ret paladin can:
Holy Strike
Proc Seal of Command
Judge Command

... and none of this uses a global cooldown. Adding any form of on-demand damage to this combination will break pvp worse than it already is.

Twow claim in their class design principles that they didn't want ret to become warrior-lite, but the only 2 meaningful changes to ret's damage output that they've implemented has been a Heroic Strike knock-off and a selfish version of Sunder Armour. The attachment to Holy Strike and refusal to change Seal/Judgement of Command will trap this spec's pve potential in a corner forever.

But the worst part of all this is to be in any way viable in a raid setting ret is completely dependent on a Windfury totem. When a spec's acceptable performance is dependant on not only another class but a specific group combination highly sought after by all other melee dps, that's a clear indication of bad design.

It robbed us of our straightforward rotation of judging JoTC. And it boggles me that instead of making SotC/JotC (mostly SotC that's the problem here) interesting abilities that bring proper utility (see imp. JoTC in TBC), they leaned heavily into making it a SITUATIONAL GIMMICK ABILITY.

Yes, paladins have had their fair share of gimmicks to make gameplay interesting (see SoR fishing procs) but it was never the main thing, it was just an added bonus. It is really bad game design making us dependent on it..

author: Jolikmc
subject: Re: Macros
content_md:
The absolutely Vanilla version of this macro should be something like…
Code: Select all

```
/run --CastSpellByName("Judgement");
/cast Judgement
/run SpellStopCasting();
/run CastSpellByName("Seal of Command");
```

Notes
- "/run CastSpellByName("")" casts the **highest rank available**.  For spells without ranks, "/cast" is simplier.
- Adding two dashes before the first "CastSpellByName("")" causes the macro's icon to display the **cooldown** or **availability** of the quoted spell.  Vanilla never had proper "spell being casted" tooltips.
- There are AddOns that can add the *Burning Crusade*-style shortcuts in, as well as proper tooltips and automatic icon changing for macro icons.

 
Hope this helps!

author: Kairion
subject: Re: Ret raid rotation
content_md:
Thats not too bad of a prio list if you don't get windfury.

But generally in Raids should be among the first ones to get totem support.

So if you have Windfury you want to start the fight out with JoW/JoL
Keep **Seal of Righteousnes** up at all times. Since SoR can trigger windfury & crusader enchants it outperforms SoC in most circumstances.
Keep Holy Strike on CD
Apply 5 stacks of CS
Judge on CD (pay attention to swingtimer, you don't wanna hit without a seal active)
Drop Consecration if mana allows it
Use remaining free CDs for crusader strike (either rank 1 or max rank depending on your manapool)

Your swingspeed is still relevant if you use SoC as expected.
But when using SoR Swingspeed is also relevant in some ways. You want ideally a swingspeed of 3.4 seconds. That is slow enough so the extra wf procs are chunky and it gives you a perfect swingspeed to keep holy strike on cooldown.
If you have a swingspeed below 3.33 you can only use holy strike every 4 hits instead of every 3. If you have slower weapons, feel free to stack some haste, but if you are faster than 3.33 you might end up loosing dmg from getting more haste.

Mana will be an issue (especially starting out), Additionally to leaving out consecration, you can use holy strike rank 1 in a pinch. Particularly while lvling thats a great way to save mana!

author: Boras
subject: SoW/JoW cause zero threat and need to be fixed
content_md:
Paladins are very mana dependant and mana regeneration is a necessity in order to keep tanking effectively. They are also known as THE aoe tanks since they are able to generate so much threat to all mobs via ret aura, consecration, holy shield, redoubt, blessing of sanctuary, seal of wisdom, and judgement of wisdom.

However, there is a very serious problem with this server as wisdom procs DO NOT cause any threat whatsoever. Every point of mana regenned via a wisdom proc should give 0.5 threat. This is not the case. Righteous fury should also affect this just like seal of light and judgement of light. So, for every point of mana regenned by the prot paladin with RF on, they should be receiving 0.95 threat. This needs to be addressed immediately as it is a very game breaking bug.

All holy spells cast by the paladin are modified by righteous fury for all those who refuse to believe. This means blessings, seals, judgement procs, etc and should reflect this on turtle wow.

Instant
Requires Paladin

Hey everyone,

had a similar post but a few things changed, so I gotta ask again:

When I found out about turtle WoW and saw the changes for paladins, I immediately wondered, if SoR is now more DPS compared to SoC. Now I have to think of a few factors:

 1) I just begin with raiding. My gear is full blue, some SP ret gear, some crit plate items.

author: Aeternusdoleo
subject: Re: How to level with AoE grinding?
content_md:
There's no shame in learning from others as well.

I'm still a newbie in many ways when it comes to pallying, but playing a protection pally in PvE (it's slow, I'll grant you that), I'm usually doing:
 - Concentration aura. With the other spell interrupt reduction talents, your self heals will never be interrupted by damage.
 - Righteous Fury, just because.
 - Sanctuary blessing on.
 - Seal of wisdom. Target the group of mobs I want to attack and body pull them. Keep attacking one to regain mana.
 - Tap on Holy Shield. Enemies start damaging themselves on Holy Shield, Shield Spike and the retaliation from Sanctuary.
 - Line of Sight pull: Walk backwards to a convenient spot, behind some terrain to force ranged enemies to close and bunch everyone up.
 - Consecration. Then Holy Light or Flash of Light to start self healing.
 - Judgement on the Seal of Wisdom to increase mana regain. Re-judgement whenever an enemy dies as you target the next one.
 - Holy Shield again as soon as it's off cooldown.
 - Keep self-healing, Holy Shielding and whacking the enemies until they are all dead. If there's a stronger one in the group of you find you have abundant mana you can use Crusader Strike and Holy Strike for additional damage.

If you picked engineering, you can add a few cheap explosives for more damage. I like to chuck an iron grenade as an opener. The stun gives you some breathing room too. If you find yourself running out of mana frequently while doing this, switch to a faster attack speed weapon, even if it means sacrificing a bit of damage.
You'd be much better served though with a build like this by teaming up with a dedicated damage dealing class like a mage or hunter.

author: Getplucked
subject: (Quick guide) Fixing swing timers with Holy Strike
content_md:
As Paladin players likely know, most swing timer addons are broken with Holy Strike, in that when you use it, the addon does not think you swung your weapon and thus does not show a swing timer.

I found a way to fix this with GryllsSwingTimer, and it looks like similar things might work for other swing timer addons.

What you do is just open the main .lua file (GryllsSwingTimer.lua) and go down to line 214. You should see a function called CombatSpells, listing a few abilities that work on next weapon swing. You just have to add Holy Strike to this list, like this:

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/EJTYJK5.png)

And now the addon will properly show your swing timer when you use Holy Strike.

I'm fairly certain this works with SP_Swingtimer as well. Just haven't been able to test it because that addon is randomly refusing to work/load for me.

author: Getplucked
subject: Can Paladin just get a normal taunt like the other tanks?
content_md:
Druid is a "hybrid" class but still has a regular taunt spell, so I don't understand why Paladin is stuck with this weird janky setup that requires 3 talent points and also makes you use a GCD and judgement CD just to taunt.

Since using this taunt also deprives you of one of your two on-demand threat abilities, often times you taunt something and then the DPS immediately pulls threat on it again because your only threat after the taunt is an auto attack. Like imagine if taunting as a Warrior prevented you from using Sunder/Revenge for the next 8 seconds. That'd be dumb. But that's effectively what Paladin is stuck with.

It's a creative solution to giving Paladins a taunt in vanilla, but in practice it's just bad and clunky as hell. Can we just get a normal taunt spell like Warrior and Druid have?

content_md:
The problems is with this so called «taunt»:
 1.Taunt is tied to SoJ, that doesnt provide nothing viable for tanking, when it is on paladin.
 2.It is tied to seal/judgement mechanic, which is already requires usage of SoR and SoW to sustain threat and mana. This hurts the most, when you need to tank multiple targets. And now you get another seal, to use and as a result you get overwhelmed, your mana is drained.
 3.It removes SoW debuff on target, when discharged.
 4.It requires 3 points in talent tree and can be fully obtained only at 27 lvl when warrior and druid get theirs at 10 lvl, also warrior gets [Mocking Blow] at 16 lvl and [Challenging Shout] at 26 lvl which is mass taunt, druid gets [Challenging Roar] at 28 lvl without any talents required.
How to fix this mess:
 1.Solution is just give [Hand of Reckoning], that would be trained at 10 lvl, yes it would be superrior to warriors and druids taunts, but I consider it fair, because they have 3 and 2 taunts, when paladin will have only one.
 2.SoJ should reduce targets movement speed to normal, when discharged, like it was in TBC. As for its talent in prot tree, it can be turned in to 33/66/100% chance immobilizing enemy for 2 sec or something else. This also will fix problem with countering high mobility targets like shamans, druids and hunters.
 3.Another talent that devs should add is [Spiritual Attunement] - 2 point talent somewhere at row 6 of prot tree. That will provide paladin with 10% of mana from the amount healed hp. It will improve threat generation with spells, because prots mana drains very fast.

content_md:
> **Kairion wrote: Mon Jul 03, 2023 11:16 pm**
> or if a threatwipe has occured and the mob runs away from you towards your healer.

You just shot your entire argument against Paladins having a basic taunt in the foot, set it on fire, then raped its corpse by pointing out the major issue that makes taunt necessary to any class defined as being in the tank role.

Threat wipes exist. Because of the nature of the game and the way classes generate threat and Paladin's incredibly enemy-dependent (rather than player-dependent) threat-generating kit, the existence of threat wipes means that there will be situations where you lose aggro and it is 100% outside your control as a player.

I would agree that Paladins do not need a taunt if aggro was 100% within the control of the player or even the party. But it is not, and therefore, Paladin should either be given a taunt or have all of its tanking abilities removed from the game. This is not hyperbolic. It's very simple: Is Paladin a tank? If yes, they must have a taunt. If they cannot have a usable taunt, they cannot be a tank.

While Getplucked has not shown themselves to have the greatest of takes thus far, in this case, the dude is 100% correct. Hand of Reckoning is already in the game, in the spell DB (Improved Judgement of Justice actually invokes it and you can see the debuff on enemies). The only thing missing is to create a "teach to player" spell and give that to Paladin trainers.

And most importantly, paladin starts the fight with a full resource bar, warrior and druid with an empty one. Its all good saying warrior can follow up with a skill imediately after the taunt while paladin has to wait 8 seconds for his next judgement. But that ignores that warrior might be out of rage. And while its fun to poke paladin for being oom, if you let him drink, paladin starts every fight with a full resource bar, while warriors is empty.

If we give warriors, druids and paladins an equally working taunt to the others, then suddently paladin is the best tank for taunting. Since he has free spellhit in his talents, can follow up each taunt with HS into JoR, a combo that reliably deals 3-4k threat instantly and he will never have to budget his mana in the same way warriors or druids have to.

Kairon, rather than getting pissy (at someone who admittedly is very good at earning that reaction from people), consider that JotC has been acknowledged as flawed by the devs, it is likely going to be reverted, and Hand of Reckoning was recognized as necessary by old Blizz long before the bogeyman of "modern Blizzard devs".  Turtle doesn't have to operate entirely on doing everything differently than Blizzard eventually did just for its own sake. We cannot have a meaningful discussion about good game design so long as people fanatically cling to "Turtle must do things differently than Blizzard did" or "Blizz bad, Turt good".

Taunt without an opportunity cost was never good game design to begin with, but that's a discussion for another day.

But giving paladin a baseline taunt without drawbacks ignores a few things about the class that fundamentally distinguishes paladins from other classes with access to tank. If your taunt is baseline you get access to it on the only healer in the entire game who doesn't mind catching threat. Druids have to go into bearform to not die when taunting and warriors simply can not heal. A decent taunt especially in conjunction with on demand immunity from bubble is a major aspect for the non tanking specs of the class.

Paladins taunt is worse than the Druid / Warrior one in the sense that you have it often on CD from using judgement. But it still has its invaluable upsides. Getting knocked up & threatwiped? Paladin taunts increased range allows you to cast taunt while still in the air, preventing the mob from running off. A warrior in the same situation will have to wait till he is back to the ground, and then run after the mob. A great asset for instance in construct quarter trash. At the same time, for every instance where the game hard requires taunts (planned tank swaps for instance) it does its job to an adequate degree. The argument that paladin needs the same taunt as warrior comes from people who do simply not want to adjust to the different playstile of a different class.
And for anyone who argues taunt needs to be used retroactively for DPS ripping threat, no it doesn't. you bring a 30% threatreduction for DPS with blessing of salvation to any situation you are going to, as well as a pseudo taunt in blessing of protection and DPS ripping threat is ALWAYS their fault and not something a tank has to be able to correct.

Paladin taunt is more cumbersome than it has to be simply because it purges the useful judgement you had on your target before taunting. But otherwise it does what it's meant to do, facilitate tankswaps and solve threatwipes

Uh...paladin healers don't wear plate lmao
A majority of your BIS gear is leather/cloth until you get to T3 gear. And even then, the offpieces are usually competitive/better than T3.

And the other tanks have multiple taunts, whereas Paladin only has one.

We're objectively worse than the other classes for no good reason.

subject: Paladin 2.0 Nerfs and Reworks
content_md:
I thought its time for an updated List for a definitive fix all paladins related issues. i mean not just buffing paladins, this has significant nerfs too.

 1. bubble changed from -50% attacksped to -50% all dmg like in wotlk
This is a needed change to compenaste for paladins higher dmg output on twow

 2. Holy Strike and Seal Of Command double dip formula removed
SoC double dipping is blizzlike, the formula has always been
((70% weapon_dmg  ) + spellpower bonus dmg ) *1.15, but the weapon dmg itlsef is already incrase by 15%, therefor benefitting twice from dmg multipliers on attackpower.
But this has become an issue with the addition of holy strike. The weapon_dmg in the fomula needs to be adjusted to be without dmg multipliers. This will be a MASSIVE nerf to paladin burst in pvp, and full physical ret paladin dmg in pve and should not be done in a vacuum.

 3. Seal of Command procc dmg increased by 5% per rank
Currently higher SoC ranks only incraes the judgmenet dmg. Often times you can just use rank 1 to safe mana.
With this change rank 2 would be 75%, and max rank 5 would be 90%, making it benefitial to acutally go for the max rank as inteded. This buff offsets the double dip nerf not completly but buffers it. Paladin dmg would be more consisten but without extreme double dip burst

 4. Crusader strike rework to be less frustrating
 4.5 second CD added (no more degenrate and unfun cs spamming, fishing for wf proccs, which is a huge nerf in raids, no more cs spamm under bubble which is a huge nerf in pvp)
the 103 dmg it does turned to holy (more threat for protection pala)
added a small sp coefficient (dmg slightly increases with stacks from itself, it will still do only around 150 dmg and now with cd, overall a nerf)
libram and pvp bonus spellpower applied only once on the first stack and not 5x giving paladins hundres of sp from these items (unbalanced design making thse items ridicolous strong, but this will super nerf paladins in pve)
you will need more time to stack the 5 cs because of the cd. paladins working together to get 5 stacks fast will be much intersting gameplay. in pvp it wont be possible to stack to 5 quickly and mega burst.
Lastly I think the ability should be able to crit, everything can crit besides dots. This is a blatant break of vanilla wow conventions on what to expect how abilities work. It woild be OK after the CD is introduced.

 5. Judgmement of crusader restored
Just remove that forced proccing custom mechanics. noone rly likes it, everysone complaints about it, its a balacmne nightmare. its not worth the trouble.
while we could go and find some new effect, the easist and most straightforward is just a revert to its original form everyone is familair with.just make it stack with crusader strike again.
The only reason the mstacking was a problem before and had to be removed was because of the librams and pvp gloves bonus being applied 6 times in total then with 5x cs and 1x from judgement.
after that is nerfed to 1x from cs and 1x from judgemnt (see crusader strike nerf above) it would be totally fine to stack.
This will mean that paladins in raids can stay somewhat competetitive after the crusader strike nerf aslong as you got 2 paladins in raid, one for judgemtn of cursader one for jugment of wisdom.

 6. Holy Shield made use able while silenced
Change holy shield definiton form spell to ability, so that you can use it while being silenced just like holy strike already is and Warriors shield block is too. this will make tanking for paladins fairer. Note that warr sheild block is also of GCD while paladin holy shield requirres a GCD.

 7. Vindication is bugged and does not work currently in pve
This talent reduces the targets strenght and agiltty when procced. the problem is, on cmangos npcs do not have strength or agllity unlike in classic where they do have it. he reuslt is the talent only works in pvp in twow but its not even worth using there.
 --> Make it reduce the targets attackpower or attackspeed instead since npcs do have attackpower. this way it will be finally atleast working in pve, would be a workaround if you dont want to fix the acutalg bug of no agi and streght values on npcs
 -->An alternative suggestion could be that it reudces the targets chance to crit with meele by 1/2/3%, which would allow for intersting tank theorycrafting and help offset paladins inabillty to get crit immune in raids

And that is it. no absurd paladin buffs. a list of small tweaks that will make it more balanced and more fun, both for paladin haters and paladin enjoyers

Now come the more experimental reworks and buff after we fixed the pvp mess with the changes above:

 8. New Argent defender 31 prot talent, 12 second CD active ability: strike your target with your shield dealing X base dmg + 300% block value + 33% sp as holy dmg. triggers redoubt on use.
This allows to keep redoubt up more reliable and with holy shield you can become crush immune, jsut like warriors allways could reliably with their 75% shield block. It also gives paladins anotheer holy trheat ability with sheild to make up for losing vegance. currenly all prot palas are acutally ret talented isntead

 9. make reckoning 3 talents instead of 5, so 33%/66%/100%
This change is needed because twow nerfed reckoning. on classic in can store up to 5 charges and then you can mega burst. on twow you are capped to 1 extra hit. noone uses this talent. non in pvp not ib pve. it is worthless. make it ateaslt cost 2 talent points less to make up for it.you also cant get Seal of Command + Reckoning on twow which finished of this pvp specc compeltely.

 10. anticicaption talent made usefull, changed to reduced dmg by 1/2/3/4/5%
currently it gives 2/4/6/8/10 defesen with 5 points. its a total noob trap. it scales horribly into endgame too, noobody uses it in raids ever.
New effect is to make up for paladins not having defesnive stance which reduces dmg by 10% but also has the tradeoff of lowered dmg by 10%. now its an intersting option for raid tanks to take instead of the shield specc talent that gives mana on the same line.

 11. Improved seal of righeousness talent fixed
Currently it increase the BASE dmg by 3/6/9/12/15%. That's nothing, no ones uses it. Another noob trap because they don't know it does not incresec the total dmg as the tooltip suggests.
Change it to apply after bonus sp like you did for warlocks curse of agony talent and druids moonfire idol. but change it to 2/4/6/8/10% to keep balanced.

 12. Exocism add 1.5s castime, make it usable against all targets, with a 10% bonus cirt chance against undead and demon.
Everytime I step into stratholme I feel like, this is it. This is how paladins should be. With a range Pull and extra holy dmg threat.
Adding it just as it is as instant spell woild be broken thought in many cases. A cast time will ensure it not totally abusable in pvp and we have enough pvp nerfs above anyway. Bonus crit chance on demon and undead preserves it's original flavour.

Tackling pala dps is not that easy but doable. You need to lock at many things

author: Redmagejoe
subject: Re: Are paladins good to tank?
content_md: Tankadins are pretty crazy on this server, even while still having some shortcomings that will most likely be addressed in the next round of class changes. From level 20 on, they're solid dungeon tanks and can even 1v1 elites at level 38+ once they have Seal of Light / Seal of Wisdom. You will thoroughly enjoy your Tankadin leveling, just be prepared for working harder as a mana tank. There are some tricks to optimize your tanking rotation and behaviors to be mana-efficient, but it is not uncommon to drain on mana by the end of a dungeon pull if you aren't careful.

author: Rof
subject: Paladin prot and ret fixes
content_md:
i've been thinking about these changes for a hot minute now but i think the way to fix paladin is this

Removed Holy Strike as a baseline ability (this ability is just too strong for every paladin to get for free, its straight up as good as some classes 31 point talents meanwhile ret and prot 31 point talent is dogshit)

Repentance - Moved up one row

New Ret 31 point talent - Holy Strike (its as good as a 31 point talent so why not make it the 31 point talent, also fixes prots stupid wep gearing, and holy's burst in pvp)

Two-handed wep spec - now increases ALL damage by 2%/4%/6% and reduces threat generated by 5%/10%/15% (this is the threat reduction talent rets are missing compared to other classes, its weaker than those other threat reduction talents because rets are tankier than most classes and it does more than just threat reduction)

on to prot

Precision - Increases Physical hit by 1%/2%/3% and increases spell hit by 2%/4%/6% (this is to help increase the effectiveness of taunt and exo landing)

One-handed wep spec - Increases ALL damage by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10% and increases stamina by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10% (this helps solve the stam issue prots have and to atleast slightly off-set the loss of veng)

Ardent Defender - moved up one row - now 5 ranks - Reduces damage taken by 25% while below 30%/35%/40%/45%/50% health

New 31 point talent - Divine Exorcism - Removes the targeting requirement of Exorcism (this is to replace Holy strike as the main threat ability while also making prot more spell based versus rets wep based gameplay)

Exorcism should remain the way it is. The devs lean heavily on inspiration from WC3, which limits their baseline holy blasting potential to undead targets. In it's current form, exorcism accomplishes this pretty well.
What ret needs is a button they can press with a reasonable cooldown that does some damage. This isnt for the purpose of increasing their dps (although it would be nice for them to be somewhere other than bottom-mid) but to make the spec more fun to play.

A combination of the above would allow ret to be competitive for mid-range damage in most raids, then be competitive for higher spots in undead raids like Naxx. It fits thematically and rewards the player for making it all the way to the end game raid.

But due to the design of Holy Strike and Seal/Judgement of Command, ret is trapped in a corner with no way of adding a damage output ability that doesnt break pvp even moreso than it already is.

author: Aeternusdoleo
subject: Re: Need help with Protection Paladin leveling talent build
content_md:
One option you have leveling as a pally tank is to put points in Holy initially, and go for full Spiritual Focus. That allows you, in combination with the Concentration aura, to self-heal while tanking. You'll need a decent mana bar, and this strategy really starts to kick off when you get access to Seal of Wisdom, Sanctuary and Holy Shield. A shieldspike on your shield also helps. Your damage reflection will wittle down melee enemies like a slow, persistent AOE.

It is much slower in soloing, but in terms of early tanking it works well. Once you're at 5 Concentration, start the protection tree with Redoubt, Precision, 2 ranks of Toughness. Then Sanctuary (this will be your main blessing on yourself) Shield Specialization and Improved Righteous Fury (assuming you go tank stuff). Improved Seal of Justice is a must as soon as possible as it's the only Paladin taunt. Then Holy Shield. Reckoning, Onehanded Specialization. Finish Toughness and Anticipation. And 2 points in Unyielding Faith.

You'll probably want to respec once you go raiding (or whenever class changes hit) but this build will do well while leveling. With Concentration aura on your heals won't ever be interrupted (short of enemies with spell interrupt effects, watch out for those), and you can gain additional aggro on enemies by self-healing mid combat while your holy shield and sanctuary keep damaging the enemies. A fast weapon and Seal of Wisdom on whatever enemy needs to go down first then allows you to regen mana.
Soloing, this build has a slowish TTK in one versus one, but it can stand up to a lot of enemies and elites singlehandedly. Endurance over firepower. The only thing it struggles with is elemental ranged enemies that are scripted to run away (such as those wizzies in Strahnbad) because this build is melee and does not have much in the way of stun-and-hold. Pair with engineering to compensate for this is a good option.

author: Getplucked
subject: Paladin dungeon tanking guide
content_md:
**Note that this guide is specifically for leveling and 5mans, not raids.**

While leveling my first character here (Hunter), I ran into many Paladin tanks that seemed to have no idea what they were doing. Some of them not using a seal while attacking, others just mindlessly spamming consecrate and OOMing themselves, struggling to hold threat...it was a nightmare. I thought maybe the class just wasn't good, but then I tried it myself and found it surprisingly easy to tank, so I figured I'd put together a quick guide to help others be less bad at the game.

The biggest mistake I saw people making is that they were just spamming threat abilities and burning through mana. I see Warrior tanks do this too, just going ham and ragestarving themselves even when they already have more than enough threat. You don't need to go ham on threat in 5mans, especially if you've got Blessing of Salvation on the DPS. (which you should lol) Often times you can hold threat just fine with Seal of Righteousness + Holy Strike. I only ever used Consecrate with 3+ mobs.

 ----
 ----

 **TALENTS**

Pretty straightforward, honestly. We don't need to spec 11 points into Holy for Consecrate anymore, so the standard build is 21 points into Prot for Holy Shield and then put the rest into Ret to eventually get Vengeance. The +15% physical/holy is just a thicc threat boost. Plus, since you're 30 points into Ret, you can throw on a 2h and be a decent DPS if needed.

Level 20: <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin/0-5IC1>

Level 40: <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin/0-5IDL0J-5CI>

Level 60: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin/ ... J-5EUVCC6U](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin/0-5IDL0J-5EUVCC6U)

 ----
 ----

 **GEAR**

There's really not much spell damage gear while leveling, so just grab any Str/Stam gear you can find. Int is fine too. As for weapons, a slower 1h is good for larger Holy Strike damage, but it doesn't matter all that much. Just get whatever 1h has the highest dps number on it, and whatever shield has the most armor/block value.

 ----
 ----

 **THE PULL**

BEFORE YOU PULL:
 -Is your healer in range?
 -Does your healer have a decent amount of mana?
 -Do paladin buffs have at least 1 minute remaining?

If you answered "no" to any of these, don't fucking pull you dingus. So many tanks just ignore healer mana and run off to pull more shit when I'm at 20% and drinking. It's obnoxious.

Anyway, here's how most pulls should go:

 -Mark a skull
 -Holy Shield while running in
 -target skull and press Holy Strike so you hit it as soon as you're in range
 -If there's more than 2 mobs, Consecrate, if not, then don't
 -Judgement of Righteousness + Seal of Righteousness autoattack on 2nd mob
 -Swap back and forth between autoattacking the two mobs, focusing more on skull

And from there you really just keep Holy Shield on cooldown and use holy strike / judgement as necessary.

This would hold threat perfectly fine 99% of the time in my experiences. I really only used Consecrate when there were more than 2 mobs, or if something suddenly pulled and I wanted that extra threat just to make complete sure that everything would be on me. This idea that you need to use Consecrate all the time is just wrong; you can hold threat just fine without it.

When it comes to Paladin tanking in 5mans, the goal is to use as little mana as possible while still holding threat. Nobody likes having to wait for the paladin tank to sit and drink every single pull. Just like how Warriors can save rage in between pulls, you should be trying to save as much mana as you can to minimize drinking time.

Thankfully, mana management is much easier on Turtle WoW, since we now have a talent that gives us 2% mana back on every single block, and with Holy Shield + Redoubt, your block chance is pretty fuckin' high. It gets even easier when you get Seal of Wisdom and at least 1 piece of "adds X damage to your attacks" gear. At that point you have effectively infinite mana and almost never need to drink. The less you need to drink, the faster the dungeon will go.

With Judgement of Wisdom and 1-2 pieces of "adds X damage to your melee attacks" gear, you can start racking up huge amounts of mana, allowing you to use Consecrate more often without worrying about draining your mana. At this point, you can start opening pulls by judging Wisdom on skull alongside Holy Strike, and then dropping a Consecrate. I had 0 threat issues during all of my tanking from 40-60 doing this. Even managed to hold threat off of DPS that were 5-6 levels higher than me. It was pretty nice.

The earliest "adds X damage to your melee" item you can get is this one:
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80704>
Technically you can get a pair of gloves at 24, but they're super expensive (only drops off a rare spawn) and you don't even get Seal of Wisdom until 38 anyways, and at 38 you can easily solo RFC for the chest piece. Just corpse-run your way into Orgrimmar and you can walk past 99% of the trash in RFC to get to the boss you need, Bazzalan, at the very back of the instance. He only drops 3 different items so it shouldn't take too many runs to get this.

The next one you can get isn't until 51, though it's a drop from Hateforge Quarry, so you'll wanna be at least 54 or 55 before heading in there.
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60568>

You can also pick up Fiery Plate Gauntlets at 54, cheap crafted item you can just get off the AH.
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12631>

These will all stack with each other. Wearing all three of them will effectively get you EIGHT chances to proc Judgement of Wisdom on every single melee swing. It's utterly broken. You don't need all three though, you can get more than enough mana regen just wearing two of them. Since chest armor tends to give the most stats, I swapped to a normal "Of the Bear" chestpiece and used the gauntlets/boots.

In closing, the biggest tips for Paladin 5man tanking are:

 -Don't spam abilities, only put out as much threat as you need
 -Consecrate is not needed unless you're tanking 3+ mobs, or if you have plenty of mana from Judgement of Wisdom
 -Always put salv on the DPS (unless they're low threat or a hunter who knows how to feign)
 -Download a threat meter so you can see how much threat you have and know if you need to pump more
 -Best buff for yourself is Kings, if you don't have it, use Wisdom or Sanctuary depending on mana needs
 -If a mob is close to dying, you can just let DPS kill it, as it will likely be dead by the time they pull threat.
 -In general, there's no point in pumping more threat on a mob if it's going to die before the DPS will pull threat

GEAR

There's really not much spell damage gear while leveling, so just grab any Str/Stam gear you can find. Int is fine too. As for weapons, a slower 1h is good for larger Holy Strike damage, but it doesn't matter all that much. Just get whatever 1h has the highest dps number on it, and whatever shield has the most armor/block value.


----
----

THE PULL

BEFORE YOU PULL:
-Is your healer in range?
-Does your healer have a decent amount of mana?
-Do paladin buffs have at least 1 minute remaining?

If you answered "no" to any of these, don't fucking pull you dingus. So many tanks just ignore healer mana and run off to pull more shit when I'm at 20% and drinking. It's obnoxious.


Anyway, here's how most pulls should go:

-Mark a skull
-Holy Shield while running in
-target skull and press Holy Strike so you hit it as soon as you're in range
-If there's more than 2 mobs, Consecrate, if not, then don't
-Judgement of Righteousness + Seal of Righteousness autoattack on 2nd mob
-Swap back and forth between autoattacking the two mobs, focusing more on skull

And from there you really just keep Holy Shield on cooldown and use holy strike / judgement as necessary.

This would hold threat perfectly fine 99% of the time in my experiences. I really only used Consecrate when there were more than 2 mobs, or if something suddenly pulled and I wanted that extra threat just to make complete sure that everything would be on me. This idea that you need to use Consecrate all the time is just wrong; you can hold threat just fine without it.

When it comes to Paladin tanking in 5mans, the goal is to use as little mana as possible while still holding threat. Nobody likes having to wait for the paladin tank to sit and drink every single pull. Just like how Warriors can save rage in between pulls, you should be trying to save as much mana as you can to minimize drinking time.

Thankfully, mana management is much easier on Turtle WoW, since we now have a talent that gives us 2% mana back on every single block, and with Holy Shield + Redoubt, your block chance is pretty fuckin' high. It gets even easier when you get Seal of Wisdom and at least 1 piece of "adds X damage to your attacks" gear. At that point you have effectively infinite mana and almost never need to drink. The less you need to drink, the faster the dungeon will go.

With Judgement of Wisdom and 1-2 pieces of "adds X damage to your melee attacks" gear, you can start racking up huge amounts of mana, allowing you to use Consecrate more often without worrying about draining your mana. At this point, you can start opening pulls by judging Wisdom on skull alongside Holy Strike, and then dropping a Consecrate. I had 0 threat issues during all of my tanking from 40-60 doing this. Even managed to hold threat off of DPS that were 5-6 levels higher than me. It was pretty nice.


The earliest "adds X damage to your melee" item you can get is this one:
https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80704
Technically you can get a pair of gloves at 24, but they're super expensive (only drops off a rare spawn) and you don't even get Seal of Wisdom until 38 anyways, and at 38 you can easily solo RFC for the chest piece. Just corpse-run your way into Orgrimmar and you can walk past 99% of the trash in RFC to get to the boss you need, Bazzalan, at the very back of the instance. He only drops 3 different items so it shouldn't take too many runs to get this.

The next one you can get isn't until 51, though it's a drop from Hateforge Quarry, so you'll wanna be at least 54 or 55 before heading in there.
https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60568

You can also pick up Fiery Plate Gauntlets at 54, cheap crafted item you can just get off the AH.
https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12631

These will all stack with each other. Wearing all three of them will effectively get you EIGHT chances to proc Judgement of Wisdom on every single melee swing. It's utterly broken. You don't need all three though, you can get more than enough mana regen just wearing two of them. Since chest armor tends to give the most stats, I swapped to a normal "Of the Bear" chestpiece and used the gauntlets/boots.




In closing, the biggest tips for Paladin 5man tanking are:

-Don't spam abilities, only put out as much threat as you need
-Consecrate is not needed unless you're tanking 3+ mobs, or if you have plenty of mana from Judgement of Wisdom
-Always put salv on the DPS (unless they're low threat or a hunter who knows how to feign)
-Download a threat meter so you can see how much threat you have and know if you need to pump more
-Best buff for yourself is Kings, if you don't have it, use Wisdom or Sanctuary depending on mana needs
-If a mob is close to dying, you can just let DPS kill it, as it will likely be dead by the time they pull threat.
-In general, there's no point in pumping more threat on a mob if it's going to die before the DPS will pull threat
