author: Liljon
subject: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
Topics of the post:
 1. How Paladin changed from Vanilla to TWoW
 2. Obscured information
 3. Retribution is unplayable
 4. When tanking, threat is the name of the game
 5. Holy is as awesome as ever
 6. Change without sacrifice
 7. Conclusion

The goal of this feedback post is to do a detailed breakdown of where I see Paladin currently within the sandbox of TWoW, - primarily Retribution as that is what I played the most here - do a detailed breakdown of the mechanics that make and break it, and share my suggestion as to where it could be improved without sacrificing it's intended design. I will attempt to the best of my ability to present objective reality and accurate information and draw an unbiased conclusion, however, I will make readers aware when I am delving into the subjective territory of my feedback to avoid confusion. With all that being said, I don't expect the entirety of the post to be read (or at all), as it is a massive behemoth and I don't include a tl;dr simply because there is so much to talk about and I do not wish information to be compressed to the point of it possibly losing it's value (however, I have tried my best to be conscise).

To give some context about myself: I've been playing WoW non-stop since 2008 in it's many forms, and have always mained Paladin. I've always played every spec and sub-spec, have always done my best to push it to the limit and I primarily come from a background of endgame raiding and PvP (although I don't do very much PvP on Vanilla and TWoW by proxy, as I find that it aged poorly). Here on TWoW, I've been playing non stop for the last 4 months on this character at level60 (given I leveled my current toon last Autumn), primarily playing Retribution and its three variations (Spelladin, Hybrid and Full AP), although currently I am playing Hybrid. I've also put a fair amount of time into Holy and Protection. Currently, I'm raiding BWL with my guild, and I'm close to finishing up my BiS pre AQ40 - only needing UTB, Scroll and the cloak from the Silithus Abyssal Council bosses. I've also gone out of my way to pick up my D1 set.

My feedback here is purely based on endgame raiding, with only occassionally reaching into leveling and PvP content. I will skip a larger introduction to Paladin, as most of us are already well aware of the role of the class, and instead will jump into the nitty-gritty of TWoW. I will also be using a lot of abbreviations as the post goes on to make writing this easier.

 **1. How Paladin changed from Vanilla to TWoW**

Fundamentally speaking, Paladin remains mostly the same, but it has seen significant combat improvements. First of all, it is important to note for TWoW that Paladins and Shamans can play together, which means both sides get access to some new buffs, primarily Windfury. World Buffs have also been banned from raids, and there are a bunch of itemization changes and new items to be seen.

The core combat gameplay still heavily relies on auto attacks, which Holy Strike doubles down on, but we also see the issues with itemization being made up for with Crusader Strike adding significant amounts of spell power as a debuff to the enemy. Now, while on the TWoW Class pages, it is claimed that CS can't proc damage based procs, however, they absolutely can at the moment. Whether or not this is a bug, this makes the base Paladin combat rotation much more involved, as we have access to Windfury Totem, and a core mechanic of a Windfury proc is that it resets the swing timer, creating a spicier rotation where you want to time your CS-es and Judgments just after you swing with your weapon.

 **And as a small sidenote, I would argue that this should not be fixed as it makes the base gameplay much more involved.** However, you also have to account for the lack of information that the Windfury spells provide, as it doesn't state anywhere that it resets your swing timer, which it really should. While spamming CS in hopes of getting WF procs is still a DPS gain, it is a larger DPS gain to time a CS right after an auto attack, as if your swing timer isn't ready when you proc WF, you don't actually do an auto, you just do your WF hits.

Some SP coefficient buffs mean that sustain damage has been slightly increased (Consecration, Seal of Righteousness), and SP geared Rets become a significant threat boon with Retribution Aura for some Tanks.

Seal of the Crusader has been changed up more than half a year ago. The base Seal is still not strong enough to be our main seal (mostly because SoR's damage proc is just stupid strong mechanically), but the Judgment effect received a confusing at best rework, making the new Judge effect have a 30 times higher chance to proc weapon effects and enchants. This Judgment effect in fact has proven to be so disrupting and broken that certain weapons have received special conditions to either not or barely benefit from the new Judgment. Which makes me ask, what is the point of this Judgment effect? Information regarding this spell is highly obscured, one could easily think "Oh I'll just go and craft a Dark Iron Pulverizer and dunk on people in WSG" then it turns out that this weapon has received a specific nerf because of the JotC. Myself, I personally have ran 86 runs of UBRS in hopes of getting the Blackblade of Shahram, which, if my maths line up, would be about an infinitely stronger weapon than Might of Menethil with this new Judgment as it lets you swim in +50 stacking stat buffs and 30% haste procs. And I don't even know if it would work or not, because no one knows if it works with JotC.

New items with on hit damage effects added to TWoW on top of the fact that SoR double procs those effects and Windfury existing has made Judgment of Wisdom generate infinite mana, completely eliminating mana issues for both Prot and Ret. Even Holy Paladins on a lot of bossfights could go in and swing their weapons if they are willing to sacrifice some healing to engage in a riskier playstyle that gives them infinite mana without having to specifically build for spellcrit. **Personally speaking, the combination of having access to near infinite mana and Windfury is what makes Paladin combat truly enjoyable on TWoW, however, it also presents some problems that I will delve into a bit later.**

Perhaps most significantly, and something that can easily slip by people's attention, Holy Shock, aside from benefitting from a healing and damage buff (on top of Healing Light being extended to both portion of Holy Shock) has had it's cooldown lowered from 30 seconds to 20 seconds. This makes deep Holy Spelladin builds much more appealing, and offers some meaningful gameplay variety, especially going into Naxx where you can get extra benefit on the 5% spellcrit of Holy Power.

Precision having been extended to also cover Spellhit% has also made it so that Paladins are no longer at the risk of innate holy resistance removing all of their damage on some of their spellcasts, and perhaps by accident has also helped to create the strongest taunt in the game. With Improved Seal of Justice, the Judgment effect now acts as a Taunt on top of it's base mechanic, and because of Precision 3/3, and given that most Tank builds are hitcapped, this taunt is impossible to miss or resist (note that Judgment isn't subject to parry or dodge). This power comes at a cost though - many people argue that the taunt competing for Judgment is bad design, but I actually don't think so. You should always let some other Tank generate better threat, which you can then make up for with this absolutely overpowered Taunt. And if there is no threat, either on pull or a threat wipe, you JoR anyways to establish threat, which, remember, is also a spell that always lands. What I think conflicts with SoJ however is the fact that Crusader Strike exists, which can GCD lock a Tankadin, causing a delay in taunting that other classes don't have. Warrior and Bear taunts are OGCD (excluding Mocking Blow, but the strenght of this spell is that Warriors have 2 taunts), and so is Judgment, but SoJ is not, which can delay your taunts especially if someone suddenly critted a Shadow Bolt and ripped threat. The other small annoying side of it is that if you judged Wisdom beforehand, Justice will remove the Wisdom effect, making Pally tanking without a Ret in tow (especially one who has the CS libram and PvP gloves) a bit awful.

To go off of that, a recent fix has also made it so that rage/energy/mana procs generate threat, apparently as intended. This opens up a lot of threat generation for Prot Paladin - currently working on a Hand of Edward set with 2/3 incendosaur, and I am already generating miles more threat than my guild's Paladin tank. Having to judge Justice as the sole melee Paladin can be quite damaging to sustained threat generation, assuming you are supposed to keep threat for a long period of time after taunting.

While there have also been other various talent reworks, the main takeaways are that SoC can no longer be used together with Holy Shock in PvP (a good change), Prot had Redoubt and Shield Spec significantly improved, and you don't have to go down till the last row to get Holy Shield, another giant buff as this allows for more threat focused talent builds. Ardent Defender unfortunately is more of a leveling / AoE farming talent than a raiding talent, as it's rare to benefit from the mitigation component when you are more than liable to be oneshot when you are below 35% MT-ing a boss. However, keeping in mind the much better itemization on TWoW, Prot is finally a good tanking option in raids, which is always a good thing.

In fact, all three roles of Paladin are good, however, Prot and Ret don't come without their quirks. While I have delved a little bit into it, I'd like to dedicate a new section to some of the design issues I've encountered.

 **2. Obscured information**

There are a lot of different mechanics in this game that are simply never communicated to players, even from level1 onwards - and I am going to list them all.

The game doesn't tell you what your main stats translate to. STR, AGI, STAM, INT and SPI are never precisely communicated to the player based on the class you play.

The game never explains the hit table, melee and spellhit, weaponskills, parry hasting and the importance of standing behind a mob when hitting it.

The game never explains the swing timer, spell pushback and what causes the swing timer to reset.

 **The game never explains threat generation, nor is there a natural way to track it.**

Edit: The game never explains how Rage generation is calculated, the energy tickrate and mana regen mechanics.

The game never explains that Seal of Righteousness can trigger all damage based procs.

The game never explains that you can use on-hit items to generate extra procs of Judgment of Wisdom. In fact, it also doesn't explain why Judgment of Wisdom isn't PPM based but Judgment of Light is, and also why on-hit items only really work with JoW but not JoL.

The game never explains Windfury's mechanics.

The game never explains which spells of Paladin are based on spellhit, and which are based on weapon skills and melee hit. In fact, as a sidenote, since the last patch on 07/18, HoW seems to have shifted to spellhit% table, causing roughly 75% of all HoWs to miss. On that tangent, it is also never explained which spells benefit from spellcrit% and which benefit from meleecrit%.

The game never explains the buff and debuff cap.

The game never explains which buffs and consumables stack with each other, and which don't.

The game never explains which weapon procs work with JotC and which don't.

The game never explains which weapon procs scale with spell power, and which don't.

Sometimes, the game even lies to you, telling you that items like Ragehammer and Sword of Zeal raise your raw damage dealt by some amount, only for it to not actually increase anything (because it actually raises attack power by 20/10, barely a DPS gain).

The issue is that knowing all these small details is what is going to truly improve a person's gameplay. A lot of this is the fault of Blizzard of course, as they are the ones that made the game, but I would argue that TWoW should have made an effort to improve on explaining the base mechanics of the game. In Cataclysm, they actually had a really good solution for the unintentional lack of information - they developed a new option that allowed you to have simplified or advanced tooltips. Basically, your Crusader Strike would either say "Strike with your weapon and generate a Holy Power." or "Deal 135% physical weapon damage (with the tooltip updating based on your talents and such) to your opponent and generate Holy Power if the attack is successful". It is also important to note here that on your character sheet on Cataclysm, it was easy to tell that you only needed 5% hit to always connect against a level 85 target. I would suggest that this should be worked on over time - there are Warriors that don't even know that if they use Heroic Strike or Cleave while dual wielding, their main hand weapon only needs 9% hit and not 24%, which is what makes those spells so strong, not their raw damage dealt.

 **3. Retribution is unplayable**

Unfortunately, pushing Ret to it's limits also comes with a massive downside. Once you figure out a build that works for you, get your on hit items, windfury, consumes, all the buffs and such, you are going to see something horrifying. This issue has been present for a long time, which was then skyrocketed by the new change on 07/11 that caused mana procs to generate threat. **Ret Paladin is threat capped.**

From a first glance, the core suspicion would be around Windfury procs with a strong 2 hander. And yes, it does generate significant threat and damage, however, it doesn't account for what pushes Ret over the top.

First, Judgment of Wisdom. As it procs a lot due to SoR and on hits, especially as Spelladin with faster weapons (and also having access to the on-hit offhand Lantern from Survival), sustained threat generation has skyrocketed significantly, when you can generate anywhere between 300 to 2.5k mana per auto attack. While this significantly helps Prot Paladins in threat gen, it also significantly hurts Ret Paladin.

Second, and while I can't confirm this as extracting information from Vanilla is borderline impossible, but I've always had a massive suspicion - I'm convinced that Holy Strike is generating threat twice. It just simply generates absurd amounts of threat, even when it doesn't crit. What I'm guessing is happening is that the game thinks you swung twice - once for Holy Strike, and once as just a normal auto attack. Or maybe Holy Strike isn't subject to Blessing of Salvation and other threat reduction effects. I don't know because I can't tell because the Vanilla client is terrible.

The point is, Ret both generates too much sustain threat and has insane threat spikes. It has to be one or the other, it can't be both. If you generate too much sustain threat, you can adjust your build to generate less mana and focus more on regenning mana through consumes, Innervates, Shadow Priests or Arcane Mages. If threat is too spiky, you can adjust your rotation so that you don't CS after every auto, but instead use Consecration or help with cleansing and such, or just hold back a little bit. **I would argue what makes Ret extremely fun in raids is both the absurd mana economy and Windfury, and I'd like to see that element retained in some way.** I could get rid of all my on hits and massively reduce my mana economy, but it just feels shallow.

However, at the moment, I can rip threat off of Naxx geared Bears, if I get (un)lucky enough. Testing post JoW change, I generated 16k threat in 2 swings on the lvl63 target dummy. And while that was an insane RNG chain, it kind of proves the point. Perhaps a better example would be raiding MC with my guild post-change, and while on Golemagg, I suddenly spiked 7k threat, overtaking our otherwise good Fury Prot. After bubbling to drop threat while Golemagg was 50% hp, and AFKing for 15 more seconds afterwards, I started attacking again. By the time the boss was 6% HP, I overtook threat again. **This shouldn't happen, ever.** Oh, and I wasn't flasked for this attempt, in fact, I didn't even use any consumable other than 2 GFPP-s.

 **4. When tanking, threat is the name of the game**

First of all, Prot has been massively improved in the areas it needed improving. Mitigation is much better with Redoubt and Shield Spec, mana economy is much better due to Shield Spec and JoW on hits, spike threat gen is significantly better with unmissable Judgments and Holy Strike, and sustain threat gen has been greatly improved with CS-es spellpower debuff and how frequently you can block now due to Redoubt - and of course, since the mana proc change, this aspect improved again. And of course, we have a Taunt. While not specifically tied to the class, Tea with Sugar is a fantastic consumable that especially Prots gain a massive benefit from. However, there are a couple things that stand out to me as large issues.

Despite making up a significant portion of your threat, Holy Strike is subject to insane variance with dodging and parrying. It is extremely punishing on pulls to have your HS parried, because establishing long term threat depends quite a bit on Holy Strike. While the mana proc change helped to mitigate this, and the fact that you can also tank with Hand of Edward giving you free Holy Light procs to generate threat with (which also scales with Righteous Fury, because remember, it's a Holy spell), Prot builds that put a larger emphasis on mitigation, which inevitably will happen on some bossfights will lack behind on threat much more so than they should.

It is also worth to note just what differentiates a mitigation vs threat build when it comes to Prot, because for the most part, it's mostly based on your itemization. The thing is, talenting anything below Holy Shield in Prot is a bit of a meme. One-Handed Weapon Spec is still 5 points for barely any gain, Reckoning is a PvP talent and Ardent Defender is terribly useless when main tanking due to the mitigation effect being worthless when you're that low HP - which basically means that for the most part, you can only really differentiate mitigation builds from threat ones is if the Paladin in question talented 5/5 in Toughness and Anticipation, because after you got Holy Shield, most Paladins just simply go down Ret to pick up threat and efficiency tools, or Holy if they have a Hand of Edward. Ultimately it will come down to itemization moreso than anything, which isn't a bad thing in itself, but it does mean mitigation builds don't really have a greater identity.

 **5. Holy is as awesome as ever**

Honestly, not much to say here. I really have no feedback on Holy other than it just simply continuing to be an amazing and fun healer. Perhaps the only thing that might be worth looking into is that due to the lack of World Buffs, early Holy Light builds are not as viable due to lacking ~20 spellcrit - 3% from Savvy, 10% from Dragonslayer, 5% from Songflower, and the remaining 1-2% from main stat buffs that scale your intellect. I've been finding myself needing on more DPS gear than usual because it has spellcrit%.

So, with all that being said, how would I go about making Prot and Ret better? First of all, it is important to establish a couple things.
 1. Changes have to adhere to the core gameplay and style of Paladin.
 2. Changes that take away have to replace with something that is at the very least equivalent to what was before, but preferably better.
 3. Changes have to create interesting and nuanced gameplay.
 4. Changes have to be efficient when it comes to managing game development resources.
 5. Changes have to be easy to pick up and understand.
 6. Changes have to have long term value.
 7. Changes have to maintain balance across the wider game.

The very first change I'd make is to revert the change on mana/energy/rage procs generating threat. This just creates excess unwanted threat for DPS without Tanks being able to keep up, and looking into Holy Strike's threat calculation to make sure that it is actually generating 100% and not 200% threat (again, I might be on copium for this one, but I long suspected this to be a possible issue).

Now, we get to how Prots can generate better threat despite Holy Strike's variance, and I think that Seal of the Crusader is the perfect tool for this. Change the Haste to be replaced with making your auto attacks (and possibly Crusader Strikes, if SoR would continue generating more overall threat) deal 100% holy damage. This would play into Righteous Fury significantly, but would also create some degree of choice when it comes to JoW, as SoR of course can proc JoW and also double procs on hit items. You can either choose to dish out max rank spells with a Hand of Edward to do Holy Lights with SoR, or you can choose to play it safe and be able to build mitigation without losing significant chunks of threat. Deep Prot could also see some improvements - One Handed Weapon Spec should be a 2-3 pointer talent at most and give the same benefit, but also extend it to Crusader Strike damage. Excess talent points can then be funneled to Toughness and Anticipation to create a true mitigation build.

Ardent Defender can go in some directions.
 1: Extend it to Wrath's variation that gives a small cheat death effect, which would make the passive much more viable when main tanking raids - although I would argue that cheat deaths are extremely lame.
 2: Make it so that that damage that reduces you below the HP treshold is also mitigated. For example, if you are sitting at 50% hp, and you get hit by something that takes 50% of your hp, Ardent Defender would activate, causing that effect to only take 37.5% of your hp.
 3: Make it so that Ardent Defender instead of reducing damage taken below a set HP value would instead allow for spell damage to be blocked, which would make up for the lack of health compared against Warriors and Bears.

Either way, a solution has to be found to create a true mitigation build. Choice matters a lot when it comes to RPGs, and this option is sorely lacking.

I haven't adressed Judgment of the Crusader yet. A spell that causes players to always second guess themselves is not good design (especially with a lack of a PTR, disallowing Paladins to test certain weapons beforehand). And here I am at a bit of a loss. We can't move Imp. SoJ's effect to just be the base effect of JotC, because having to talent into a taunt is what defines a Paladin Tank. You can't have JotC be some sort of a damage Judgment, because then there is nothing to differentiate it from JoR. You also can't have it tied to resource restoration, as JoL and JoW already do that. So, perhaps, some form of mitigation, or a personal buff would be the way to go to distinguish it from the rest. Maybe increasing block chance by 10%? Here I am totally unsure what the solution is, but a solution has to be found. Because if not, we will continue to wander around blind as to which proc weapon is the best and why it's Blackblade of Shahram for both Prot and Ret, because who needs a shield when your Stamina and Agility keeps going higher and higher and your threat skyrockets with the insane haste and Strength values. Flame Wrath AoE farming will become a victim, but it has to be done to make the game better.

Beyond that, I would love to see one change made for Sanctity Aura. At the moment, it is a completely selfish Aura - it is beyond rare to have another Paladin or Smite Priest benefit from it. Every other aura, the group can benefit from. I've always wanted to see Sanctiy Aura increase (R)AP and SP by some value, as not only does Ret benefit from both, but it would be an actual *aura*. Sanctified Command's mana restoring portion is also kinda useless given how little it restores. With SoC being a primarily PvP seal, I'd argue that the resistance to purge effect should be extended to all Seals and Blessings (with Blessing of Freedom and Protection being a likely exception).

Oh, and, do everything I listed in point 2.

 **7. Conclusion**

The reason why I've written such extensive feedback and criticism is because I - despite everything I just went over, and how much I shit over some design decisions and the palpable lack of QA testing at times - love WoW and like playing on TWoW, and I'd like to see this project do better. Discussions around Paladin are wide and varied, however I found that a lot of topics weren't really touched on by a lot of those who do engage in discussions, and so I wished to bring forward what I had on my mind, because the current state of Ret has almost made me quit the game.

I hope that this post was a comprehensible and enjoyable read. Thank you for taking the time to get this far.
content_html:
Topics of the post:
1. How Paladin changed from Vanilla to TWoW
2. Obscured information
3. Retribution is unplayable
4. When tanking, threat is the name of the game
5. Holy is as awesome as ever
6. Change without sacrifice
7. Conclusion

The goal of this feedback post is to do a detailed breakdown of where I see Paladin currently within the sandbox of TWoW, - primarily Retribution as that is what I played the most here - do a detailed breakdown of the mechanics that make and break it, and share my suggestion as to where it could be improved without sacrificing it's intended design. I will attempt to the best of my ability to present objective reality and accurate information and draw an unbiased conclusion, however, I will make readers aware when I am delving into the subjective territory of my feedback to avoid confusion. With all that being said, I don't expect the entirety of the post to be read (or at all), as it is a massive behemoth and I don't include a tl;dr simply because there is so much to talk about and I do not wish information to be compressed to the point of it possibly losing it's value (however, I have tried my best to be conscise).

To give some context about myself: I've been playing WoW non-stop since 2008 in it's many forms, and have always mained Paladin. I've always played every spec and sub-spec, have always done my best to push it to the limit and I primarily come from a background of endgame raiding and PvP (although I don't do very much PvP on Vanilla and TWoW by proxy, as I find that it aged poorly). Here on TWoW, I've been playing non stop for the last 4 months on this character at level60 (given I leveled my current toon last Autumn), primarily playing Retribution and its three variations (Spelladin, Hybrid and Full AP), although currently I am playing Hybrid. I've also put a fair amount of time into Holy and Protection. Currently, I'm raiding BWL with my guild, and I'm close to finishing up my BiS pre AQ40 - only needing UTB, Scroll and the cloak from the Silithus Abyssal Council bosses. I've also gone out of my way to pick up my D1 set.

My feedback here is purely based on endgame raiding, with only occassionally reaching into leveling and PvP content. I will skip a larger introduction to Paladin, as most of us are already well aware of the role of the class, and instead will jump into the nitty-gritty of TWoW. I will also be using a lot of abbreviations as the post goes on to make writing this easier.

1. How Paladin changed from Vanilla to TWoW

Fundamentally speaking, Paladin remains mostly the same, but it has seen significant combat improvements. First of all, it is important to note for TWoW that Paladins and Shamans can play together, which means both sides get access to some new buffs, primarily Windfury. World Buffs have also been banned from raids, and there are a bunch of itemization changes and new items to be seen.

The core combat gameplay still heavily relies on auto attacks, which Holy Strike doubles down on, but we also see the issues with itemization being made up for with Crusader Strike adding significant amounts of spell power as a debuff to the enemy. Now, while on the TWoW Class pages, it is claimed that CS can't proc damage based procs, however, they absolutely can at the moment. Whether or not this is a bug, this makes the base Paladin combat rotation much more involved, as we have access to Windfury Totem, and a core mechanic of a Windfury proc is that it resets the swing timer, creating a spicier rotation where you want to time your CS-es and Judgments just after you swing with your weapon.

And as a small sidenote, I would argue that this should not be fixed as it makes the base gameplay much more involved. However, you also have to account for the lack of information that the Windfury spells provide, as it doesn't state anywhere that it resets your swing timer, which it really should. While spamming CS in hopes of getting WF procs is still a DPS gain, it is a larger DPS gain to time a CS right after an auto attack, as if your swing timer isn't ready when you proc WF, you don't actually do an auto, you just do your WF hits.

Some SP coefficient buffs mean that sustain damage has been slightly increased (Consecration, Seal of Righteousness), and SP geared Rets become a significant threat boon with Retribution Aura for some Tanks.

Seal of the Crusader has been changed up more than half a year ago. The base Seal is still not strong enough to be our main seal (mostly because SoR's damage proc is just stupid strong mechanically), but the Judgment effect received a confusing at best rework, making the new Judge effect have a 30 times higher chance to proc weapon effects and enchants. This Judgment effect in fact has proven to be so disrupting and broken that certain weapons have received special conditions to either not or barely benefit from the new Judgment. Which makes me ask, what is the point of this Judgment effect? Information regarding this spell is highly obscured, one could easily think "Oh I'll just go and craft a Dark Iron Pulverizer and dunk on people in WSG" then it turns out that this weapon has received a specific nerf because of the JotC. Myself, I personally have ran 86 runs of UBRS in hopes of getting the Blackblade of Shahram, which, if my maths line up, would be about an infinitely stronger weapon than Might of Menethil with this new Judgment as it lets you swim in +50 stacking stat buffs and 30% haste procs. And I don't even know if it would work or not, because no one knows if it works with JotC.

New items with on hit damage effects added to TWoW on top of the fact that SoR double procs those effects and Windfury existing has made Judgment of Wisdom generate infinite mana, completely eliminating mana issues for both Prot and Ret. Even Holy Paladins on a lot of bossfights could go in and swing their weapons if they are willing to sacrifice some healing to engage in a riskier playstyle that gives them infinite mana without having to specifically build for spellcrit. Personally speaking, the combination of having access to near infinite mana and Windfury is what makes Paladin combat truly enjoyable on TWoW, however, it also presents some problems that I will delve into a bit later.

Perhaps most significantly, and something that can easily slip by people's attention, Holy Shock, aside from benefitting from a healing and damage buff (on top of Healing Light being extended to both portion of Holy Shock) has had it's cooldown lowered from 30 seconds to 20 seconds. This makes deep Holy Spelladin builds much more appealing, and offers some meaningful gameplay variety, especially going into Naxx where you can get extra benefit on the 5% spellcrit of Holy Power.

Precision having been extended to also cover Spellhit% has also made it so that Paladins are no longer at the risk of innate holy resistance removing all of their damage on some of their spellcasts, and perhaps by accident has also helped to create the strongest taunt in the game. With Improved Seal of Justice, the Judgment effect now acts as a Taunt on top of it's base mechanic, and because of Precision 3/3, and given that most Tank builds are hitcapped, this taunt is impossible to miss or resist (note that Judgment isn't subject to parry or dodge). This power comes at a cost though - many people argue that the taunt competing for Judgment is bad design, but I actually don't think so. You should always let some other Tank generate better threat, which you can then make up for with this absolutely overpowered Taunt. And if there is no threat, either on pull or a threat wipe, you JoR anyways to establish threat, which, remember, is also a spell that always lands. What I think conflicts with SoJ however is the fact that Crusader Strike exists, which can GCD lock a Tankadin, causing a delay in taunting that other classes don't have. Warrior and Bear taunts are OGCD (excluding Mocking Blow, but the strenght of this spell is that Warriors have 2 taunts), and so is Judgment, but SoJ is not, which can delay your taunts especially if someone suddenly critted a Shadow Bolt and ripped threat. The other small annoying side of it is that if you judged Wisdom beforehand, Justice will remove the Wisdom effect, making Pally tanking without a Ret in tow (especially one who has the CS libram and PvP gloves) a bit awful.

To go off of that, a recent fix has also made it so that rage/energy/mana procs generate threat, apparently as intended. This opens up a lot of threat generation for Prot Paladin - currently working on a Hand of Edward set with 2/3 incendosaur, and I am already generating miles more threat than my guild's Paladin tank. Having to judge Justice as the sole melee Paladin can be quite damaging to sustained threat generation, assuming you are supposed to keep threat for a long period of time after taunting.

While there have also been other various talent reworks, the main takeaways are that SoC can no longer be used together with Holy Shock in PvP (a good change), Prot had Redoubt and Shield Spec significantly improved, and you don't have to go down till the last row to get Holy Shield, another giant buff as this allows for more threat focused talent builds. Ardent Defender unfortunately is more of a leveling / AoE farming talent than a raiding talent, as it's rare to benefit from the mitigation component when you are more than liable to be oneshot when you are below 35% MT-ing a boss. However, keeping in mind the much better itemization on TWoW, Prot is finally a good tanking option in raids, which is always a good thing.

In fact, all three roles of Paladin are good, however, Prot and Ret don't come without their quirks. While I have delved a little bit into it, I'd like to dedicate a new section to some of the design issues I've encountered.

2. Obscured information

There are a lot of different mechanics in this game that are simply never communicated to players, even from level1 onwards - and I am going to list them all.

The game doesn't tell you what your main stats translate to. STR, AGI, STAM, INT and SPI are never precisely communicated to the player based on the class you play.

The game never explains the hit table, melee and spellhit, weaponskills, parry hasting and the importance of standing behind a mob when hitting it.

The game never explains the swing timer, spell pushback and what causes the swing timer to reset.

The game never explains threat generation, nor is there a natural way to track it.

Edit: The game never explains how Rage generation is calculated, the energy tickrate and mana regen mechanics.

The game never explains that Seal of Righteousness can trigger all damage based procs.

The game never explains that you can use on-hit items to generate extra procs of Judgment of Wisdom. In fact, it also doesn't explain why Judgment of Wisdom isn't PPM based but Judgment of Light is, and also why on-hit items only really work with JoW but not JoL.

The game never explains Windfury's mechanics.

The game never explains which spells of Paladin are based on spellhit, and which are based on weapon skills and melee hit. The game never explains the buff and debuff cap.

The game never explains which buffs and consumables stack with each other, and which don't.

The game never explains which weapon procs work with JotC and which don't.

The game never explains which weapon procs scale with spell power, and which don't.

Sometimes, the game even lies to you, telling you that items like Ragehammer and Sword of Zeal raise your raw damage dealt by some amount, only for it to not actually increase anything (because it actually raises attack power by 20/10, barely a DPS gain).

What I'm guessing is happening is that the game thinks you swung twice - once for Holy Strike, and once as just a normal auto attack. The point is, Ret both generates too much sustain threat and has insane threat spikes. It has to be one or the other, it can't be both. If you generate too much sustain threat, you can adjust your build to generate less mana and focus more on regenning mana through consumes, Innervates, Shadow Priests or Arcane Mages. author: Ravenstone
subject: Re: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
Thank you for the post, was a nice read. I'm only going to focus on the SoR vs SotC bit of this as it is the part I feel most strongly about.

I'm in agreement with Geojak on the thought that SoR shouldn't double proc. I think your suggestion would take the class in the wrong direction. I don't think SoC and SotC do compete against SoR as SoR just eclipses both of them in terms of effectiveness. You say equalizing the Seals wouldn't be interesting, though I'm not entirely sure what you mean by equalizing. In my mind they should all be distinct with their own use cases. Currently it isn't interesting because SoR is better 99% of the time. There is very little reason for Paladins to be using anything else. It is the best tanking Seal, and it is the best DPS Seal. It completely sidelines SotC and SoC in PvE. In PvP I believe Holy Shock is a better build than anything Ret offers and thus SoR will be the Seal of choice again, though haven't played in a while now so maybe that has changed.

I also don't agree with the suggestion to change SotC into a tanking seal since it has never been viewed as such, and just feels forced by todays circumstance rather than by intended class design.

Inherently, I feel like I am the opposing side of your view that the proc based gameplay with absurd mana economy is fun. I think it completely removes all decision making and cheapens the gameplay in the moment since you no longer have to think about your mana. I'd prefer the Paladin be more thematic and be good reliant on his own abilities rather than reliant on procs, and consequently completely circumvent an aspect of gameplay.

author: Liljon
subject: Re: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
@ravenstone
To explain, the reason why I used the word "compete" despite SoR eclipsing SotC and SoC - as you correctly put it - is because SoR, SotC and SoC are all, without exception, damaging seals, therefore they compete to be used. SoW competes against SoL, debuffing Judgments compete against each other as well. You can only use one at a time.

And I'd like to emphasize the primary reason why SoR is infinitely better than the rest - Windfury. Per auto, you have roughly 36% chance to proc a Windfury with SoR. The thing is, the moment you take WF out of the equation, you'll instantly begin to see the Seals be a bit more diverse. SoC is suddenly hyper useful against low HP and CC-able targets. SoR is good for longer drawn out fights. SotC is... well, only useful on Chromaggus. The only good argument for SotC is if you have drastically low hit% as the added haste compensates with more attacks to land. But as soon as WF is in the mix, SoR becomes the best.

All three of these Seals have wildly different ways of doing the same thing - dealing damage. And what Geojak was arguing for is that those two Seals are useless because SoR is so strong. Which is why I said that equalizing them wouldn't be a good solution.

The thing is, Windfury has massive implications on class design. It adds SO much damage and procs to the game. Again, consider on hit effects without WF. Suddenly, managing mana is way more involved, you get your choice in itemization - do you want more or less, are you using faster or slower weapons? WF procs however make you generate much more mana, like, significantly more. And the thing is, this also affects Rage for Warriors - it is common to see, even without WF as gear improves, for Warriors to be rage capped, but WF immediately ragecaps any warrior. WF also helps D1 rogues proc way more energy. It is one of those things that have to affect either everyone or no one (including Shamans themselves), because the moment we change how resources are managed for 1 class, we enter the slippery slope.

Personally, I've only been using 2/3 Incendosaur with a slow weapon because of this and I still end up low on mana sometimes, forcing me to downrank on Crusader Strike and Consecration.

And to round this all up, this is why I'd like to turn SotC into a tanking Seal. Letting players feel and be strong is amazing, and SoR + JoW + WF is the golden ticket to that. It's really no different* from Warriors power fantasy. We might "dumb down" the mana eco, but the DMG rotation is actually quite nuanced on top of basic Paladin utility.

Aside from current SotC just being a mess in itself cause of its Judgment. Prot Paladins are subject to the dumbest threat variance due to Holy Strike in a game where threat is king, and I believe turning SotC into a tanking Seal is the best way to take a Seal that has no real identity.

And about SoC, I've had a couple deep ret buddies play Warsong. Repentance and SoC SLAPS in small scale fights.

author: Liljon
subject: Re: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
Oh, SoC is absolutely very good in **extremely short fights** as the proc is based on PPM - SoC is set to 7. The only variance is crits on the procs. Of course, assuming there is no WF available.

The thing is, I absolutely see where you - and many others who argue that our damaging Seals should offer more choice and be diversified more - come from. It sounds like a dream to have that selection, and I'd enjoy the design you proposed quite a bit myself. However, we simply can't rule out Windfury. Even for Spellrets at the moment, WF is the best weapon imbue you can get (even better than Flametongue / Shadow Oil) - you'd have to massively rework or remove WF if you want to accomodate a more personalized selection, therefore, according to your proposal, SoC would become the best seal and SoR and SotC would wallow in mediocrity until you don't have a Windfury.

One of the things that I'm in favour of - especially knowing how slow TWoW is on development - is making sure that changes are as efficient as possible. Maybe a greater rework has a place in the future, but for now, I'd argue that for now, TWoW should do it's best to **finish** what they have on the table currently. And when it comes to a redesign, they have to put in a lot of thinking into how they can make it a more compelling and enjoyable class without sacrificing it's identity and power.

In my mind, the things they need to finish are threat generation across Ret and Prot, extending Ardent Defender to activate on damage that would bring you to the HP treshold, and making sure that game mechanics are better communicated to the players. With these changes, it is my belief that Paladin overall would be set up for the long term, buying the dev team time to rework Paladin (or at least the damage Seals) without any major pressure.

Edit: one thing I left out. SotC really never had any identity, both on Vanilla and TWoW. Back in Vanilla, the debuff cap meant you couldn't benefit from it (although there were raids built around judging every rank of SotC for big holy damage gains and stack priests and paladins) without pushing some other more important debuff off. On TWoW, Crusader Strike is just an infinitely better version of SotC and honestly for the longest time I was questioning why SotC was even left in the game with CS present - not only have they increased the debuff cap, but also created a spell that does damage and doesn't conflict with Judgments, on top of it also being able to proc stuff (which, again, according to them is not an intended mechanic, but it is what it is).

author: Ravenstone
subject: Re: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
Correct me if I'm wrong, but it appears to me that the entire premise of your last post is specifically around being in a raid environment. The majority of the game you will not have access to WF. Even in a raid environment you are not guaranteed WF 100% of the time. This is where the diversification of Seals should show. As it stands today, you could never bother learning SotC (and in my opinion SoC) and not miss out on anything. You would be able to Tank and DPS near optimally without ever choosing a different damage Seal. I understand you wish to change this with SotC becoming a Tanking Seal but in my eyes that goes against the thematics and original identity of the ability. Honestly, I think reverting to Vanilla JotC, buffing SotC and removing SoR ability to double proc gives a far better foundation to build a better Ret and Prot than currently. I acknowledge there would be many more issues that would need to be addressed than there currently are, but I still feel it'd be better long term. I also acknowledge that this is very unlikely to happen, but that doesn't change my stance.

Regarding SotC in Vanilla, again it had its identity, but as you correctly state, it wasn't able to be used in raiding due to the debuff limit. But to make the claim it didn't have an identity because it wasn't used in a raiding environment ignores the fact that it was used it most other facets of PvE. It also suffered from the Seal half being incredibly ineffectual, but the Judgement debuff was valued, proven by the fact CS now has the effect.

In TWoW, JotC has been supplanted by CS, which is undeniably the better spell in terms of effectiveness. Having said that I think CS is a badly designed spell, and quite frankly disingenuous on the part of the TWoW team. The very fact that you wondered why SotC still exists I feel should never have happened.

author: Liljon
subject: Re: My experience with Paladin - feedback (LONG)
content_md:
Oh, you are absolutely correct - I said as much in the OP, I mainly come from a raiding environment with my feedback.

As for SoC, you are correct, you never really have to learn it barring PvP - you can if you wish to optimize dealing damage to low HP / CC-d targets in raids (and even anywhere else tbh) which can happen quite a bit when you don't have Windfury, but SotC is an actual GODSENT for farming gold. Flame Wrath is just busted. And of course, as I noted in the OP, Blackblade of Shahram is a weapon that exists, but you can even go for an Arcanite Champion with Crusader enchant pre-pull and judge JotC while the Tank is building threat, if you don't want to be stuck in UBRS forever.

To bring up another argument for making SotC a tanking seal - or at the very least, not reverting it to it's original state: imagine a world where we have no debuff cap for SotC to get stuck on. Now, you would still not really find the space to fit it into your raids, for a couple reasons:
 - Paladin slots are being taken up by Shamans, therefore giving you less Paladins to put up all your Judges
 - Prot Paladins can't ever judge Wisdom / Crusader on Taunt heavy fights because Justice pushes it off, therefore it has to be Rets
 - Judgment timers aren't restored globally, individual Paladins have to refresh individual Judgments with their attacks
 - Paladins are brought in 3 separate roles, and it is likely you won't have multiple Rets
Crusader Strike to me is just insane QoL. Being able to globally apply a debuff, not unlike Sunder, on top of it also doing damage and not being at the risk of falling off is just amazing. Of course, not to mention that TWoW has increased debuff caps, and the fact that Prot Paladin is a thing means CS is absolutely vital.

And I understand that not every composition and situation is going to be optimal. Hell, the guild I'm raidleading, I should consider myself blessed that we have up to 6 Windfuries in our raids, and 4 guaranteed almost every raid. But at the end of the day, even outside raids, where do we really fit in our Vanilla Crusaders? Judging SoR / SoC is just simply better when you are constantly facing low HP targets, be it a dungeon or open world, not to mention that for longer drawn out fights as a solo Paladin, you would probably want Wisdom anyways to actually be able to cast heals and other spells. To me, Vanilla SotC doesn't go beyond "that one Seal we use for leveling when we have low hit% but a super slow weapon, up until level 20 when we go sword and board AoE farm mode".

I also want to say, at the risk of delving into nitpicks and whataboutism, the original Crusader Strike from the Vanilla Beta behaved exactly like here on TWoW - no cooldown, relatively high mana cost, physical damage (though it did more back then), and applies a stacking Holy SP debuff. SotC was created to make up for the axing of Crusader Strike from the OG Beta. If anything, SotC is just a hollow shell of what was once a fantastic spell. Then again, there are plenty of things they axed about Paladin design, even during the live release of the game.

At the end of the day, something has to be done about SotC, and threat in general. Rets generate too much and Prots are subject to too much variance. Reworking SotC based on my idea is one way to go, there are plenty of other ones to take.

Judging SoR / SoC is just simply better when you are constantly facing low HP targets, be it a dungeon or open world, not to mention that for longer drawn out fights as a solo Paladin, you would probably want Wisdom anyways to actually be able to cast heals and other spells. To me, Vanilla SotC doesn't go beyond "that one Seal we use for leveling when we have low hit% but a super slow weapon, up until level 20 when we go sword and board AoE farm mode".

I also want to say, at the risk of delving into nitpicks and whataboutism, the original Crusader Strike from the Vanilla Beta behaved exactly like here on TWoW - no cooldown, relatively high mana cost, physical damage (though it did more back then), and applies a stacking Holy SP debuff. SotC was created to make up for the axing of Crusader Strike from the OG Beta. If anything, SotC is just a hollow shell of what was once a fantastic spell. Then again, there are plenty of things they axed about Paladin design, even during the live release of the game.

At the end of the day, something has to be done about SotC, and threat in general. Rets generate too much and Prots are subject to too much variance. Reworking SotC based on my idea is one way to go, there are plenty of other ones to take.

author: Rudezlad
subject: Re: Idea for Paladin Change
content_md:
Yeah, Reckoning, as it currently stands, is flawed in two major ways, in both pve and pvp:

 1) As a tanking talent, you strive to become immune to crits, as in, have defense 390 for pve. The more defense you have over your current lvl x 5, the lower the crit chance against you is, with base value being 5% chance to be crit by enemies of your own level. So when that 390 defense gets achieved, you can no longer benefit from reckoning in pve.

 2) The effect of reckoning proc is not tied to weapon speed and/or type, which makes it most effective for slow 2h weapons, and least effective for fast one-handed weapons. But since it requires you to be hit (and crit), you can't really benefit from it as a dps unless you are actually getting hit (or solo), and in my experience when you do get hit as dps, the actual tank will instinctively try and make the enemy stop hitting you and hit them instead.

 3) In PVP, chances are that reckoning would proc a lot, since player character melee dps tend to have a higher crit chance than pve enemies. A fix to address reckoning's flaws might make it less useful with regards to pvp.

In TBC, reckoning was changed in following ways:

 1) Its proc chance was made to be 2% per talent point, so at 5/5 it would have 10% chance of proccing when being hit
 2) Its effect was changed to give (and overwrite whatever reckoning stacks you previously had) you 4 stacks of reckoning for 8 seconds, and every autoswing you make removes 1 stack of reckoning from you while making your autoswing hit twice.
 3) While the proc chance is lower in pvp against high crit players, 10% proc chance for double autoswing effectiveness for 8 seconds makes up for it.

This fixed the talent with regards to striving for crit immunity, and with regards to weapon speed benefits. A fast weapon would hit 4 times in that 8 second time window, whereas a slow weapon would hit 2 times, maybe 3 times. This fix would be ideal, although it might be a bit strong in comparison to other vanilla talents, so maybe adjust that 8 second timer down to 4 seconds and nrof stacks to 3 to keep it in line with the power of other talents. Either way, having a talent that no longer works when you become uncrittable is a very bad idea.

Reckoning is also not just about damage, but also about regaining mana (or health) through judgement effect being on the target you hit twice with reckoning. It is basically a threat increasing effect either way, since mana regain / heal also generates aoe threat, and the additional payload of damage is single-target threat. And with the additional mana you regain through working reckoning, you have better mana economy for keeping consecrate and holy shield up at all times.

content_html:
After playing Turtle Wow for some time, I have given Protection Paladins some serious thought. I have provided a breakdown of talents and abilities below that I feel would make Protection a much more flavorful spec to play and making them somewhat viable in raids, but still not as perfect as Protection Warriors for big boss fights.

When looking over these talent changes, you will notice a dramatic difference in the required number of points spent in the Protection tree. This is because the Retribution tree points are very cheap and go a long way compared to the ridiculously expensive talents in the Protection tree.

Effectively, the points are not actually massive when you consider the new changes.
Protection Paladins lose access to Vengeance and Seal of Command with this new build and Paladins must choose between One Handed Weapons Specialization talent or having Improved Retribution Aura. Aoe dmg vs Single target dmg flavor choice.

I really like the intended function of classic Protection Paladins, a tank that slowly drains their target through attritional damage.
Essentially, Holy bleeds that come from multiple sources of passive abilities. Ret aura/Holy Shield/Sanctuary/Shield Spikes/ETC.

I wanted to build on this idea that Protection Paladins are not immediate damage dealers, but stack damage over time and build threat slowly but surely over time for tanking purposes. This makes for incredibly fun gameplay, but also keeps the spirit and functional place of Paladins in the tanking tiers.

What is the end goal here? Make Protection paladins a very viable, but second choice tank, behind Protection Warriors.
Allow Protection Paladins to enjoy themselves with entertaining gameplay and not constantly fight an uphill battle. Protection Paladins should be able to MT most bosses in raids and hold threat on their intended targets. Swapping Protection Warriors and Paladins depending on the fight would be a nice change of pace. Edited

(Talent)Improved Devotion Aura 2/2: Increases the armor bonus of your Devotion Aura by 15%(Total 30%) per rank. Devotion Aura also grants the Paladin 4% Stamina per rank(Total 8%).

- Devotion Aura is largely useless to Prot paladins in it's current state. This change helps Paladins soak damage from
raid/dungeon bosses without also buffing them during AOE farming(which they already are good at). This means this
buff really only buffs the Paladin in specific situations and is not a flat-out increase at all times. It could also be tied to
"Requires a Shield to be equipped". Obviously, this talent will only benefit the Paladin casting it and not the party they are in. Think of this as almost a defensive stance.

(Talent) Redout 3/3: No changes except 10% per rank(Total 30%).

-Dropping cost to 3 points to be used in conjunction with Improved Devotion Aura.

(Talent)Toughness 5/5: Increases your armor value from items by 4% per rank(Total 20%) and reduces damage taken from spells by 3% per rank(Total 15%).

-Toughness is an expensive talent for only a 10% armor buff. This talent would be best suited for deeper in the Protection tree as to not benefit Retribution. If you look at other classes, the majority of 5/5 talents are vital to their build. This would give Paladins a decent hardiness to melee damage as well as a bit of magic protection, considering the lack of a spell reflect. Protection paladins do not use bubble during PvE encounters, as they are the tank and lose all threat.

(Talent)Anticipation 3/3: While under the effects of Righteous Fury, increase the Paladin's chance to block by 2% per rank(Total 6%).

-Anticipation is known to be the worst talent in the Protection tree. 5 ranks for only 10 defense is completely worthless. The block could also be replaced with a dodge increase. Knocking this down to 3 points allows Prot paladins to learn the next talent change listed.

(Talent)Improved Hammer of Justice: Delete. Replace with:
Holy Ground 2/2 : Increases the threat generated by Consecration and all affected targets are slowed
by 10%(Max 20%) per rank. Targets affected by Consecration cannot flee.

-Consecration is a wildly expensive ability for Protection paladins but is also the bread and butter of aoe threat. This
allows the Paladin to keep mobs nearby and a speed/time buffer to re-target and aggro loose mobs. The anti-flee mechanic would be a really nice flavor add to Prot paladins that would make them unique to other tanks, but it is not as necessary as the extra threat.

(Talent) Improved Righteous Fury 2/2: Increases the amount of threat generated by your Righteous Fury spell
by 30% per rank(Total 60%).

- 10% threat buff, nothing major. Dropped to 2 required points.

(Talent) Improved Seal of Justice 3/3: Replace with:
(Talent) Seal of Justice 1/1. Melee attacks strike two additional targets and apply Holy Justice, which deals 50 holy damage
over 15 seconds. Holy Justice can stack up to 5 times. Each of the Paladin's weapon attacks also deal up to 25% weapon
damage as additional holy damage, based on the number of Holy Justice stacks applied to the target.

- This obviously is an aoe version of Seal of Vengeance, with a slightly less bonus damage multiplier. This would be extremely
beneficial to hold threat on multiple targets in dungeons and aoe farming would be much more entertaining, not to mention
questing would be much better.


(Talent) Reckoning 2/2: Gives you a 17.5% chance per rank(Total 35%) to gain an extra attack after successfully blocking an attack. That can only happen once every 5 seconds.
Updated Reckoning change after discussion in Discord.
(Talent) Reckoning 2/2: Gives you a 20% chance per rank(Total 40%) to gain an extra attack with an additional 60% holy damage after successfully blocking an attack. That can only happen once every 6 seconds.

-Reckoning is currently never taken in favor of Vengeance in order to deal more damage and hold threat. This could be averted by making Reckoning actually aid in damage. Vengeance is also super RNG dependent and leaves the paladin without threat generation often. By giving this ability a higher probability of the extra swing, but capping how often it happens, gives the paladin a sustained damage increase without making it a lottery jackpot when aoe tanking multiple mobs. These updates were applied after discussing the damage output of vengeance being far superior to even the Reckoning changes. This attack would also stack with the updated Seal of Justice aoe changes.

(Talent)Toughness 5/5: Increases your armor value from items by 4% per rank(Total 20%) and reduces damage taken from spells by 3% per rank(Total 15%).

 -Toughness is an expensive talent for only a 10% armor buff. This talent would be best suited for deeper in the Protection tree as to not benefit Retribution. If you look at other classes, the majority of 5/5 talents are vital to their build. This would give Paladins a decent hardiness to melee damage as well as a bit of magic protection, considering the lack of a spell reflect. Protection paladins do not use bubble during PvE encounters, as they are the tank and lose all threat.

(Talent)Anticipation 3/3: While under the effects of Righteous Fury, increase the Paladin's chance to block by 2% per rank(Total 6%).

 -Anticipation is known to be the worst talent in the Protection tree. 5 ranks for only 10 defense is completely worthless. The block could also be replaced with a dodge increase. Knocking this down to 3 points allows Prot paladins to learn the next talent change listed.

(Talent)Improved Hammer of Justice: Delete. Replace with:
Holy Ground 2/2 : Increases the threat generated by Consecration and all affected targets are slowed
by 10%(Max 20%) per rank. Targets affected by Consecration cannot flee.

 -Consecration is a wildly expensive ability for Protection paladins but is also the bread and butter of aoe threat. This
allows the Paladin to keep mobs nearby and a speed/time buffer to re-target and aggro loose mobs. The anti-flee mechanic would be a really nice flavor add to Prot paladins that would make them unique to other tanks, but it is not as necessary as the extra threat.

(Talent) Improved Righteous Fury 2/2: Increases the amount of threat generated by your Righteous Fury spell
by 30% per rank(Total 60%).

 - 10% threat buff, nothing major. Dropped to 2 required points.

(Talent) Improved Seal of Justice 3/3: Replace with:
(Talent) Seal of Justice 1/1. Melee attacks strike two additional targets and apply Holy Justice, which deals 50 holy damage
over 15 seconds. Holy Justice can stack up to 5 times. Each of the Paladin's weapon attacks also deal up to 25% weapon
damage as additional holy damage, based on the number of Holy Justice stacks applied to the target.

 - This obviously is an aoe version of Seal of Vengeance, with a slightly less bonus damage multiplier. This would be extremely
beneficial to hold threat on multiple targets in dungeons and aoe farming would be much more entertaining, not to mention
questing would be much better.

(Talent) Reckoning 2/2: Gives you a 17.5% chance per rank(Total 35%) to gain an extra attack after successfully blocking an attack.  That can only happen once every 5 seconds.
Updated Reckoning change after discussion in Discord.
(Talent) Reckoning 2/2: Gives you a 20% chance per rank(Total 40%) to gain an extra attack with an additional 60% holy damage after successfully blocking an attack.   That can only happen once every 6 seconds.

 -Reckoning is currently never taken in favor of Vengeance in order to deal more damage and hold threat. This could be averted by making Reckoning actually aid in damage. Vengeance is also super RNG dependent and leaves the paladin without threat generation often. By giving this ability a higher probability of the extra swing, but capping how often it happens, gives the paladin a sustained damage increase without making it a lottery jackpot when aoe tanking multiple mobs. These updates were applied after discussing the damage output of vengeance being far superior to even the Reckoning changes. This attack would also stack with the updated Seal of Justice aoe changes.

(Talent) One-Handed Weapon Specialization 2/2: Dropped to 2 points from 5. Increases the damage you deal with one-handed
melee weapons by 5% per rank(Total 10%).

 - This talent is a flavor choice for the Paladin. They can either choose this talent or dig into the Retribution tree and finish off their points with Improved Retribution Aura. Trade off is increased damage to 3 melee targets vs increased damage to 4+ targets.

(Talent) Ardent Defender 1/1: Reduce all damage taken by 35% for 15 seconds and regenerate 15% of your mana over that time. 2 minute cooldown.
Updated Ardent Defender after Discord discussion.
(Talent) Ardent Defender 1/1: Reduce all damage taken by 35% for 15 seconds and increase your threat generation by 30% for 15 seconds. 1.5 minute cooldown.

 - Ardent Defender has been skipped over by every decent Protection Paladin due to it's benefit almost never working. If a Paladin reaches 25% health, even a 35% reduction in damage will not stop them from being one-shot. It would be nice to have a panic button when boss fights get hairy or a quick mana boost if you make a mana mistake. The updates to the changes were made because other Paladins felt that mana management should not be as forgiving as this change would allow. Also, threat generation for later tiers of raiding has become problematic, this change would assist the paladin with holding threat for the duration of fights.
content_html:
After playing Turtle Wow for some time, I have given Protection Paladins some serious thought. I have provided a breakdown of talents and abilities below that I feel would make Protection a much more flavorful spec to play and making them somewhat viable in raids, but still not as perfect as Protection Warriors for big boss fights.

When looking over these talent changes, you will notice a dramatic difference in the required number of points spent in the Protection tree. This is because the Retribution tree points are very cheap and go a long way compared to the ridiculously expensive talents in the Protection tree.

Effectively, the points are not actually massive when you consider the new changes.
Protection Paladins lose access to Vengeance and Seal of Command with this new build and Paladins must choose between One Handed Weapons Specialization talent or having Improved Retribution Aura. Aoe dmg vs Single target dmg flavor choice.

I really like the intended function of classic Protection Paladins, a tank that slowly drains their target through attritional damage.
Essentially, Holy bleeds that come from multiple sources of passive abilities. Ret aura/Holy Shield/Sanctuary/Shield Spikes/ETC.

I wanted to build on this idea that Protection Paladins are not immediate damage dealers, but stack damage over time and build threat slowly but surely over time for tanking purposes. This makes for incredibly fun gameplay, but also keeps the spirit and functional place of Paladins in the tanking tiers.

What is the end goal here? Make Protection paladins a very viable, but second choice tank, behind Protection Warriors.
Allow Protection Paladins to enjoy themselves with entertaining gameplay and not constantly fight an uphill battle. Protection Paladins should be able to MT most bosses in raids and hold threat on their intended targets. Swapping Protection Warriors and Paladins depending on the fight would be a nice change of pace. Edited

author: Khagrim
subject: Re: Straight up not having a good time
content_md:
Some advice for lvling prot pallies
You don't need strength, it does nothing for you
Try to find mail/plate of the Eagle (stam/int). More int = more mana = more Consecrations and Holy Shields
Quests usually don't reward int mail/plate so your best bet is AH. You don't need to buy a mount at 40 so you should have enough gold.
Use a fast weapon. Seals and Judgements of Light and Wisdom don't have ppm so fast weapon = more procs = more mana which seems to be the main problem pre 60.
Your best weapon for mana regen is a lvl 33 green Knightly Longsword with a whoping 1.5 speed. You can use it all the way to 60 cause there are no faster weapons that pallys can use. Flurry Axe is slightly better but is a world drop epic so costs accordingly. Maybe TWoW added more fast weapons, will check database.
Engineering is great. Grenades are a great way to range pull and get some initial aggro and you can use Target Dummies if a pull goes wrong.
Don't bother with keeping aggro on all things all the time. It's Vanilla and it's almost impossible for any class at low lvl. If skull runs away from you let the dps finish it and switch to the next target. If dps complain ignore them.
Use 2-3 Consecrations in a pull, be conservative with your mana. Use rank 1 Consecration if you really need more after the initial 2

content_md:

> Updates: 8-8-23
>
>  (Ability) Hand Of Reckoning. Taunts the target to attack you. If the target is tauntable and not currently attacking you, deal (1*0.5 Spell Power) holy damage. Costs 5% total mana. 25 second cooldown.

I wanted to touch more on this:

I proposed to replace the mechanics of Seal of Justice completely, because prot needs it's own damage seal that works with it's gameplay. The changes to the seal allow Prot to stack aggro on their targets and secondary targets along with actually producing damage to their target.

Also, with a 5% mana cost and a 25-second cooldown. You actually have to plan your taunts.
content_html:
Updates: 8-8-23

(Ability) Hand Of Reckoning. Taunts the target to attack you. If the target is tauntable and not currently attacking you, deal (1*0.5 Spell Power) holy damage. Costs 5% total mana. 25 second cooldown.

This ability was given to paladins in wrath pre patch because it solved so many issues with core mechanics. The Paladin community has been begging for it. With the change to seal of justice, a taunt will still be needed for major fights. This should not be useable on PvP targets. I increased the mana cost from 3 to 5% because many paladins want mana conservation to be a prime consideration for paladins.
I wanted to touch more on this:

I proposed to replace the mechanics of Seal of Justice completely, because prot needs it's own damage seal that works with it's gameplay. The changes to the seal allow Prot to stack aggro on their targets and secondary targets along with actually producing damage to their target.

Right now, Prot has a serious inability to deal any significant damage, which is why all raid tanking Paladins have swapped over to a 2H ret-heavy build. Without a 2H weapon, they can't hold threat reliably. With a combination of a true taunt and a damage-stacking seal, prot can finally hold threat in raids and dungeons.

Also, with a 5% mana cost and a 25-second cooldown. You actually have to plan your taunts.

author: Hellion
subject: Re: Prot Paladin Changes (Updated)
content_md:
Any reason to skip over righteous defense, the taunt that was added in TBC? it worked wonderfully for me and i tanked everything in TBC classic. it fits well in line with the multiple mob trash tank theme that's already present with the class/spec.
 -you deal with twice the CD of the warrior's taunt(17 seconds IIRC)
 -you can get aggro of up to 3 mobs at once
 -works by casting it on the player, rather than the mob.(this can be worked around via macro making it apply to the mob's target.)

i agree about giving the class seal of vengeance although its not necessary to make it hit multiple mobs. I think you have more than enough of that with all the passive attacks like consecration and blessing of sanctuary. if something should be added to hit multiple mobs, i think it should be something with snap threat like judgement of righteousness. maybe it could hit 2 extra mobs by putting points into an existing or some new talent. although I still don't really feel it needs it.

Ardent Defender TBC version was junk even then and adding it into vanilla was a mistake if they weren't going to buff it. It doesn't need to be OP cheese like WotLK though. making it a panic button I agree with. Not as beefy as shield wall with the 30ish % damage reduction and maybe it could gain some kind of effect that makes it better for tanking multiple mobs.

kind of going on and on here but just wanted to share more opinions because I love the class and its theme.    happy_turtle

One thing I would love to see added to the talent tree in exchange for some of the useless stuff, is something to increase shield block *value* via stacking a stat. right now, 20 points of strength gives just 1 block value. its not very good to be frank. Block value's strength for a paladin lies in tanking several mobs at once. instead of stacking tons of HP for tanking through singular big hits, when tanking lots of mobs who each hit for a small amount, shaving down that amount by raising block value is the way to go. There is a talent that increases block value by 30% but I think there should be an option to stack stats to increase it farther. as it is now, there just isn't enough block value in game to make it worth stacking and strength gives too little return. buffing the return from strength might be good but another route could be intelligence. With the current shield block talent, you may actually want to stack Intelligence, because if you have a larger mana pool, you will receive more mana back when blocking. all the while your base spell costs remain the same.

another talent thats total junk in its current state is the one handed sword specialization. the way its currently worded, the only thing it will increase is the actual sword swing's damage. this will increase your SoR very slightly but not enough to make it worth it. In TBC it was changed to give a 10% increase to all damage. That's probably too hot for vanilla though. considering that righteous fury only increases threat caused by holy damage, the increased white damage from your sword swing is next to worthless and absolutely not worth 5 talent points.

Devotion aura is a tough one. its not very good for tanking because its not enough armor to really compete with the threat gains of sanctity aura or retribution aura. I think it would be a step in the right direction to make it increase armor farther or add some kind of scaling armor buff. another direction you could go is to make it encompass all the defensive auras. shadow resist, fire resist, frost resist... if the talent buffed those that could be appealing. a 3rd idea would be reducing all damage by a flat % like we got from Righteous Fury in TBC. that gave us 6% total damage reduction with 3 points into the RF talent. not sure if 6% would be too much but we def don't want to step on warrior's toes with their 10% damage reduction via defensive stance. besides, we have a lot of auras, none of them should be over or underpowered in a perfect world.

Thats all I can think of for now but I really do like a lot of the stuff you've brought up and suggested. I don't want our class to be overpowered but I do think its reasonable to want to make some of the useless parts of its kit more useful. IDK how often the Devs read this stuff or how much of it is actually possible to change but I'd be happy to throw more suggestions or insight out there.   happy_turtle

author: Jrobz
subject: Re: Prot Paladin Changes (Updated)
content_md:
Lots of good ideas here. Lemme add mine and some back story.

I tanked on Paladin all through Classic Vanilla and raid Tanked through BWL. I had full T2, Scarab, DPS caster rings, 400 +SP, etc. Having actually done this, while trying NOT to BoK spam (aka IMO play it 'right'), the primary issues I saw are:

Constant (1-60) on no decent pull
Mid (20-60) Severe mana issue due to gearing options - drink after every pull
Late (when DPS is in full raid gear) on our Shields dont scale for damage reduction

author: Jrobz
subject: Re: Prot Paladin Changes (Updated)
content_md:
That certainly isn't a bad idea as that sweeps over the itemization issue among a few other things.

If STR/AP is to be a major stat for (at least Prot/Ret) Paladins, drawing in significantly more SBV from STR could fix the Shield scaling/survivability issues. The other core viability issue is Tank Paladins going Ret in later stages of content due to Prot threat ceilings. My more broader changes seek to fix both of these while keeping Prot the tank tree tookit through out the 1-60 and end game.

Just like the Druid Bear, you never want the Hybrid classes to be broadly superior to the Mainline Class at their niche, but I think the game has enough varied encounters to where a Hybrid tank can have moments of shining and still be broadly capable of filling the role. I would think this is a worthy design goal for Druid and Paladin tanks. I think if we tune this 'ideally', RAIDs would be optimized by having a Tank of each type. My Guild tried this in Classic Vanilla, and it more or less worked well through BWL, though Paladin was the first to cap out in late Phase 4 (PreAQ) just as Bear was really just getting gearing to shine. Bear was not in a great spot until BWL gear.

content_md:
> **Poggo wrote: Tue Oct 24, 2023 3:46 pm**
> with these suggestions not adressing crits/crushings?

Crushes are problematic within the existing class abilities and combat model.  Can't stack enough avoidance/block to get to consistent full-uptime 102.4.   Within our present ability framework they'd need to modify the redoubt talent to function in a more reliable manner--and that doesn't help druids any.  It'd probably be easier overall to do it the other way around, and draw down Shield Block a bit so that warriors are also crush-vulnerable, then tune the encounters accordingly.

The excessive difficulty of reaching crit immunity can be solved via itemization, A good start would be reverting the spring 2005 defense gear nerf to its stat budget cost.  WoW-style itemization with fixed stat budgets are by nature harsh on hybrid classes that require more stats to do the same job .  It's a weakness of the system.
