Paladins and every other class are getting revamps for v1.17.2 and it may be far too early to guesstimate on how things will go from here without some information from the team.

Akos I have no idea what kind of Paladin style you played or if you played Paladin at all while leveling to max or doing any kind of raiding but your viewpoint seems to be based on vanilla instead of Turtle-WoW.  Everything you said seems to be vanilla-based PvE minus a brief mention of Holy Strike and PvP.

As someone who's actually done all that you've talked about, lemme give you the real picture.
First, I won't be enough of an absolute clown as you are to ignore actual raid mechanics that actively harm and punish those who are casting spells in melee range.  That's a stupid idea and a stupid design.  It was never going to work that way and eventually by Tier 3 Blizzard finally realized this.  Holy Paladins in melee aren't going to be a thing and nothing you suggest will ever change that.  You're actively an absolute moron for even suggesting this and I question whether you've ever done a single raid in any version of vanilla either on Turtle WoW or otherwise.

Warriors don't use shields when tanking non-raid bosses; they often use shields only for specific sections/parts/phases and then do fury/prot to build up threat before swapping back.  In dungeons no warrior bothers to be prot or use a shield as it doesn't build up threat fast enough to satisfy the 'rush' mentality of most DPS on the server and that's partly why you see an empty valley without tanks (or healers) in the LFG system.  People tired of trash DPS who don't know how vanilla aggro works.

In leveling dungeons, a Paladin does not 'leeroy in and pull 3 packs'.  You're thinking of WotLK Paladin that can do that pretty easily and self-sustain (even solo) but not in Vanilla.  Even with the buffs to Paladins the tank still needs to keep an eye on damage and avoid pulling too many packs of ELITE mobs.  If they're non-elite then a Paladin has a bit more leeway to pull but elite mobs are still very tough.  As a brief example, the elite mobs both inside AND outside of Uldaman in the infamous 'tablet room' are so numerous and respawn so quickly as to overwhelm anything that isn't a min-maxed group of level appropriate characters.  Even fully raid-geared 60s who aren't in a tanking gear/spec can end up dying to these mobs (spamming interrupts) if they aren't careful about it.  Merely typing this kind of garbage into a post and thinking you are correct in your assumption makes you seem like an ass, as the saying goes.  You don't know because you're talking nothing but flatulence from said ass.

In raiding, Paladins are often asked to go Holy if healing is an issue for the raid and if they want to use the (frankly busted) 100% mana regen for healing spells via the Illumiantion talent.  Many raid leaders end up being like you and aren't in tune with how Turtle WoW paladins work compared to regular vanilla.  They still feel Paladin tanks or DPS aren't as useful or necessary and they'd be quickly mistaken.  Shamans (without a proper taunt at all) have tanked Naxx in raiding guilds.  If the guild works together they can do whatever is needed to get done and that includes Prot Paladin main tanks and otherwise.  With the JoJ taunt they can actively plan and perform in 99% of raids and raid bosses, minus a handful of raid bosses that mana-drain (a certain boss in AQ20 comes to mind).  Paladin DPS requires specific gear and setup but can perform on-par with most other DPS.  Thing is that vanilla isn't even about min-maxing and never has been.  It was made to be easy enough for a wide variety of skill levels to enjoy raiding.  The community being hostile and exclusionary to force absolute instrumental play is what caused the shift towards that being a requirement for raiding.

All 3 paladin specs on Turtle WoW are useful and viable and capable of whatever is needed both leveling and at endgame raiding and in PvP.  Prot pally may be relegated into a 'point defense' role but they can perform that role fairly well.  The hybrid Prot/Ret build for PvP also works pretty well in both damage and survivability while being built like an absolute tank.

content_md:
Vidnar, my goal was not to keep the paladin class in a disadvantageous position.
If you actually read what I have written, I think that their balance can be 'off' to both directions depending on the context. My goal is to nerf them where they are too strong and buff them where they need help.
Don't mention my name in the same context with the same tone ever again.

I want to avoid further animosity and discuss this in a civilized way.
 **Will be extremely tldr, wanna write my opinion in detail to avoid misunderstandings from my end.**

Based on what I've seen and experienced, I'm telling you, my opinion. about the current state of paladin builds, which will probbaly change as the class changes come.
I do not see them as OP monsters. But I see a duality in the perception of the paladin. One side is like 'I heard that my bro got instakilled in BG by a plate-wearer in a bubble who can selfheal etc', the other side is like 'we were bad for 15 years at Vanilla servers and at the moment the bullying target becomes decent, bullies start to hate'. Both of these are exaggerations.
Paladin was an individually weak class built upon utility. It is true that TWOW 'readded' originally existing abilities to the pala which were removed before realease because of gameplay-ideological reasons. Pala was supposed to be more than what we got back in the day.
Blizzard has learnt from its failure and made every build decent for later expansions (maybe except for the cats, Blizzard has no idea what to do with cats).
We are here arguing over a problem which was solved by Blizzard 10+ years ago.
But we are also limited in how to execute our own changes since every big conceptual change will go against the Vanilla+ design of the server. So design space is rather narrow.

TWOW made paladin a more valid class by increasing DPS output and giving prot more ways to use holy damage to generate threat (among other changes).
But by doing so, they also created a very bursty gameplay rotation (based on holy damage!) which rubbed many people the wrong way. This is why those guys think palas are demi-gods and they repeat stuff like 'nerf holy strike' and 'crusader strike bad' even if they don't know what those abilities even do.
Pala being disgustingly good in PVP is not an opinion. People exaggerate here: pala PVP is indeed disgusting but you can argue that an ele shaman (which doesn't get this amount of sh*t) is equally disgusting at PVP. Here people sit on the 'bro, I got one-shot, it was holy damage in a bubble bro' train and start to argue about things they don't fully understand.
Despite freedom, you can kite the pala. A good hunter, ele shaman or frost mage can easily win those matchups.
But based on this, the 'pro-pala' side flat-out calls the 'pala-haters' retards, arguing that since there are several disgusting PVP builds, pala's PVP tier is justified and nothing should be changed at all.
I'm somewhere in the middle. Would tune down all classes at PVP which I consider above A rank. But it's a personal opinion.

The other side of the coin is raid performance which is a lesser known aspect of the pala because it can't be that easily sold by things like 'bro they one-shot in a bubble bro'.
Palas (not including holy in this whole thing, they are different) are more-or less struggling at the raiding environment. I heard people talking about super-DPS retris and such but every time I was at a raid, I checked the logs and retri consistently places itself around moonkin, well below those who are usually top DPS (some mages and warriors, followed by warlocks, rogues, even an ele shaman if someone has a TF). People tell that pala is bad and nerf holy strike etc without knowing how low sustained DPS retri has (and how much threat it generates for that limited damage).
As for prot, the instance logic changes with raids. At dungeons, the focus is to handle the trash packs, which are followed by a manageable boss which doesn't do too much damage. This is pala heaven, since their tanking toolkit is optimalized for situations where they are hit by many smaller-hitter mobs. At raids the focus is to survive and keep threat on a 30 meter big dragon while the DPS has some sort of epileptic seizure and speedruns button-smashing. Prot pala goes from a very good dungeon tank (in my opinion, the best) to a utility raid tank, preferably offtank. Can still MT almost everything but less ideally than a warrior.

In short, pala is extremely strong at PVP but has weak matchups and not more oppressive than some of the other classes. At raiding, pala is weak.
And what triggers me regarding this whole thing is the way people go around the whole pala vs. shaman thing. Of course it has to be pala vs. shaman. The average TWOW player is a somewhat bald, 30+ guy with a job. And these 30+ guys somehow find a way to spread hate with the pala vs. shaman topic since these classes are faction-specific and of course they represent the whole faction. In actuality it is about a weird identity feud between Alliance and Horde which I think is very childish for adults. I don't wanna 'troll with my shaman buddies to bully poor palas' or 'oppress the abandoned shammies and lie about how OPs the palas, who the admins surely play, totally are'. I just want a balanced gameplay where nothing goes above A rank or below C rank. For me it's not a pala vs. shammie whatever. I just wanna point out how I'd change this class so I'd find it more enjoyable (as the original forum thread was about).

I'd make them less potent at PVP, probably cutting down burstiness (and would also rework some other OP PVP classes). In the meanwhile I'd add defensives for prot and sustained damage to ret so they can move up from the 'moonkin position' at the raid DPS races.

author: Perka123
subject: Ideas for fixing paladins
content_md:
Holy:
Holy Shock: Removed from talent tree and replaced with Light's Mercy
Light's Mercy: Heals your target for X amount of damage, and splashes four nearby allies for 25% of the healing done.
 1.5s cast time, 30 seconds cooldown.

Protection:
One-Handed Specialization: Your one-handed weapon attacks deals 2%/4%/6%/8%/10% of it's damage dealt to nearby targets as holy damage.
Holy Shock: Put it in deep in the prot tree and make it force the target to attack you for 4 seconds (not a taunt, more like Mocking Blow)

Ret: Replace Repentance with Holy Strike. Repentance can become a level 40 baseline spell.
Holy Strike: Reduce Critical strike damage by 20%, cooldown increased to 14 seconds.
Crusader Strike: Cooldown increased to 4 seconds, damage increased by 20%

Bubbles:
Divine Shield: Removed or maybe a deep Holy Talent.
Divine Protection: Cost changed to all mana up to 50%. Increase cooldown from 3 minutes to 10 minutes cooldown.

 **WHY THO?**  mad_turtle
The problem is what every one is complaining about; the burst damage and survival capabilites of paladins in PVP.
By placing Holy Strike at the bottom of the the Ret tree it is no longer combinable with Holy Shock.
"But it still hits to hard". Yes, that why I propose a nerf to it's critting. To make up for it we buff Crusader strike a little bit, to remove it's boring spamming and giving some meaning to it.

Now, Holy Strike is an important attack for Prot pallies, so we give them Holy Shock from the holy tree to make up for it. I've seen a lot of people having hard time adapting to the taunt baked into the Seal of Justice, but instead of completely removing it I opted to make Holy Shock force the attackers attention to help out a little bit.
O-H Specialization I don't really have any argument, I'd just thought it be a more fun talent than just a flat damage increase on single targets. Might not be necessary due to Retribution Aura and Consecration.

To fill the empty spot at the bottom of the holy tree we slap Light's Mercy in there, a fast and powerful panic splash heal worthy of replacing Holy shock.

And lastly, bubbles. I've also seen a lot of people complain about the survivability of paladins with their plate armor, HoF and bubbles.
By nerfing the bubble without taking away it's core principle we make it a life saver that share cooldown with Lay of Hands. This allows paladin to still be able to become immune to damage but at a greater cost.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Ideas for fixing paladins
content_md:
Wanted to reply to this sooner, but finally got to it.
Thanks for adding a section explaining your justification for these changes. Makes it much easier to follow your line of reasoning.

Just like every holy strike discussion let me start by saying there is a bug that applies % dmg bonuses to both the physical weapon damage and then again once its converted to holy. This should not be in the game. There is historic reasons for it on Seal of Command, but since Holy strike is a completely custom ability, there is no justification why it should have this interaction in the first place.

But lets come to the actual discussion at hand

Shockoboy spec is no doubt strong, but while they do have access to Holy strike now, they lost their access to Seal of Command with the previous set of Turtlewow classchanges. While Holy Strike is more Reliable, the SoC variant could potentially punch harder. Which of the Two being more frustrating to fight against is really anyones choice.

If you were to remove holy strike from their arsenal, it would only be fair to give them back their access to SoC.

At the same time holy strike is a centerpiece to paladin for PvE. It allows any breed of paladin to much easier tank in dungeons, it substantially improves the leveling experience and it also serves a vital part for raidtanking. By burrying it deep in the rettree, that is all lost. And you still get blown up by deep rets all the same.

Reducing its crit damage is similarly problematic, as you can end up with scenarios where a hit that replaces your autoattack hits weaker than said autoattack. After all, the abilities damage is not even that insane, but the damage of the autoattack is folded into holy strike too.
If you get hit for a 1.2k Crit from a Warrior and a 1.3k Mortal strike, all is well, but a 2.5k Holy strike is weird.

Id be okey with nerfing bubbles duration. More often than not, you don't need all 12 seconds of it. But nerfing its cooldown makes the class most succeptable to CC in the entire game even more easy pickings for anyone with good crowd control.

Paladin still has no gap closers and is a freekill for all classes that can effectively kite. Im sorry for warriors & rogues, but to ever make the matchup winnable for them is basically impossible. Every class in wow pvp has some hard counters due to the rock paper scissors (and mushrooms) gamedesign.

That all being said, this entire discussion would be completely solved, if holy strike would just apply the targets armor for damage calculation & the bug is fixed

Its actually more or less copy/pasted from the beta version of WoW. It was made by Blizzard merely as a placeholder ability.
Very wisely never intended to be in the final product.

Shockadin has a variety of other perfectly viable Seals. SoC not needed.

You don't typically "fight" against a Ret/Holy Paladin in PVP -- they just nuke you to death in seconds with broken abilities.
You could fight a Prot Paladin but you can often simply ignore them as their damage is rather poor.
But of course no one plays Prot in PVP as its better to 'nuke ppl to death in seconds' rather than "try to outlast them with defense + skill".

Vanilla Paladin Tank players used to whine that all they needed was "a taunt to become viable" -- T-WoW Paladins have moved the goalposts to now whine that they also "NEED Holy Strike too!!". Self-serving dishonesty

Simple fact is that Paladin should not have a 'nuke'. There are countless "game design/common sense" reasons for this.

Warriors are god awful in PVP (for countless reasons). Even that video you reference explains this.
If you are getting stomped by a Warrior you are bad at PVP and deserve to lose.
P.S. Mortal Strike costs 30 rage and is a capstone talent. Its fine that it can hit hard.

No, they should not nerf Bubble duration as that is a core/iconic ability of the Paladin class.
They did change it but only to match TBC version (this was arguably not even a nerf).

No, Paladin is not the 'most vulnerable to CC' -- that is laughable.
Warrior is infamous for being a Frost Nova cuck -- who stands in CC as his team dies around him.
Charge/Intercept are awful and/or extremely unreliable abilities btw.

A Paladin simply charges in on a 208% speed speed mount and deletes a caster.
If inside (where they cannot mount) then they are probably within a cramped room wherein they can -- you guessed it -- delete a caster.

Anyway 1:1 isn't really a thing in PVP Battlegrounds. If a Paladin is chasing a caster/huntard then they are probably bad at PVP and deserve to die/lose.
They had reasonably fair matchups against everyone -- except Rogue/Warrior wherein the Paladin would generally win.
Shadow Priest was a hardcounter to Paladin i suppose.

Anyway T-WoW Paladin has no hard-counter as it is a broken/overpowered class.
It dominates all others -- there is no "fair matchup"...
Except against Frost Mages perhaps -- as Frost Spec is also broken/OP in PVP.
Shadow Priest is now a fair matchup becuz "Pain Spike" made them more OP as well.

This leads to my whole point: T-WoW Paladin Gooners would rather make all classes broken/OP rather than simply remove the half-baked disaster known as "Holy Strike" from the game.
(Either that or nerf classic, iconic, core abilities such as Bubble. lol)

P.S. Ret Paladin was a talent tree designed to provide defensive SUPPORT in PVP.
They were not intended to be a One-Man-Army Golden God GigaChad who aggressively charges in as a 'spearhead' -- as they do today in Turtle Team's World of Paladincraft.

Nor were they intended to 'dominate' in ANY form of PVE.

They were intended to follow closely behind Warriors/Rogues/Etc and spam Cleanse and buffs --
Acting as a bannerman -- around whom their teammates rally and ultimately win the match.

author: Archeon
subject: New Paladin "Epic" Class Changes...
content_md:
These changes overall seem terrible to me,

The fact this was considered for Paladin:
Removed: Sanctified Command

Is crazy, Considering in literally every original vanilla pvp scenario any class which can dispel does dispell paladins and then continue to just spam it non stop leading to the gameplay loop of the paladin being forced to spam seal spells for the entire fight, and this being immediately resolved in tbc... either indicates that anyone who suggested removing dispel protection didnt play paladin in vanilla/tbc or intentionally suggested dispell protection in bad faith to undermine the class.

Secondly you literally identify the issue of "Developer Comment: Mana restoration part of this talent has been quite useless" but fail to understand the issue, the issue isnt that mana restoration is useless but that the design of the mechanic in its current form is useless... the current iteration of paladins getting 20% of their mana back from command judgement presents again a lack of understanding of how the class works, the seal is the primary damage component of the spell and does the same seal damage at rank 1 as max rank... so in many scenarios when conserving mana in pve you just use rank 1... which has a low mana cost meaning no party regen with the talents current form... all you had to do was make it so the talent gave mana back based on a percentage of damage done by the seal not the judgement and it instantly fixes the talent....

Rework: Repentance

lul wut... who asked for this.

all you had to do is make seal of command cleave as the capstone and make repentence the 11 point talent so this trash talent was accessible to the other specs for utility if desired.

I seriously dont even know what the thought process was here.

The new strikes kind of seem interesting however seems like holy strike will be mostly a pve spell realistically, given the option between the two the trade off for a disepllable strength buff doesnt seem worth it in pvp.

Seems like wider community input may have been quite helpful...

author: Mor'ladim
subject: Paladin's Crusader Strike and Holy Strike
content_md:
Currently the rotation looks like this for prot/ret Paladin:
Holy Strike - 6 sec, Crusader Strike - x3*6 sec,then ret/pal renew buff Holy Strike and spam Crusader Strike.
Paladin's defense has a similar principle.

I suggest removing Holy Strike from the general book and adding it to line 5 or 7 of Holy Paladin, removing the overall cooldown, or adding a trigger from blessed strikes.

This solves the problem of removing the damage component of Holy Shock that matches your vision

Developer Comment: Holy Paladin’s damage right now can be quite bursty at times, thanks to Holy Shock. With the new talents allowing for it to reset, we felt like the ranged burst could become too dangerous. Overall Holy damage should be higher thanks to the new strikes, but will require you to remain in melee.
While we understand that the “shockadin” specialization is beloved by many, it does not fit our vision for the class.

and we can now remove the Holy Strike components from Blessed Strikes, Righteous Strikes and Crusader Strikes and give Crusader Strike as a buff. let's call, for example, holy power that gives buffs to talents of the same name.

I would also like to say something about the Stronghold of the Righteous.
It's worth reducing the damage and increasing the CD. this is too strong an ability for a tank in 3 directions Damage/Aggro/CD.

For comparison:

New Spell: Barkskin (Feral)
Learned at Level 44 with new ranks at Level 52 and 60.
Requires Bear Form, Dire Bear Form, Cat Form
The druid's skin becomes tough as bark, reducing the damage of the next 5/10/15 melee attacks by 50%. Movement speed is reduced by 20% during its duration. Lasts for 12 seconds.
(10 Minute cooldown)

Shield Wall (warrior)
Instant	30 min cooldown
Reduces the damage taken from melee attacks, ranged attacks and spells by 75% for 10 sec.
Improved Shield Wall moved from row 5 to row 6. Now reduces the cooldown of Shield Wall by 5/10 min and increases its duration by 1/2 sec - from talent

New Capstone Talent: Bulwark of the Righteous (7th Row Capstone)
Requires Shields.
Bash the target with your shield, dealing 556 to 601 Holy damage and reducing damage you take by 40% for 12 seconds.
(3 Minute Cooldown, 200 Mana Cost, 5 Yard Range, has a 43% Spell Power scaling coefficient for all ranks.).

author: Jeanierose
subject: Re: High Elf redemption spell
content_md:
Pick up the quest "Tome of Divinity" from the Paladin trainer in Goldshire.
He sends you to a trainer in the Cathedral.
He gives you the Tome of Divinity.
Open your bag, click on the Tome of Divinity: "This item begins a quest."
Talk to the Cathedral trainer (whose name I can't remember.)
He gives you a quest to find Stephanie Turner in the Trade District. (Have 10 linen cloth in your bag.)
Go back to the trainer, click, he gives you a Symbol, talk to the wounded man near the altar.
THEN go find the man you need to resurrect at Hero's Vigil.
Fight the bad guys there until you get the Script.
Return the Script to the wounded man in the Cathedral.
Talk to the trainer. You get Redemption.
Level 13, by the way. Maybe 12, I don't know. Took me forever to figure this out.

author: Eulogy
subject: The new retribution paladin rotation feels sluggish. Anyone else?
content_md:
Hey there fellow paladins   satisfied_turtle_head  ,

after trying out the new retribution paladin for several hours my suspicions prior to the patch have been confirmed:
The new rotation feels sluggish and dull.

I'm definitely not the only one that feels this way, since I've talked to many others that share this opinion more or less.

Our dedicated class designer, Lhian, stated that these changes are more along the lines of what the old Blizzard team intended, but the original devs also had a major horde bias and fairly little interest in paladins.

Could we stray away from this path and try to mitigate this issue? At the very least I'd like to propose splitting up the shared cooldown of Holy and Crusader Strike. Obviously the numbers would have to be adjusted for it to not be too strong.

Ideally I'd suggest for Holy Strike to just have a 1,5 GCD. It feels good to have something spammable.

I have to disagree from a feeling and design stand point.

Paladins are historically a archetype of character that brings people that wants to feel the fantasy of the hero. Thats done by giving them high impact skills with great effects you cannot spam.

You are a dude with a giant twohanded weapon smiting your enemies.

GDC Striking paladins were a travesty, thats something you do to classes you want to give the feeling of attacking really fast and being agile: Monks, rogues, etc...

Not saying things cannot get changed or give paladins more buttons to press in between hits (Enhancement shaman has a 8cd skill and a 9cd skill and still with shocks in between you don't feel you aren't pressing buttons that much) but not spammeable attacks.

content_md:
Maybe my English is really bad, but I'll try to tell my vision of the paladin. Many say that this is vanilla + and there is no need to use talents and skills of other add-ons, including Wotlk. However, Blizzard showed in SoD that it is possible to change the paladin's ret for the better.
 1. CD for CS and HS should be different, and it would be good to make an exorcism instead of HS, which will work on everyone (like in SoD).
 2. Following the example of SoD, you can make CS regenerate mana and not spend mana when using it, you could add mana regeneration like in Wotlk when using justice.
 3. It is necessary to return protection from the dispel of the seal in talents, or even get away from the system of using the seal once every 30 seconds and make, for example, the seal as a buff for 5-10 minutes. (Wotlk).
 4. Add at least some mobility to the class. For example, like in cataclysm, when using justice, the running speed increased by 3 seconds.
Now the paladin is a disabled class. The seal system was a mistake, it was introduced by Blizzard right before the start of vanilla. So if we have vanilla+ on the turtle, maybe we will make a paladin DD, and not something else.
There will simply be a paladin who will use justice, CS, exorcism and consecration. And not constant pressing on the seal, which can be dispelled and 2 hits with a common cooldown.

subject: Paladin HOLY rewok help !
content_md:
Hello, I am a main paladin holy player, I have been playing with this class for years since the classic and I also went through several expansions with this same class and specialization. I would like to express myself in a constructive way about the new paladin holy archetype that they just gave us, they want to make us heal in melee with this terrible rework design that they implemented to the class which as a veteran player I see it unfeasible and inefficient, next I will show some of my ideas about why this version of the paladin holy is unfeasible.

 1. As a melee healer I have to deal with the boses' silence mechanics which consequently decreases my efficiency as a healer.

 2. This brings me to the next point, as a melee healer I don't have enough hit to hit a raid boss and activate the mechanics of the new holy shovel system.

 3.The bonus set and armor of the paladin healer has never been benefited by the spirit stat since its main stat is Int, stamina and critical so the new set is completely unfeasible as this healer works.

Now I will mention some changes that really benefit the class:

 1. remove the [Blessed Strikes] talent since we are not going to heal to melee , if not as it has always been done efficiently at range.

 2. Bring back the [Divine Favor] talent that gives us 100% critical chance to heal which is very efficient in emergency cases to keep my tank or a raid member alive .
.
 3.Bring back the previous version of [Illumination] that for each critical heal the healing spells didn't charge you mana and therefore it was the only way to be able to keep mana during long fights.

Personally I think that the other talents are fine and don't need any changes... I think that with these changes they will bring back to life the pala holy that has been cruelly destroyed and put back together in a kind of a very bad frankenstein...(bring back the holy shock that does damage in the classic version).

Finally I would like to add something about the new holy paladin tier, this set should only give intellect and stamina, because the spirit they added is useless. My tier 3 is a thousand times more efficient than the new one. This only talking about stats, because, the design seems fantastic to me and I think it's the only thing that is useful to go to the new raid, as a healer paladin and get it for my transmog collection.
I hope they listen to our criticisms from the whole paladin community holy and can fix the class.

author: Cheruscan
subject: Incentivice Utility Spells for Rets
content_md:
Hello fellow Light enjoyers and anyone interested, since the patch hit I have observed many opinions about the new paladin good and bad.

Regarding the bad, SP Ret has been severely kneecaped with the nerfing of key items and Hybrid suffers as a consequence (still ok just feels like a novelty rather than a choice to have SP on our equipment)

Most newer Ret pallies were already drawn towards AP since pre raid gearing is quite one sided for us, except for the T0.5 set but that requires gold and luck with the drops (ie time). This results in many Rets suffering from a condition I like to call „warrior brain“ they simply forget that they play a hybrid class and refuse/forget to use utility abilities like BoP/BoS/BoF or Cleanse.

Furthermore there have been complaints about our rotation being to simple atm, which isnt unwarranted since we press 4 buttons, 2 of which are on the same CD. Consecration isnt used by AP ladins outside of trash and even there it eats our mana away very rapidly, Hybrids (which often rely on WoC) therefor use Rank 1 but this still means a heavy strain on mana if you want to keep the uptime 100%

I propose a simple solution, add a new talent to the 1st row of prot tree that goes as follows

„Your Flash of Light/HoS/HoP/HoF give you *buff1* your next 2 crusader strike/consecration cost 25/50/75% less mana, lasts 7secs. Your Cleanse gives you 2 stacks of *buff2* your next autoattack is empowered with 3pt holystrike, lasts 30secs stacks up to 10 times.“

Maybe like this as a 3 pointer or maybe a bit different as 5 pointer.

This would incentivice using utility spells in our rotation, so more buttons to press, also it makes consecration cheaper to use, which helps SP/Hybrid rets. Opens up more plays for our melee healers  aswell and makes the mana drain of cleanse a bit easier to manage.

author: Vidnar
subject: The many pros and cons of new Paladin and how to fix them.
content_md:
The long awaited class changes finally dropped, for our favorite armor clad bringers of salvation, freedom and retribution and hings look... Wierd.
For those who just want tldr: class changes for paladins feel like someone had an idea how to fix them but someone else forced their crippling for "balance reasons". Like half cooked stew or half baked bread.

Seals and Judgements

The basic mechanic that have seen a bit of tuning for 3 most popular seals (command, wisdom, rigthnouess) but the rest were either ignored (Justice, Light) or just thrown into trash (Crusader).
Command finally got that AP/SP corelation so you wont feel like you shaft yourself going for either or both.
Rigthnouess for spelladin got its talent finally working and is worth taking! Hurray!
Wisdom got its proc chance improved to 100% and buffed so it itsnt just some measly investment, requiring 10 sec to make even.
Melee skills such as Holy Strike and Crusader Strike proc Judgements on the target.
Now for Crusader, Justice, Light and Wisdom.
In terms of damage, they are worthles and im utility not far behind.
Wisdom requires you to stand there and hit the target for half a minute straight to go from zero to full mana but in the meantime you cant atack or use skills as they dont proc seals (more on that later). Who wants to sit in the raid for that long and fall behind on their contribution to killing a boss? Forget about PvP, that's like a death sentence. During leveling it might be okay if you get only one mob on yourself. Dungs will be a slog as mobs will die too fast to even bother, maybe on a boss?
Light is just... Dull. Triggering doesnt effect the group to justify its low health return and now it will be just easier to pop SoW and use flash or two.
Justice lost all its usefulness with giving paladin a baseling taunt (and thank God for that, the talent was awful to use), relegating it to a skill you learn and never use.
Crusader... Oh boy. The previous iteration of it forcing procs sounded good on paper but then every single weapon proc has been nerfed, not only reducing viability of that seal but also hitting with a nerf bat other classes such as shamans and warriors. And now we are back to increasing holy damage target takes with judgement (which you will never use, mana issues for later) or seal that decreases your damage dealt by 60% and doesnt even give you anything substential in return.

Crusader Strike, Holy Strike and holy sh*t

At long last paladin had a chance to something ressembling a rotation. HS doing moderate damage and always having a buff depending on the spec, CS giving you ramping up buffs to boost your melee and casting haste, meler strikes finally refreshing judgements on target, removing ungodly and frankly retarded inconsistent damage of HS ranging from nuke to a wet noodle was a good call.
What went wrong?
The only reason you use HS is to refresh a buff if you have one, your melee strikes dont proc your seals and on top of that they have shared CD. Why. Just why? Cause of WF Totem? That's like a percentage of a percentage of a game. So you just stand there and auto atack like its 1.12 again.
Also, who in the world thought that forcing paladin into melee healer was a good idea, without giving them any kind of defensives against cleave, silences and stuns just didnt thought it trough. And the removal of holy shock damage component? Great even less more buttons to press as DPS, cause that's what hybrids want, less options yet still being hybrid taxed aka paying for nothing.

Itemization, oh how we missed you.

We got them. Finally after so long we, boys in holy plate, got our alternative tier sets, so we can finally be Saviors, Protectors and Retributors!
But holy crap have they butchered them. Holy is mostly okay, being simple int, hsp, stam with a bit of crit.
Prot got something better than Kharazan 10man set so they wont feel like half of the gear they need to steal from warriors.
But retribution? Why in the hell does it have stats like spirit or haste? We already buff our haste with new CS and spirit doesnt scale with anything so why is there? You have less mana and hp in full T2 ret than in its holy variant by almost 1k of mana and hp.

...but path to Redemption is always there.

All the ranting and pointing to flaws is done, now we can start thinking about how to fix that new mess. Give your suggestions, ideas, maybe new info that came out i didnt seen. We are all here to make it work, so in spirit of jolly cooperation, lets get to it, starting with baseline.

Seals, as our bread and butter should not be wasted when you cast judgement OR make their cost reasonable to promote their changing depending on the situation. Maybe add some bonuses to encourage that?

Crusader should be our go to cleave seal. Its damage reduction could be capped at 30% but have us hit two more targets with our atacks (auto, CS, HS). Maybe let Ret cut down on damage penalty as capstone? Have Holy deal, well, Holy damage?

Justice could be CC seal as its effect has chance to stun. Maybe let it work as innterupt if you judge the target with it? Improve running speed while its on? Heck, or let it keep enemy at normal speed like in later expansions.

Light and Wisdom as utility seals in concept are great! You smack someone and benefit your party that way. Make them have some scalability so they dont fall off in later parts of the game. Or maybe have it work on whole group, leaning that way more into support aspect.

And most importantly ALL the seals should have some form damage component. SP, AP, Hybrid, anything.

Holy and Crusader Strike should be separate CDs, simple as that. And more importantly, let melee skills proc seals. As it stands there is no reason for them to not be on separate CDs.

Now, to fix the glaring issue of paladins ranged options (we are the only class in game that Has a problem like this and nothing to compensate) i suggest to give us a new ability akin to flame shock called Righteous Brand.
Simple x sec CD ability for short range that deals damage and puts a dot on the target. And as a Holy, let Holy shock be an upgrade, giving back the shockadin option back, ret much needed ranged option in pvp and tanks a ranged pull.
Other suggestions would be to make excorcism more worth it to use, maybe have its effectivness be that of 50% on other targets?
Hammer of Wrath having an option to be turned instant?
At least that's it for now. Lets see what you come up with.
Deus Vult!

author: Harkonnan
subject: Re: The many pros and cons of new Paladin and how to fix them.
content_md:
First off, a great thank you to the dev's for putting such hard work and dedication into this server, it really shows!

And thank you for the write-up Vidnar, I agree with most of your points, even if the reasoning in my part is a bit different. also enjoy your videos, keep both of these activities going!

for my part, I feel that the reason that HS and CS share a CD is to limit top end damage. I don't play a pally on this server at level cap yet raiding, So I can't comment on how a raiding pally is affected.

But from a leveling perspective, Mana is our top issue. In spite of you saying that HS is not worth using, I use it by default when leveling. Why? because it allows me a few extra mobs in-between drinks. I still drink allot. too much.

I think that your idea to simply make judgement not consume seals would go a long ways towards that. It reminds me that even when WoW made that change, they still added a talent that gave a ret pally back 25% of their mana on each judgement because they were such mana hogs. We need more mana options, period.

I would LOVE your idea of a baseline skill like righteous brand. I support giving holy deep tree skills to buff it too. I do think however, that having both CS and HS as individually useable skills, AND having RB as a new skill in our rotation, would push our damage into the insane levels, and I'd hate to see them have to nerf our damage from either one to compensate.

If you had a choice, which one would you choose? separation of CS/HS, or a new skill like your RB mentioned above? Me I'd prefer RB. it sounds cool, We REALLY need a ranged pulling skill. Even Warriors with their amazing Charge ability can use bows/guns. rogues who stealth everywhere have throwing from level one. We are the only class that cannot control anything from range.

I understand devs! I get it. You want the Pally to have a melee oriented vibe and feel. But the warrior is 100% melee! and they still have a ranged pulling ability that at least does some damage. They key here is to not make that ability something that defines the class. Just make it a baseline ability, and have a talent in each tree that affects it.

Another options is to definitely give us a wrath style exorcism. Make the damage baseline, and make it a guaranteed crit for undead and demons. Adjust the damage to compensate for balance, and give Ret a talent that reduces it's CD by 5 seconds.

Last few points for the dev's:

 1) Ret's capstone, Repentance, is just not a well developed skill. Even if the new changes give it good damage, it's still only useful in raids or against bosses that are immune to sleep. It's literally the ONLY capstone in the game that is so limited. It only sleeps certain mob types, and it only damages mobs that are immune to sleep. PLEASE PLEASE just get rid of it and replace it with something else.
I've given plenty of ideas in previous threads, I'll just summarize here. a dash ability (very fast one ons a 3s CD or somthng), adding cleave to our SoC, DIVINE STORM BABY!, It's not just about Repentance being clunky and weird feeling, It's about the sheer fact that the skill itself does not match the "Retribution" concept, I haven't seen a single person that likes it, even with the changes, But I see plenty of pallys that hate it with a passion.

 2) last point about CS/HS: I think that the attempt to make both viable in each tree is admirable, but in the end it feels like overcomplicating things for the pure sake of overcomplication. I think that making CS a more ret thing and HS a more prot thing should really be the  focus. LIke change the Prot talent Righteous Strikes to combine both bonuses to HS.
from the perspective of Ret, eliminate HS as a "buff" and instead of CS increasing speed even more, give CS a buff that increases holy damage. It already has a speed increase, and having more really makes speed on gear less desirable for pallies. it's better to buff Holy damage, and give more to the class feel of "hit once, hit hard". You can either make it a debuff on the mob so it takes more holy (party buff), or buff the paladin only to make it more realisitic and not OP.

topic_title: The many pros and cons of new Paladin and how to fix them.

author: Harkonnan
subject: Re: The many pros and cons of new Paladin and how to fix them.
content_md:
Here's another thought:

Get rid of HS. New CS:  base form, X weapon damage + Y holy damage. reduce mana cost by 20%. applies Zeal, which increases Holy damage and healing by 10%

 - Ret talent Crusading Strikes gives: 10% of mana pool returned every CS, and 2/4/6% extra attack speed per stack of Zeal. 3 ranks.
 - New Ret talent (same tier as Crusading Strikes) : Holy Might: Using judgement applies holy might buff, increasing Strength by 10/20%. 2 ranks.
 - This way Ret has pretty much the same stuff, but it keeps ret specific CS buffs, and helps with the mana issues, and doesn't cost any more talent points then it already does.

 - Prot talent Righteous Strikes: Zeal increases Threat and Holy damage of CS by 2/4/6/8/10% per stack, and block by 2% per stack. as long as a zeal stack is up, provides Safe Harbor, increasing Armor and all the Paladins resistances by 10%
 - This turns CS into a tanking powerhouse. Keeps most of the benefits of the original skill, but also makes up for the loss of attack speed with a more tank-oriented bonus.

 - Holy talent Blessed Strikes: CS has a 20/40/60/80/100% chance of resetting Holy Shock CD, and Zeal increases healing from Holy shock and Righteous Brand by 5/10/15/20/25% per stack.
 - This makes CS and Zeal more applicable for Holy spec, and buffs Rb making it more healing oriented.

The I would implement Righteous Brand and just have it as a base skill that is similar to Moonfire: a small amount of damage on hit and a decent Holy damage DoT. If you want it to be buffed by a healing spec, you could always do something like add to the talent Sanctity Aura: Also allows RB to be cast on a Friendly target and heal for the same amount.

There ya go. HS/CS debacle done with. CS is now a basic skill that is buffed individually by each spec in ways that make sense, and we have a ranged talent that makes up for the loss of HS. Actually its even better then having HS, since it's something we'll use on CD. Actually, now that I think about it, it shouldn't have a CD. Ret/prot won't be spamming it because of Mana issues, but it is now an amazing tool for Holy to use in their rotation.

Lastly, I really think A "Divine Storm" should be our replacement for Ret. We need something to replace repentance, It allows for better cleave (we can't sustain Consecrate with our mana pools). Make it X% weapon damage as Holy, and also provide a slow debuff for 3 seconds, on an 8s CD. hits up to 4 targets.

author: Khagrim
subject: New Vengeance talent as an example of bad design
content_md:
One of the main draws of Vanilla WoW is that hybrid classes are exactly that - hybrid. Paladin's base kit allowed them to fill any role in a leveling dungeon group just by swapping some gear. Talent specialization was a cherry on top and enhanced your main playstyle. But you were still able to heal or even tank most pre 50 dungeons as a Retribution paladin. I know because I've done it both on TWoW an Era. One could argue that due to Vengeance talent deep Retribution could produce threat comparable or sometimes better than Improved Righteous Fury.

And now we come to the problem with the paladin rework. Vengeance now has a built-in threat reduction. And ret absolutely needed threat reduction! But by baking it into Vengeance the hybrid potential of the class is diminished. Which brings the design closer to the later iterations of WoW and further from Vanilla. So if you are leveling as Ret you can't just put on a shield and fill a tank role. Thus limiting options and making tank shortage worse.

I understand it's not a problem at endgame where most people have respec devices, but as a leveling and HC enthusiast I feel that it is a problem worth looking into.

One possible solution would be to add an additional condition that threat reduction only works while wearing a 2h weapon. Similar to Warrior's Defensive Tactics that increases threat in battle and berserker stances but only if wearing a shield.

subject: Re: Give paladins seal twist
content_md:
Love it or hate it, classic is full of janky mechanics that are considered bug to some while for others favorite playstile.
Seal twisting, totemtwisting, hs queing, spellbatching for shatters on mage, melee weaving, wand weaving etc.

There are multiple options to dealing with it. Blizzard (and turtle in some cases) chose the boring but save option. Remove those mechanics and just add a simple dps button like crusader strike back in instead.

You can instead also embrace some of the concepts players have discovered.

If you give paladins a talent that lets seals linger for 1-x seconds after they recast a new seal, you have sealtwisting instantly retained as a mechanic players can properly tracked in their interface. No addon needed.

Blizzard included it in Classic for historical purposes, because they removed batching, which would have otherwise made seal twisting impossible, but it is 100% a bug. Classic was intended to be an archive that allowed players to play the game as it was back in the day.

Seal twisting was entirely a bug that stemmed from the way spell batching worked, in the same way that two warriors could charge each other, or two mages could polymorph each other. It was not intended gameplay by the original vanilla devs at all.

As an aside, anything that requires precise timing on a server where people could have upward of 200ms ping that may vary from moment to moment, and does not have spell queuing is 100% bad game design. The only way I would approve of seal twisting is in the form of a mechanic that actively allows you to have two seals up for a short period of time, removing the requirement to effectively play a rhythm game at 200ms ping. An example of this would be the way SoD handled it, by including a set bonus on ret tier gear that allowed them to maintain a second seal for 6 seconds after casting a new seal:

> T1 6pc: Your Seal of Command, Seal of Righteousness, and Seal of Martyrdom now persist for 6 seconds after you cast another Seal, or until you cast a third Seal. Your Judgements can now trigger multiple Seals if active.

This would also give you breathing room to be able to use other abilities such as strikes and consecration

author: Reploidrocsa
subject: Re: Which profession as a future Holy Paladin
content_md:
Depends a lot on what your goals are.

 5 man and casual content and no plans on alts? Mining with some profesion that uses minerals (blacksmithing, jewelcrafting or engineering). This gives you a source of materials and can craft some items better than dungeon drops.

Endgame raiding? Consumable crafting professions. Alchemy and herbalism are a safe pick, since you'll use potions and elixirs on a daily basis.

PvP? Engineering with mining. Engineering gives you extra tools and CC consumables. Mining again to supply with materials.

You're thinking on staying here playing regularly for years and do some serious raiding? Enchanting will take a lot of time investment, but once you get the rare recipes you can semi afk in a capital whispering anyone needing a enchant you have "pssst, i can enchant what you're looking for if you bring me the mats and some tip". Very low gold income but almost efortless once you got the recipes. Pair it with jewelcrafting specialized in gemology to enchant others people jewerly for the same deal as enchants. Perfect if you can have the client open all day semi afk.
Remember that without mining you'll have to level up an alt or buy the materials from the AH

Planning on leveling alts? Get double crafting profession on your main. Engineering is very useful in both pve and pvp (mostly on pvp) and another profesion of your liking. Engineering also allows you to craft dynamites which can be used for ranged pulls if you ever need to do so. For now, most important materials you might need can get gathered in the world, so you can have a dedicated miner/herbalist for your daily needs while your main enjoys more crafting stuff

author: Manletow
subject: So... they nerfed Holy Strike.
content_md:
My hate thread about (old) Holy Strike was a massive viral hit with countless replies and nearly 9000 views.

They massively nerfed this fan favorite ability and yet I must admit I am surprised/impressed that there has been hardly any whining whatsoever from Paladin players.

However, I suppose it was a 'favorite' simply because of how overpowered the damage was -- not because it was fun/interesting to use.

By contrast; Shaman Mains have been crying endlessly ever since CC2 was released.
This is especially ironic given that Shaman was provided with a brand new (fucking sweet) melee attack that hits for at least 700 damage in crappy blue gear.

So is the new/improved Crusader Strike really so good that it's a satisfying replacement for Holy Strike?

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: So... they nerfed Holy Strike.
content_md:
What you have to understand is that holy strike under ideal scenarios (raidbuffed bis gear) "only" ever critted for 3. 5k ish maximum. And that is already factoring in the 2x 15% dmg increase from the doubledipping vengeance. This while replacing an auto attack that would itself deal about 1.5k ish damage under those circumstances

Realistically you would hit only for about 2.5k in good gear on a BG. Any hit bigger than this was due to a bug when it comes to how berserking (and vengeance) is applied to holy strike.

It first applies the damage bonus to the white hit, and then again to the holy strike ability. So with berserking and vengeance you had a whopping
+110% damage bonus. With ampliers like this, almost any ability would have hit hard.

Considering the old holy strike would only give +130ish holy damage and replace an auto attack aside from armor pen and this buggy amplification, the new holy strike/or the instead casted new crusader strike is strictly better than the old one except with this one bug being considered.
Thats for the PvE play

When it comes to pvp aside from the bug, the new crusader strike in conjunction with an auto attack is about equal in value to the old holy strike against any target with 45% or less armor (e.g. everyone that isnt bear)
So ye for the most part, this is a buff to paladin. And all it cost us was an instant ability without cd that would regularly hit for less than 100dmg.

But turns out, pvpers only tend to complain about the flavor of the month oneshot

author: Imonobor
subject: Removing shockadins was a mistake
content_md:
In general, outright removing ANY playstyle or build that some players enjoy is not good design. Sure, it might have been overpowered in some cases, but by outright removing the ability to use Holy Shock offensively, you ruined the playstyle for each and every player that had this build, and of everyone who wanted to try it.
Shockadins were unique in that they were an offensive healer, and other classes can not replicate such functionality easily. So in my opinion, removing this build was a mistake, because you remove a unique playstyle.

My suggestion is to return the ability for Holy Shock to be cast as a damaging spell on enemies to the baseline spell, however, remove it if the paladin has one or more talent points into divine favor:

Divine Favor: "Holy Shock critical strike chance is increased by 6/12/18/24/30%, but Holy Shock can no longer target enemies."

This gives players choice whether to specialize into pure healer for stronger shocks, or keep the damaging option, but not crit as often - which is the main complaint about shockadins - their crit burst.
The amount of damage on the damaging component could also be balanced accordingly, so it's not overpowered, it doesn't have to be the same as the healing component, or even have the same SP scaling.

It is way better to balance something that players enjoy and keep it in the game, rather than removing it outright.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: What a ret pal rotation for leveling?
content_md:
Judge wisdom if stuff takes more than 5-6 swings to kill. Otherwise dont use a debuff judgement, keep command up while swinging and click either crusader strike for fast killspeed or holy strike if you wanna conserve more mana while killing.

Do not use hammer of wrath if you wanna keep chainkilling. It costs too much mana

Buff yourself with either wisdom or might. Kings is only worth while levelling if you have good gear

Make sure to wear a SLOW weapon (anything faster than 3.0 you should only consider if its a big weapon upgrade as both crusader strike & soc heavily benefit from slow weapons)

Ifyou cant decide between two weapons try them both. So you get a feel for it

author: Siltrim
subject: Feedback on Ret Playstyle
content_md:
Hey

I want to give my Feedback on Ret Paladin:

First of all, this post does not care about any numbers. Numbers can be tuned. I do not excatly know why, but playing Ret is not so much fun atm/anymore. My guesses when I think about it are the following:
Youre only looking on timers to not fuck stuff up.
- You need to watch a swing timer, for Judging/reapplying the Seal

- You’re constatly on a hastle to keep the CS stacks up. Its just so bad when they fel off between groups. Remember: 18 seconds and 3 gcd to build them up.

- HS is another timer to keep up for the buff
To add on the Timers, the Rotation itself feels empty – espacially outside naxx. In Naxx you got a usable Exo now and thats fun to use, but outside youre just looking on timers.

I was playing a lot of Enh sham too since patch and boy is it fun. Simple mechanic – Stormstrike buffs your next Lightning Strike and earthshock. So a Prio list and not a fixed rota. Handling diff shields lets you actively decide between mana and dps at all time, throwing totems in there…. Its fun.

Why do I bring up the sham? With the downtime after Judgement and CS or HS, Ret Pala reminds a lot of Enh Sham b4 CC2 (the dead time, not the numbers) – but with additional timers you have to check every second. xD

My Suggestions would be, cut off some timers and add other usable stuff in the toolkit.
- I know, you dont want us to have a good aoe for 0 mana, so consec prob isnt the button

- Exo outside undead/demon would loose vanilla charm

- But we still have a completly useless button: Hammer of Wrath. Maybe a complete overhaul. Ive done a suggestion for it in discord and copy it to the end of this

- The changes with SoC are cool, it feels nice to press.

- HS maybe feels good, when it does not hit like a wet noodle – you only press it for another timer.

- CS itself is cool and I like the idea of getting stronger with each hit. Very paladin like. But if it uses a timer, it should last longer.
Here an idea, to replace a timer HS for Example:
With one of the attacks you could build stacks that last and dont reset after X seconds. Each stack buffs you in some way (paladin like). After X amount of stacks, you get an empowered version if the attack that has stacked it and the stacks get deleted.

I hope it gets read
cheers

Hammer of Wrath suggestion:
It could be just a Range Weapon attack with X% of Wep Damage on a 30 sec to 1 min CD. Without any restriction on how much HP the NPC has left.

This would massivly help Tanks to Pull stuff and gives Rets an option to do anything in Range (except Exo, but thats just undead). With the condition as Weapon attack, you can make sure it will not get too strong with SP as a tank. And a long CD should help with any PvP issues

author: Aalena
subject: Re: Feedback on Ret Playstyle
content_md:
I've been tempted to write my own feedback on the changes for the class overall, but my biggest annoyance at the moment is that I don't like how Crusader Strike and Holy Strike works, especially as they share cooldown. While one button is useful for one spec, the other just ends up being a chore you have to manage. Yes, as Ret, it's a lot better than spamming the Crusader Strike every second for Windfury buff, but could still be better.

For Ret: Crusader Strike is your go-to choice for damage. Also gives a nice attack speed boost! But you need to use Holy Strike purely for the strength buff (And it's a shame since using attacks to heal/restore mana to the group is something I wanna do, even as Ret).

And while not Ret in specific, still issues with them for the other two specs.
For Prot: Holy Strike for damage, some regen and the extra threat. Crusader Strike is purely for the buff. The annoying thing though is that unlike Ret with HS, this has to be used 3 times for full effect and if that drops off... Well, have fun getting your stacks back.

Overall, I feel like we could get rid of one of the buttons, add some of their functions to Judgement, and use the CS/HS Talents on each tree to instead buff the one remaining and Judgement.
content_html:
I've been tempted to write my own feedback on the changes for the class overall, but my biggest annoyance at the moment is that I don't like how Crusader Strike and Holy Strike works, especially as they share cooldown. While one button is useful for one spec, the other just ends up being a chore you have to manage. Yes, as Ret, it's a lot better than spamming the Crusader Strike every second for Windfury buff, but could still be better.

For Ret: Crusader Strike is your go-to choice for damage. Also gives a nice attack speed boost! But you need to use Holy Strike purely for the strength buff (And it's a shame since using attacks to heal/restore mana to the group is something I wanna do, even as Ret).

And while not Ret in specific, still issues with them for the other two specs.
For Prot: Holy Strike for damage, some regen and the extra threat. Crusader Strike is purely for the buff. The annoying thing though is that unlike Ret with HS, this has to be used 3 times for full effect and if that drops off... Well, have fun getting your stacks back.

For Holy: I don't have much experience with it but I never much bother Crusader Strike to refresh Holy Shock, so it's a dead ability on my end and just use Holy Strike.

Overall, I feel like we could get rid of one of the buttons, add some of their functions to Judgement, and use the CS/HS Talents on each tree to instead buff the one remaining and Judgement.

author: Papum69
subject: (Updated 8.0) Possible improvments to the current Paladin Talent trees.
content_md:
With the current changes to all paladins the Holy paladins can now be in the heat of battle for extra benefits, yet to hit with melee and spells in high end pve without much hit rating is not that good for an Holy paladin wich lacks severly in that department. Also some other ideias for the other paladin trees.

 **Suggestions:**

 **1 -** Now that '***Holy Shock***' has been changed to only heal, leaving only '***Holy Strike***', '***Crusader Strike***' and normal seal Judgement's/melee swings to do holy damage it is not probably worth having '***Sanctity Aura***' in the holy tree anymore for just an +10% holy damage increase. Instead move it back to the Retribution paladin tree (as its more beneficial there for the sake of spending less unnecesary or forced [if using the 'Seal of Crusader' talent point] talent point and by so having more to spent on chosen usefull ones) merged into the '***Improved Retribution Aura***' stating 'Increase the damage done by your 'Retribution Aura' by 15%/30% and increases Holy damage done by party members within 30 yards by 5%/10%.'.
And in place of '***Sanctity Aura***' create an new 1 point talent called '***Sanctity***' that states 'increase your weapons skill with one handed weapons by 2 and increase your chance to hit with spells by 2% also extends the range of you Holy Strike and Crusader Strike to 8 yards'.
This will help Holy paladins with hit chance for both melee and spells and not be in the middle of all the melee's yet also not be in the back with all the casters, instead create an new middle zone for them so they have an increased reach to those that are in the back or further away as well as those in melee range.

 **2-** Add to the '***Benediction***' talent the ability to reduces the chance your Seal spells will be dispelled by an additional 18%/36%/54%/72%/90%.

 **3-** Add to the '***Improved Blessings***' talent the ability to reduces the chance your Blessing spells will be dispelled by an additional 2%/4%/6%/8%/10%.

 **4-** Make '***Blessing of Kings***' baseline for all paladins.
This way Holy paladins will have more talent points to spend elsewhere instead of having to dump a lot on useless points just to get to one talent, also all other paladins will have easy access to it aswell.
Now whit the removal of the '***Blessing of Kings***' talent there remains an 1 point talent void in the Retribution tree for a new talent at tier 3.
It could be an talent to help out the Retribution and/or Protection paladin in what they still lack/needs, possibly a gap closer from an new 1 point talent called '***Crusade***' that extends from the '***Pursuit of Justice***' talent and is an activated ability wich multiplies the speed % amount of '***Pursuit of Justice***' temporarily by 400% = 40% speed from the normal 8% (can be used while mounted and won't dismount you) for 4 sec. with an 30 sec. cd.
It can have an mechanism wich prevents it to be used as an direct escape tool wich is that when activated it will mark an target within 25 yards for 3/4 sec., and the paladin will only benefit from the extra movement enhanced speed (the normal 8% while remain active regardless for if you decide to run away from the marked target during the duration of '***Crusade***') if moving towards that target.

 **5-** Add to the '***Seal of Justice***''s judgement the ability to reduce the movement speed bonus of the target to 0.

 **6-** Add to the '***Seal of Command***''s judgement the ability to do the extra damage to targets that are immune to stun or incapicitation aswell.
Helps making this seal a bit more viable in pve raid encounters aswell.

 **87-** Change '***Precision***' & '***Guardian's Favor***' to tier 1 of the Protection paladin tree in exchange of '***Improved Devotion Aura***' going to tier 2 of the same tree.
This will give accessability to some more much needed hit rating to the now changed Holy Paladin and also Retribution paladin wich now struggles to get to that talent as it previously did not.

 **8-** Make '***Improved Devotion Aura***' more appellative by changing it into '***Improved Defensive Auras***' wich now states 'Increases the armor bonus of your 'Devotion Aura' and the resistance bonuses of all your resistance auras by [20%/40%/60%/80%/100%].'.

 **9-** '***Hand of Reckoning***' ability seems more like 8 yards than what the tootltips describes it, wich is 10 yards.

 **10-** Extende the normal '***Blessings of X***' from 10 to 30 min. and greater blessings to 1 hour.
Helps in a way to conserve mana and also gives a longer period of time while in an dungeon/raid the need to re-bless and to other players that you bless while pve'ing in the world a longer benefit from the blessings while they go there own way, like the buff's other classes give others while pve'ing in the world.

 **11-** Add an interrupt (and closing for an couple of sec that school of magic) with an reasonable low cd wich is only useable in close combate like what was added in retail in WotLK the ability 'Rebuke' .
This helps the paladin not to be so sujectable to mana drain till being oom in an couple of seconds and/or being cc'd till death (paladins may have an divine intervention to break out o it yet you deal less 50% damage while in it and it has an 5 min cd so while it comes back the paladin is almost an sitting duck).
One could argue that the paladin has 'Hammer of Justice' yet that has an 1 min. cd and an simple usage of an trinket can remove it, one could also say an retribution paladin can also have repentance and that would be true but the same as above it is on an 1 min. cd.
So in resume a paladin can have 2x 1 min. interrupts against and trinket removal and taking the other cc one till it wears off and if the paladin was not able to finish the target off (because the paladin now has mainly to build up it's steady damage for an couple of seconds) so after that the opponent just cc's the paladin and/or oom's him till death.

author: Sylveria
subject: Re: Paladin design concept
content_md:
I haven't looked into everything yet, but I'd like to correct you on something:

> Historically, Crusader Strike was a Retribution talent and I think that having 2 instant strike spell this early in leveling is too much.

That's historically wrong, since in the Alpha version of WoW (0.5.3) there were no talent trees at all and Crusader Strike/Holy Strike were available to every paladin (They existed back then already). That was before the seal system has been introduced by Blizzard to replace those 2 Strikes.
Regarding the Feel to the game i also say otherwise, cuz i enjoyed it to have more than 2 ACTIVE abilities (for combat spefically) to press.
What does the paladin currently has? Crusader Strike, Holy Strike Judgement, at 20 Consecration and much later Hammer of Wrath, an execute i personally rarely use.
I count Exorcism and Holy wrath only half, because of their use against specific enemies. (So i can KINDA agree to your change to Exorcism, but to me it kinda feels off.. Exorcism useable on all Targets feels WotLK, which i never liked.)
I personally do not count the seals, cuz you wouldn't count the totems for the shaman either, would you? Regarding active combat abilities the Paladins has the LEAST.

i might edit this post later or write another entry after i finished reading. Just wanted to write right now, before i forget my thoughts. ^^

Edit: Here btw. the Strike abilities from the 0.5.3 Client

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/XfQC23p.png)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/fh8dQyJ.png)

Edit #2:

Regarding the "Leveling/Questing too easy".

I play A LOT of paladin (i have 3 paladins on 60 (1holy,1prot,1ret) another prot on 47, another holy on 30 and another prot on 26. I'm no crack regarding numbers, i only go with the flow and the feel of the class. Gameplaywise the only thing that is bothering me is the shared cooldown of Crusader Strike/Holy Strike. Everything else seems a thing regarding numbers that need to be tuned down a little.
Other than that, i'm actually quite satisfied with the Paladin in Questing/Leveling Content.

I don't know why, but since CC2 i actually have LESS Problems with mana as a Retribution Pally. The Prot Paladins has now more mana issues than before, but the Shield specilization was REALLY strong before, causing the Prot paladin to almost never go oom. Now I have to utilize Seal of Wisdom a lot more and the little hp/mp regeneration from Holy Strike helps me with that quite a bit to get back on my feet, if i got hit with several mana burns. So i personally don't see much need of change there.

I won't cover everything now since it would take me way too much time and effort and.. as i mentioned before: I'm no crack regarding the numbers/the calculations etc.
But to me it overall seems like an ABSURD amount of buffs to the paladin. I mean i love the paladin class. I really do, but even to me it seems like the paladin would be WAY overtuned, if your changes WOULD be applied.

One thing in specific i wanna mention: the Retribution-Dual-Wield.. My only answer is just.. No.. Please god no.
I can't really tell you the "why" but it just feels VERY WRONG.

author: Zulnam
subject: Re: Paladin design concept
content_md:
I mean, if you want to talk "removal of playstyle", look no further than Holy Shock.

The great irony is that, if holy shock would've been kept as it was but moved to 21 slot talent, 21/0/30 would have been a prime contender to an S tier ret paladin and 21/30/0 could have been a contender to a prime prot paladin.

But as it stands, 31-point prot is okish and 31-point ret is a meme with an inside joke (that inside joke being the little extra damage you do during a boss). Not to mention that for a full ret build you would actually need 32 points, cause balance is hard.

It's a hard nuance to notice, since Zeal covers up for most of the dps shortages ret paladin ever had (x% faster attack does translate into x% more damage), but it does so at the expense of the vanilla paladin identity. i would rather have og holy shock at 21 and no zeal, even if it meant a lower position in dps charts (god forbid the dps classes outperform a hybrid).

but that would mean more controlled damage in pvp, and then that croud would moan. all 12 of them. so damned if you do, damned if you don't.

author: Turbosaxophonic
subject: Re: Paladin design concept
content_md:
> **Sylveria wrote: Fri Dec 27, 2024 10:29 pm**
> "Instant gratification"...?
>
>  Wanna talk about how much instant gratification other classes have?

I’d love to, since there isn’t much to go around for most classes until at least level 20. Warriors don’t get anything as impactful and rotation-shaping as Cleave or Mortal Strike/Bloodthirst until 20 and 40 respectively (by the way, I think lowering Slam from 30 to 14 is a mistake too), Mages don’t get proper AoE kiting until 20 with Blink and Blizzard, and Rogues don't have the entire Poison system until 20.

Crusader Strike is as defining to a playstyle as those abilities are, and 10-19 isn’t about introducing fleshed-out DPS rotations to the hybrids (with the possible exception of Shaman, but they were meant to be the offensive counterpart to Paladin's defense and even then it's a basic caster). 1-10 introduces the basic foundation of what your class does and what its roles are, while 12-18 fleshes out your utility and reinforces those roles. You’re *supposed* to feel like something important is missing during those early levels to give players a motivation beyond new places and bigger numbers to keep leveling, and to make the moment of filling those mechanical gaps that much sweeter.

> If it's for you guys, you'd propably roll back Paladin back to vanilla with only 1 button every 10seconds. :P

My man, I already said Holy Strike is fine and I even welcome it. I’m not calling for Crusader Strike to be removed, just for raising the required level (and maybe another eventual rework, Zeal stacks encourage a bizarre momentum that doesn’t feel fitting for the class, but that’s a lot more subjective and I don't have an obvious solution for it, I’m much more focused on the early game impact). Paladin was intended to be an accessible and simple to play class, and that goes double for the early game. They were specifically designed for new players to learn the game with a more passive playstyle and not needing to worry as much about optimal sequencing.

Raising the floor and ceiling for the class isn’t an inherent problem, but doing so this rapidly and this early muddles the pacing and learning curve of the game. Personally I feel like Crusader Strike would be best as a level 40 Retribution capstone, I’m just trying to be realistic with expectations and compromise with the suggestion of baseline at 20.

> I could count down all the active abilities other classes have to push during battle (PRE Level 20).

Honestly I’m sure you could considering there would only be like 3-5 per class

> I really like the paladin, but only 1 or 2 buttons are just not fun to play. so having 2 strikes made the paladin finally fun here on turtle.
>  And sorry, but Seals are just buffs. They are not fun. Not even in the slightest. Class Balancing aside.

The Seals are more than just buffs like the Blessings are, you’re meant to actively use them and switch between them in combination with your Judgments while timing those abilities with your auto attacks. If it isn't worth it to do so and better to just stay with Righteousness the entire time (because yes, sticking to only one Seal is indeed boring) then that’s an issue of tuning and incentive.

I’m not saying no new buttons ever, just that having only Holy Strike for the 10-19 bracket would be a happy middle regarding early game engagement and complexity for players who are still trying to learn. There's a whopping *two levels* between learning Holy Strike and Crusader Strike and those two levels go by *fast* since it's only 8-10, I think it would be better to spend more time with just Holy Strike before unlocking the second Strike. Having access to both Strikes doesn’t even give you more buttons to press since they share a cooldown, it's only convoluting a level bracket that's meant to be simple. If you’re actively using your Seals and Judgements with the rest of your kit then I honestly believe there are enough buttons to press and choices to make early on, especially for someone new to the game. Again, if there’s no motivation to play like that then that’s something that should have been addressed instead.

author: Steakhouse
subject: Small QOL Vengeance's threat reduction
content_md:
The new Vengeance talent is great, but its threat reduction is undesirable in some situations.

I'm levelling as ret. However due to the nature of levelling, and thanks to the flexibiliy of my class, I am sometimes in a situation where I equip a shield and turn Righteous Fury on to tank for group quests. This will likely also happen once I'm 60. The nature of paladin in general means that whatever your specialized role is, you'll often find yourself in situations where doing a different one, even briefly, fits the situation best.

My suggestion is to remove the threat reduction on Vengeance if Righteous Fury is on.

Old description :

> Gives you a 1/2/3% increase to all damage you deal and decreases threat you generate by 2/4/6% for 30 sec after dealing a critical strike from a weapon swing, spell, or ability. This effect stacks up to 3 times.

New description, with adjusted grammar to clarify that Righteous Fury would only negate the threat portion, not the damage portion (also clarifying that only offensive spells can proc Vengeance, not all spells such as heals) :

> Your melee and offensive spell criticals give you the Vengeance effect, which increases all damage you deal by 1/2/3% for 30 secs. Vengeance also decreases threat you generate by 2/4/6% unless Righteous Fury is active. Stacks up to 3 times.

Thanks for reading !

author: Micfild
subject: Changing Seal of the Crusader
content_md:
Its been said a few times already in the turtle wow discord how Seal of the Crusader and Seal of Justice are being considered for future changes. I have no comment about Seal of Justice but i do have a suggestion for Seal of the Crusader (SotC).

With the exception of the aforementioned Seal, all the others have similar effects to their judgements. Righteousness and Command do damage, while light and wisdom will heal or give mana respectively. So my proposal for a change to Seal of the Crusader would be put it in line with this idea.

===============================================
[Suggestion] Seal of the Crusader

Fills the Paladin with the spirit of a crusader for 30 sec, **granting X Holy Spell Power**. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time.
Unleashing this Seal's energy will judge an enemy for 10 sec, increasing Holy damage taken by up to Z.  Your melee strikes will refresh the spell's duration.  Only one Judgement per Paladin can be active at any one time.
===============================================

It would be a seal/judgement combo focused on Holy spell power. Simple and flavorful, in my opinion. The overall damage of the paladin would probably be lower for single target than when using Seal of Command or Seal of Righteousness, but can be slightly higher in some circumstances involving hordes of enemies.

In any case, i feel like it would be a more useful version of the seal than the current one.

GL HF!  smiling_turtle_head
