As for this part of your comment, I can bring a bit of clarity to the conversation.   smiling_turtle_head

SotC has three parts, the attack speed increase, the damage reduction and the attack power bonus. We'll start with the last one.

 1 - How Attack power converts into Damage

The formula for AP to DPS is: 14 AP = 1 DPS
Since it increases damage per second and not damage outright, the speed of your weapon is the next key factor to understand how much damage you'll deal per swing.

=================================
Example 1: You have 140 AP = 10 DPS /// Weapon speed 2.0
Since your weapon has a speed of 2.0 your damage per swing will be 10 DPS x 2.0 = 20 damage ----> In this scenario, each weapon swing will deal 20 points of damage

Example 2: You have 140 AP = 10 DPS /// Weapon speed 3.0
Since your weapon has a speed of 3.0 your damage per swing will be 10 DPS x 3.0 = 30 damage ----> In this scenario, each weapon swing will deal 30 points of damage
=================================

What we can see is that slower weapons will deal more damage per attack, but will attack less times in the same amount of time as a faster weapon, meaning the damage of damage you'll output in a given amount of time (lets say 1 minute) would be the same in both cases.

 2 - How Haste (attack speed increase) increases damage output

What haste and other attack speed increases do in the game is reduce your weapon cooldown, meaning it will attack faster. It does this modification without changing the value of the base attack speed (which is used in the damage calculation we saw above). This means that the more attack speed your have, the faster you'll hit, but with the same damage per attack as before.

As a quick example, if you manage to acquire a 100% attack speed buff, your 3.0 speed weapon (which was dealing 30 damage) would still deal the same amount of damage, but it would strike every 1.5 seconds instead of 3.0. Effectively doubling your DPS.

Unfortunaly, the increase attack speed that comes with SotC doesn't seem to follow this pattern.

 3 - SotC damage reduction.

As Atreidon said:
> **Atreidon wrote: Sun Feb 02, 2025 4:39 pm**
> That unfortunately is wrong. Jotc doesnt give you hase, it instead modifies your attackspeed.

This means that SotC changes the base attack speed of your weapon, instead of giving you haste. The implication is the same as the AP example, meaning your DPS doesn't change.

=================================
Example 1: You have 140 AP = 10 DPS /// Weapon speed 3.0 /// No Seal of the Crusader
Since your weapon has a speed of 3.0 your damage per swing will be 10 DPS x 3.0 = 30 damage ----> In this scenario, each weapon swing will deal 30 points of damage every 3 seconds.

Example 2: You have 140 AP = 10 DPS /// Weapon speed 3.0 /// With Seal of the Crusader (just the attack speed part)
Since your weapon has a speed of 3.0 and SotC makes you attack 40% faster, this means that your new attack speed for that weapon is 3.0/1.4 = 2.14 . Your damage per swing will be 10 DPS x 2.14 = 21.4 damage ----> In this scenario, each weapon swing will deal 21.4 points of damage every 2.14 seconds.
=================================

This is why it looks like a damage reduction, but the actual DPS remains the same.
Also, since the base attack speed of the weapon was changed, every proc that depended on it (the weapons and effects that have proc per minute (ppm) in them, don't increase or decrease.

 4 - Final Thoughts - TLDR

 **What does the current iteration of SotC actually do?**

 **It gives you a flat amount of AP!** That's all!. No new effects or extra synergies.

====================================

I hope this has been informative! GL HF out there!   happy_turtle_head

Considering twow also did add a weapon based strike, it becomes pretty irredemable as a dps option with its current functionality.

Next, it might have been useful as an option to maximize the use of judgement of wisdom & light while retaining some semblance of a dps seal. Since both judgement of wisdom got more of his power shifted to the seal part and sor has the ability to proc it too, this incredibly small niche got even smaller.

Lastly it has some niche for things that only count hits against it. Such as spell pushback or viscidus shattering. Very very niche again.

Personally id probably change it to give straight haste instead of attackspeed(with adjusted numbers ofc), but that probably makes it just outcompete soc. Which is the one seal that has to be talented, so it should definitely be a usegul/better option.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: New here - are Ret paladins viable at endgame?
content_md:
On turtlewow any spec is an asset to a Guild if the Person piloting it is a decent player.

While warrior mage or a few other pure dps classes can outperform ret in a pure DPS sense. Retpaladin offers respectable damage, emergency tank vapabilities, dispell support and judgements for his raid.

It's less glamourous than topping dps meter, but a good ret keeps his raid moving in ways other classes can only dream of.

Having the ability to transform into a healer on the spot should the need arise (your regular healer has to step out for half an hour due to rl, the fight demanding more healers than the rest of the raid etc)  rounds off your profile.

author: excin
subject: [Tel Abim] Stop asking for WF, start demanding a Firestrike Sharpening stone.
content_md:
Firestrike adds additional magic damage to your melee strikes, typically fire.

Each proc is considered as separate spell cast, and as such, each proc will have the same chance to trigger judgement of wisdom as any other spell hit.

This procs on you Crusader strikes, Holy Strikes, Melee hits, and even seal procs. Practically doubling your Judgement of wisdom output, helping you sustain more higher rank consecrations.

On my last Nax run it procced 907 times, for comparison I only dealt a total of 437 auto attack hits.

Getting it:
The effect is present on a couple of items of different levels of gear and magic school flavors:
[[Flameskin Gloves]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81267) - Fire - lvl 23 World drop
[[Ring of Electrical Binding]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61332) - Nature - lvl 43 GC
[[Incendosaur Skin Pauldrons]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60572) - Fire - lvl 49 Hateforge
[[Incendosaur Skin Gloves]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60582) - Fire - lvl 49 Hateforge
[[Incendosaur Skin Boots]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60568) - Fire - lvl 51 Hateforge
[[Fiery Plate Gauntlets]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12631) - Fire - lvl 53 Blacksmithing
[[Storm Gauntlets]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12632) - Nature - lvl 54 Blacksmithing

All the above will be a significant stat gimp (except for the incendosaur stuff at starter gear) so go for the ring.

The better stuff would be
 - T2 Ret 3bonus set - Holy damage (which will work on all encounters but lock 3 gear slots)
 - Embergem Cuffs - Jewelcrafting cloth bracers - 4 Fire damage 13 Str 13 Stam (what I currently use)

And ultimately, from Lord Kazak
[[Blazefury Medallion]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17111) - fire

Now it being like minor WF, in the sense that you need to have it. It's Gimpish itemization and will always be locking 1-3 slots of your gear and cause a significant stat sacrifice, until you get that long queued for medallion with the mediocre stats.

 **What I suggest is Making it available through a consumable, perhaps a Sharpening stone.**

 **Since we already get +7 melee damage as a base, and a whopping 2% crit at top tier. I don't think a +2 or +4 [magic damage of your choice] sharpening stone (1.8 dps) would break the game.**

The only opposition coming to this would probably be some folks from the old realm who've gotten a Blazefury Medallion and see it as a rite of passage.

author: Jrobz
subject: Bubble Cleanup and Bulwark fix
content_md:
My $0.02

First off the new End Talent of Prot is good, but still seems very uninvolved with the spec given it's downtime. An End talent should be Spec defining. Look no further than the Warrior for how to do End Talents. I like the idea of a tanking defensive cooldown but not as an End Talent. Here's a idea on how to clean this up and hopefully add spice in a balanced way.

Bubble: There's 3. One is completely redundant - Divine Protection. Let's update that to reduce dmg by 50% for 8 seconds - that's it - only PvE usable - shield equipped and under RF (aka tanking). Also, let's increase the 60 seconds shared bubble CD to 10 or 15 minutes. I think the Pally Bubble can be taken town a few pegs. This gives all 3 bubbles a  useful place.

Bulwark: Reduce the Cooldown to 4s and remove the defensive element (that is handled by Divine Protection). Change the effect to consume a Holy Shield stack (and cost 0 mana) to shield bash the target for Holy Damage = X% of SBV + Y% of HOLY SP. This gives the paladin a way to consume unspent Holy Shield stacks and adds a neat element to gameplay. It scales up with SP and SBV, and gives the Paladin a way to use their mainstay ability (Holy Shield) in a more generalized way.

This would be that spec defining ability that weaves nicely in with the Seal and Zeal systems.

author: Sylveria
subject: Re: New paladin, looking for some guidance.
content_md:
Disclaimer: i Love To Play Paladin, i have 3 Paladins, but i'm No theorycrafter and dont use any Guides. I try Things Out and Take the path that Suits me the best and also feels good "To Me"! So dont expect my advise to be the best Option. ^^

 10seconds for a kill 1v1 (vs a mob of the Same Level) IS actually ok. I dont know what exactly you expect. ^^ If you have Problems with more than one mob, than you might be lacking either stamina or the Skill.

 1. I can actually only Show my own ret Talents. If it's the Most efficient one? Idk. I dont tend To use any Guides. but i went well with it.
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... AAdIFAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin?points=FAAoBAAAAAAAAAFAIAAAAAAAAAAAFoQAFKAAdIFAAAA=)
Eniugh To say: Take all 3pts in Precision (Prot Tree) as long as you're Not hit capped.
I am Hit capped with my ret so i dont need as many pts in Precision anymore.

 2. I tend to use Seal of Command as my Main Seal and usually use Crusader Strike To keep my Zeal Stacks Up and use judgment Just to use Up my Seal before it runs Out. Holy Strike becomes interesting later with the "Vengeful Strikes" Talent, that gives me another strength Boost. So as soon as i got my 3 Zeal Stacks Up, i use Holy Strike for the strength buff and Switch between both Strikes, To keep both buffs Up.
I dont rely on Consecration, since it Just Burns Up my mana.
If my mana gets Low during Fight and i know the Fight isnt over soon, i try To get my mana Up quickly with Seal of Wisdom (Not Judgment of Wisdom!). Holy Strike helps with Seal of Wisdom To regain mana Quickly.

 3. as Long as your this early in the Leveling Stage you shouldn't think too hard about what stata you build on, but later i'd say
Hit (until capped) > Crit > Str > Agi > Stam > Int

Obviously it also depends on what Kind of ret Paladin you Play, since there's also the Spelladin who instead of Seal of Command builds on Seal of Righteousness. With that one i cant Help though, but i assume they need more spellpower and Int.

author: Mcnair
subject: Re: Very new to WoW, need some guidance and a subprime loan
content_md:
Good day.
Welcome to Turtle! :)
One of the good things about WoW is that you are truly free to play the game as you see fit. While there will always be a 'meta' way to play, that tends to be rather boring and there are enough people out there doing it already. With the recent changes to paladin, your play style is definitely doable and even encouraged - if you want to be a healer that swings around with a nice 2-hander sword. There are multiple talents in the Holy talent tree that helps with yours heals if you are also actively fighting, so it might be worth for you to check these talents and aim for them.
As for professions, mining and blacksmithing is a nice pair to have as a paladin. While it might not be your cup of tea to go farming, I would recommend to spend a bit of time to level these skills up a bit more - go around just mining for copper and tin (definitely doable at your level) until your bags are full then just spend the time creating the items with the least costs that are still orange or maybe yellow. At your level you could reach about 175 skill level if you happen to also find a bit of silver. I know this could be a bit daunting task as a new player, as knowing where to look for veins could be a bit tricky, but you'll learn that soon, or you could also get some addons that have built-in maps for such things. If you keep your blacksmithing level roughly parallel with [5 x your character level] you'll see that it can provide you with amazing items that will help you a lot in your levelling.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Protection Paladin Feels Off - Seal of Fury
content_md:
Yes. I respect what you want to do, I like to theorycraft, too but there are two things here I'd have a problem with.

 1. Prot paladin is already extremely buffed. They are the best dungeon tanks and they are perfectly fine to tank all contents (except for some raid bosses who really punish mana using tanks). If you further push them, you could push them from 'very strong' to 'game breaking'.
Unless the other builds get a new wave of buffs and pala would need ways to catch up, I see no options to buff them unless we give some and also take some. But this leads to my second point.

 2. It is true that palas don't have an aoe taunt but they are still the 'aoe specialists' among tanks. They are just the best at it. You want to buff them with something they are already really good at, instead of giving them something they lack (for example range pull or a rush-like effect). I don't say palas should have access to these but further buffing something they are currently the best at feels like a 'waste of design points'.

Under design points I mean an imaginary number. Optimally different builds get around the same level of investment with talents, abilities, buffs they bring etc. Every new ability or every new buff is a further investment into a build.
But pushing the same thing they are good at over and over again gets diminishing returns. The same 'amount of buff' at a place they struggle - or if we wanna keep blind spots for builds, in which they are mediocre at - gives a much bigger push to the build.

Threat for Protection Paladins in this server compared to original Vanilla WoW is already absurd -- it's reminiscent of WotLK+ P. Pal. PvE tanking.

If Paladins don't have a ranged pull, either get one, or have someone with you do it for you; Magic Candle, Crystal Charge, any Engineering Grenade or Bomb, as well as Engineering-made but non-Engineering-requiring Dynamites, any Class with a ranged option can do the pull for you and stand back or use Line of Sight while you pop a Buff on them or everyone around you -- which will grant massive Threat considering your (Improved) Righteous Fury, and then some. You get your back scratched, you scratch others' backs in return -- simply, cooperate. Worst-case scenario and cooperation sucks, you bail or turn to the above to instead cover for yourself, because knowledge is also just as strong.

Manage your Mana better. Spend it on more proper Threat production. Fix your Stat building. Get more practice. You will not need Mana Cost reductions to hold your hand and skip you practically all the aforementioned steps.

This is Fantasy, but not necessarily Power Fantasy -- you already have so much better to work with compared to what a joke your Class is as per the original release and even final progression of Vanilla.

author: Fortheking
subject: Divine steed ability but in Classic WoW (New custom quest for the Argent Dawn charger)
content_md:
Here is my proposal for the new custom quest for a paladin. First of all I have to say I foreshadow some toxic commentaries and sarcasm but I don't care. I've created this topic with hope that someone from Turtle WoW developers glances to this my suggestion. Also I have to mention that this is my very first topic ever and I never did it before and not experienced in this that much (so if it's made not professionally I bring my apologies). Also I will be glad if this topic isn't missed.

Here is the issue. I'm not the first one and not the last one who says that Paladin is terrible at PvP in case of lack of abilities that allow you to shorten the distance between you and your enemy. Paladin doesn't have these kind of abilities at all. And in purpose to compensate it I offer to create a new custom quest for a paladin which will be allowed since level 60.
This ability already exists in retail WoW (I'm not sure if it still exists or has been removed because I haven't played retail for a long time but I took inspiration from the Blizzards themselves so I haven't come up with this idea myself). The ability is called "Divine Steed". The main point of it: you're riding your horse in the heat of battle at some particular amount of time and during this time you're protected of being stunned or slowed down and at the same time you're allowed to keep using your regular skills (basically how real medieval knights did it, they didn't fight being dismounted). For those who don't know how it works here is the explanation from the wowhead:
<https://www.wowhead.com/spell=190784/divine-steed>

Now let me share my own thoughts how can it be implemented without breaking Vanilla WoW spirit. The early Blizzards were obsessed with idea of earning something really worthy after dealing with lots of trials and struggles (so this is basically what Vanilla WoW was about — the spirit of adventure). It can be compared to the shaman quests chain.
Here is how I see it: The quest chain starts at the Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. During this chain you will be fighting with battalions of undeads and scarlet crusaders. It leads you through both Eastern and Western plaguelands and aftermath brings you right to killing some elite mob or picking some item in the raid.
After proving your devotion to the Argent Dawn you receive the ability (the Argent Dawn charger itself) and the very important thing — relic.
If this ability will be OP? I believe if this ability is binded with wearing a scpeacial soulbound relic earned for completing this chain and is working only with wearing this special relic — this ability will not be over powered at PvP.
How should the ability work: I think it's up to the Turtle WOW game devs but I would like to see it exactly how it was in the official game.

This is what I think the horse itself should look like:
[https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowwi ... 1105124619](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowwiki/images/7/7e/Crusader%27s_White_Steed.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/732?cb=20091105124619)

P.s. I ask not to judge this my offer very strictly because Turtle WoW is a Vanilla + project opened to the different ideas. Also I hope at least someone reads it and finds this idea awesome.

https://www.wowhead.com/spell=190784/divine-steed

Now let me share my own thoughts how can it be implemented without breaking Vanilla WoW spirit. The early Blizzards were obsessed with idea of earning something really worthy after dealing with lots of trials and struggles (so this is basically what Vanilla WoW was about — the spirit of adventure). It can be compared to the shaman quests chain.
Here is how I see it: The quest chain starts at the Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. During this chain you will be fighting with battalions of undeads and scarlet crusaders. It leads you through both Eastern and Western plaguelands and aftermath brings you right to killing some elite mob or picking some item in the raid.
After proving your devotion to the Argent Dawn you receive the ability (the Argent Dawn charger itself) and the very important thing — relic.
If this ability will be OP? I believe if this ability is binded with wearing a scpeacial soulbound relic earned for completing this chain and is working only with wearing this special relic — this ability will not be over powered at PvP.
How should the ability work: I think it's up to the Turtle WOW game devs but I would like to see it exactly how it was in the official game.

This is what I think the horse itself should look like:
https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowwi ... 1105124619

P.s. I ask not to judge this my offer very strictly because Turtle WoW is a Vanilla + project opened to the different ideas. Also I hope at least someone reads it and finds this idea awesome.

content_md:
Im not gonna comment about the artistic and lore implications of this. But strictly on the spell as it relates to the gameplay.

For starters, this is a pvp only spell. In PvE most fights are stationary and the ones that do require you to move out of the way of something are balanced around the fact that players move at normal runspeed.

And precisely for pvp, this spell is absolutely misplaced in classic. It works in modern wow because all the classes paladin might run at have many more abilities to gain distance themselves or defensive utilities to prevent the paladin from just bursting wm down.

You might say, but warrior has a charge, rogue sprint, shaman ghost wolf and druid has even multiple ways to get into melee range quickly. All except druid can be slowed. Having someone who makes themselve unslowable with blessing of freesom just to rush at you with MOUNTSPEED while packing enough burstdamage thanks to their significantly buffed offensive potential has no place in classic or anything that wants to be classic adjacent.

Modern wow is a fun game all by itself, but if we end up retroporting steed, we have to retroport ever, classes mobility tools. At which point we can just play retail instead

I fully agree with the last post: Paladin is, by design, a hybrid, not a pure DPS class.
Because of that, its strength doesn’t come from spamming damage abilities, but from positioning, utility, and battlefield awareness.

From my perspective, the key is not to play Ret as the “tip of the spear,” but as a second-line tactician:
Frontline: pure melee DPS
Second line: hybrids/support (Ret/Enh/Feral) who can assist, peel, and adapt
Backline: healers and ranged

When played this way, Ret becomes far more enjoyable:
you can actively support your healers, protect teammates with timely Blessings, peel with stuns, assist with spot-heals, and still deliver meaningful damage when windows open.

It’s a role that rewards awareness and leadership, not button-mashing — and that’s exactly why the class feels unique.

Respectfully, by the Light.

– Sybril Dawnbreaker, Knight-Champion of the Light, Nordanaar

author: Azcron
subject: Re: Macros for paladin
content_md:
Hammer of Wrath if target have 20% hp, else Judgement
/run if UnitHealth("target")/UnitHealthMax("target") < 0.2 then CastSpellByName("Hammer of Wrath")CastSpellByName("Judgement")else CastSpellByName("Judgement")end

Divine Protection, Hearthstone
/run CastSpellByName("Divine Protection") for b=0,4 do for s=1,GetContainerNumSlots(b) do local n=GetContainerItemLink(b,s) if n and strfind(n,"Hearthstone") then UseContainerItem(b,s)  end end end

Blessing of Wisdom if target got mana, else Blessing of Might
/run power = UnitPowerType("target"); if ( power == 0 ) then CastSpellByName("Blessing of Wisdom") else CastSpellByName("Blessing of Might") end; if ( SpellIsTargeting() ) then CastSpellByName("Blessing of Might"); TargetUnit("player"); end

Seal of Light + Judgement
/run local i,x=1,0 while UnitBuff("player",i) do if UnitBuff("player",i)=="Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Holy_HealingAura" then x=1 end i=i+1 end if x==0 then CastSpellByName("Seal of Light") else CastSpellByName("Judgement")end

Seal of Righteousness + Judgement
/run local z=0 for i=1,27 do t=UnitBuff("player",i) if (t and strfind(t,"ThunderBolt")) then z=1 break end end if z==1 then CastSpellByName("Judgement") else CastSpellByName("Seal of Righteousness") end

Seal of Wisdom + Judgement
/run c=CastSpellByName j="Judgement" q="y_Righteou" function b(k)for i=1,32 do if strfind(tostring(UnitBuff("player",i)),k)then return 1 end end end if not b(q) then c("Seal of Wisdom")else c(j) end

Seal of the Crusader + Judgement
/run c=CastSpellByName j="Judgement" q="y_HolySmite" function b(k)for i=1,32 do if strfind(tostring(UnitBuff("player",i)),k)then return 1 end end end if not b(q) then c("Seal of the Crusader")else c(j) end

author: TurtleWoW<3
subject: Leveling Spec
content_md:
Hello everyone!

I'm new to the TWoW PvE Server, and due to the differences compared to the "other game," I'm not quite sure how to spec properly with all the tweaks here.

I'm aiming for a single spec from level 1 to 60, as respeccing is quite expensive and I’m starting with 0 gold. My goal is to have a survivable build that doesn't require much drinking between mobs.

From what I’ve read on forums and Reddit, some players recommend investing 7–8 points into the Holy tree first for the Intellect bonus and pushback reduction — which can be life-saving.
However, from what I understand, these talents might not be as crucial at early levels due to the server changes. For example, Holy Strike already feels like a nice QoL improvement in terms of kill speed (currently level 7 ![😄](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f604.svg)).

My current plan:
Focus only on Protection until level 30, taking Holy Shield as the final Prot talent.

Then switch to the Retribution tree until level 42 to grab Improved Run Speed.

At level 49, switch to Holy, pick up the Intellect and pushback talents, then finish off the Protection tree and take Kings last.

For gear:
I’ll be prioritizing:
Spirit > Intellect > Spell Damage (and if possible, more Spell Damage).

Does this approach make sense for a smooth leveling experience — basically becoming an unstoppable crusader? ![😄](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f604.svg)

Thanks in advance for your insights!

[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... AAAAAAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin?points=AoCAAAAAAAAAAAAoaAZZCABoAoAAAoAoAKAAAAAAAAA=)

author: Reploidrocsa
subject: Re: Leveling Spec
content_md:
For leveling there are essentially 2 ways: deep ret and damage focused on 1 foe. This one is the most standard way of leveling, doing quests and such.

Deep prot with spiritual focus from holy tree. This will give you less single target damage since you playing with mh + shield but allows you to slowly kill 5 enemies at once, which can be very effective if you want to focus on killing mobs and kill mobs related quests.

In any case, grab any free +int gear you can get (never ninja in groups, ask 1st) so you can go and heal in case you're needed. You'll do just fine with +int gear in dungeons until you reach your mid 50's

author: Zulnam
subject: Re: fresh lvl 60 prot or ret
content_md:
prot is a much better spec to level since it's more mana efficient than the other two specs.

if you are fighting melee mobs with no fancy abilities (stuns) then you can easily fight 5 at a time, sometimes even more depending on gear and mob level.

the 1h mace from ZG is much better than the epic sword, since it procs a inferior thunderclap, which is great for aggro and also increases your survivability when farming.

prot only struggles against caster mobs, which there are not many of.

also makes it very easy to join dungeons and prot paladin is probably the easiest dungeon tank out there.

author: Melfrato1
subject: Bulwark of the Righteous
content_md:
Greetings!

Playing Paladin Tank rn and I kinda feel that Bulwark of the Righteous doesn't feel very good as an "ultimate" you can only press every 5 minutes, therefore I would suggest a change, and you lot just tell me what you think about it.

Get Rid of the 30% less damage for 12 Seconds on the Ability.

Make it 8 second cooldown so it bascially becomes the equivalent to the Warriors Shield Slam and a constant Threat Builder.
Make it increase the Block Value by 10% for 10 Seconds. (Unneeded probably)
Equalize the dmg it does for the low cooldown, so its not too overpowered in Threat.

Add a 1/1 Point Talent to the left or right to that talent that turns your Divine Protection into a 5 Minute Cooldown that does the 30% less dmg for 12 Seconds. (Similar to warrior shield wall but weaker and on lower cooldown)

author: Soymage
subject: The Holy Paladin Problem
content_md:
Hi,

Let's jump right into the issues I see with holy paladins right now:

 ***THE IDEA OF HOLY PALADIN***

Conceptually, holy paladins seem to be an **"Endurance - Tank Healer"**. I have a big mana pool. My flash of light is very efficient. I can smack with seal of wisdom during downtime to stay at full mana. No other healer is nearly as efficient with mana usage and mana generation. But mana efficiency really does not matter 90% of the time because... if you or your other healers are not ever running out of mana (only happens a few times a raid in my guild, Kara40 and Naxx) it's just a wasted stat. It doesn't matter if I have 8k Mana if I have 50% remaining at the end of the fight (which happens often). Which brings me to my second point:

The healing is just sub-par to every other class, mainly shamans. Granted, the tank healing is superb. But there are so few fights where tank healing really matters... and here's the kicker: In 40 man raids, tank healing is mostly irrelevant anyways when you have 8+ healers spamming the tanks. When my guild needs to field 7/8 raid healers because of such heavy raid damage, we obviously keep those same players/raid healers on tank-healing-intensive fights, and there is really no noticed deficiency. We do not suffer for having more raid healers than tank healers.

 ***THE NUMBERS***

The REAL reason I am so frustrated with holy paladin is not really due to the concepts I just described. It's just down to the numbers. I am going to compare Paladin healing to Shaman healing since both classes tend to spam one ability (Flash of Light | Chain Heal):

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/gGNaUKT.png)
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/4NYXl4q.png)

Looking at these two spells, flash of light seems like a much more powerful and efficient spell. But we need to factor in a few things. Shaman's talent *Improved Chain Heal* reduces the cast time of Chain heal by 1 second. Chain heal is a 2 second cast, and it hits a second target for 50% healing, and then a third target for 25% healing.
Spell Coefficients: Flash of light has a 42% healing power coefficient (1.5/3.5). Chain Heal has a 85% healing coefficient (3/3.5). When you also factor in potential 2nd and 3rd target hits from chain heal, the heal is more like 964 - 1102 (148% coefficient). This is just insane.

If you "normalize" these two spells, that is, calculate how much they both heal in, say, 30 seconds, this is what you get:

Flash of Light: 428 - 494 (42%) * 20 casts = 8560 - 9880 + 840% healing power coefficient
Chain Heal: 964 - 1102 (148%) * 15 casts = 14460 - 16530 + 2220% healing power coefficient
Chain Heal (Single Target Only): 551 - 630 (85%) * 15 casts = 8265 - 9450 + 1275% healing power coefficient

Now, I understand that getting a perfect line-up for 3 full chain-heals 15 times in a row is unrealistic... but it does happen frequently, literally any time a strong AOE hits the melee dps or the whole stacking raid (Think Kruul, Anomalus, or Chess). And it is a smart heal, so it automatically selects people to heal for you. I could go on and on about this, but I'm actually not here to bring down Shamans. I hope I'm illustrating how far behind Holy Paladins are from other raid healers. Even if some of my math is wrong or im leaving out substantial talents/effects (even with a near-perfect setup of the holy talent Daybreak for 20% healing is not going to cut it), This gap is enormous. A holy paladin is getting more than doubled by a Shaman at raid healing. And in single target healing, the shaman is STILL healing the same if you factor in Daybreak for the paladin. The coefficient issue is the main problem here.

 *source - <https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Spell-Coefficients>*
(Note: the coefficient listed for chain heal at this link is likely incorrect. The cast time was 2.5 in classic, but it was increased to 3 sec in twow, then the improved chain heal talent was added. This would mean a higher coefficient. Even if I am wrong and the coefficient is still 72%, it won't change the idea of what I'm depicting here)

Shamans, Druids, and Priests all have ways of "breaking through" the standard spell coefficient. That is, they have something that makes their effective spell coefficients more than 100% healing bonus for every 3.5 seconds of casting. They do this through cast time reduction, HoT healing, or AOE healing. Paladins only have Daybreak, and that is clunky as hell to use.

 ***POOR ITEMIZATION***

Looking at the secondary stats that benefit healers (Healing Power, Crit, Cast Speed, Mp5), Paladins do not scale well with gear and are straight up BORING to itemize.

 **Healing Power** -> (No issues here. A great stat for everyone.)

 **Crit** -> Crit has never been that good for healers. It simply does matter when you crit and overheal. Overhealing is a huge problem especially with 7 or more other healers. The paladin's benefit for a crit is 60% mana refund and applying Daybreak for 20% extra healing on your target for 12 seconds. I already explained that mana gain as a paladin is not that good. I rarely ever get close to low mana anyways. Seal of wisdom smacking makes mana efficiency not that great. I will talk more about Daybreak later.

 **Cast Speed** -> Cast speed is normally an amazing stat... but unfortunately, flash of light is sitting right on the global cooldown (1.5 seconds). This makes cast speed pointless. There is no point in casting flash of light at 1.1 seconds if I am still locked to casting every 1.5 seconds.

 **Mp5** -> Mp5 is not great for the same reason discussed with crit. I don't need more mana.

So, as a paladin, you can't look forward to getting any of these stats because they are all just so clunky.
Shamans benefit heavily from all of these stats. They do not have an infinite mana gain like paladins do. Crit is great on shamans due to proccing Ancestral Healing on your tanks, and the fact that chain heal's second and third hits are much smaller than the main hit, you don't really risk overhealing on a crit.
Druids benefit more than paladins, but their hots lack the ability to crit or speed up with cast speed, so they are also slightly problematic in regards to these stats.
Priests also benefit more than paladins with these stats, but their flash heal is also at the global cooldown of 1.5, so they are in the same boat as paladins with cast speed.

As a side note, the Kara 40 holy paladin set bonuses are garbage. (3) buff to Holy shock, (5) buff to Holy strike. Really? I shouldn't even need to explain why this is bad. What a disappointment.

 ***WHAT I WOULD CHANGE***

Looking at Turtlogs.com right now, out of the top 30 healers for Kara40, only two are holy paladins. I won't dive further into this because statistics like these require a ton of nuanced discussion. It's not enough for me to say that there should be more paladin representation in statistics, but in my personal observations I have not seen many holy paladins topping the charts in any of the pugs or guild raids ive been in.

I don't believe in changing boss fights to fit holy paladins. We don't need to add more heavy tank-healing fights like patchwerk just to boost holy pallies ego. I don't believe in giving holy paladins an AOE heal. I want classic to stay true to classic. I think most of us want to avoid the homogenization that retail suffered from making every class able to do everything. That being said, here's what I suggest:

 **Create a global cooldown modifier.** Make it so that cast speed can reduce your global cooldown below 1.5 when your spell is faster than the global cooldown. This is good for all classes, not just paladins. I don't think this would interfere with classic's integrity.
 **Rework Daybreak.** Make the talent apply off all spell casts and reduce the bonus to 15%, or make it last 30 seconds, or make the healing bonus apply to everyone within 10 yards of your daybreak-ed target with one allowable target at a time, with in internal cooldown of 8 seconds, so Daybreak won't just swap around constantly (this is my favorite. I think Daybreak could have a large light effect like Beacon of Light, but I do not wish to add Beacon of Light to classic).
 **Rework Holy Shock** I really don't know how, but it sucks. Give it a lower cooldown. Make it deal damage again. Give it more range. Make it less reliant on crits and randomly resetting cooldown. It is seriously unfun when it either doesn't crit or doesn't reset itself.

I hope you all enjoyed my rant. My paladin is Soyknight on Nordanaar.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: The Holy Paladin Problem
content_md:
Decently put together post, but i got a few points i think are crucially lacking in this analysis.

 1. The abundance of gear, setbonuses, buffs and consumables on turtlewow to help with manasustain are a major reason why mp5 sucks. The stat as a whole is budgeted way too expensive for any healer to be excited about it. Paladin is only in so far most disadventaged here because he already didnt care about mana to begin with and he is the worst of the bunch when incorporating meditation gear for manaregen.

 2. Paladin heals only deal half threat compared to any other healers. This is a property inherited from actual classic, where blizzard was afraid righteous fury + healing threat would be too strong.

 3. Blessing of Light for a sizeable increase to healing done. since the effect however is static, it only scales with spellcrit and in the cast of holy light slightly with haste

But the conclusion remains correct. The distinguishing features paladin healer has, become less relevant as gear improves.

The only actual upsides a paladin healer can currently provide in high end raids are:
 - a longer lasting manapool to speedclear trash
 - a semi permanent ~500 hp for the main heal target thanks to daybreak
 - dispell of most type of debuffs from a single target in one gcd
 - the ability to play melee healer meme to support your raid with nightfall / dark iron sunderer for dps optimisations.

While paladin remains a class of many strengths, as a pure healer,he starts strong, but gets overtaken by other healers and their traits that are much more useful in difficault raid scenarios.

Off the top of my head, i dont think a gcd reduction really solves the issue. In fact paladin is the single worst healer scaling with haste even if it impacts gcd.
This is because haste is based on the base casttime of spells. Paladin hasno castspeed talent appart from the fast goly light after judgement.

The best ways for a pala healer would likely be a way to benefit from his crits without having to let the tank drop to a unhealthy degree everytime you wanna taje adventage of a crit (albeit flash has so low base amounts of healing that this is not q big issue)

And more crucially allowing him to throw more of his vast manapool out to actually heal by giving him a new healspell that is horrendously inefficient but allows you to actually convert the manasavings into hps while having little impact on the powerlevel where healers are still ooming.

Blessed strikes alone imo can not be the answer, a spell that doesnt cost mana should not be the bread and butter healspell it is becomong in aoe fights.especially if it pulls you in the direction of a support healer with tactical weapons, but then has absolutely crazy scaling with addheal. A large chunk of which comes from the weaponslot specifically

Fair points here! I am relying on turtlogs.com, and I can only see the effective heals per second. Im not sure how to view the full breakdown of abilities. Please let me know how to view more detailed statistics for this server, as I am currently unaware.

Saying that spamming FoL is "not the way to heal as a paladin" is... strange. It is the primary way of healing as a paladin. You realise that using holy strike, you can only heal raid members who are within 10 yards in melee. Ive used it a lot myself. I know that it is a very strong heal. Even without the Kara 40 5 set, my holy strike heals about 2500-3k which is on par with a Holy Light (crazy!). But it is far too situational to consider. There are many fights like Kruul, Mephistroth, Rupturan (the most important fights, mind you) where there is tons of raid damage, but you just cannot use holy strike to much effect. But look, this really comes down to *actually acquiring the 5 set bonus*. You can't honestly expect Paladins to perform sub-optimally until they get the 5 set. I agree that holy strikes could be buffed, but it's not even an on-demand heal, so it can't be what Holy Paladins are based around.

Also, the Holy Light cast reduction from judgment does not increase your ability to heal (except when you bank the effect between encounters). It simply enables you to cast judgements without much loss of healing cast time. You still have to spend a global cooldown on a judgement anyway, which is time not healing.

content_html:
Decently put together post, but i got a few points i think are crucially lacking in this analysis.

1. The abundance of gear, setbonuses, buffs and consumables on turtlewow to help with manasustain are a major reason why mp5 sucks. The stat as a whole is budgeted way too expensive for any healer to be excited about it. Paladin is only in so far most disadventaged here because he already didnt care about mana to begin with and he is the worst of the bunch when incorporating meditation gear for manaregen.

2. Paladin heals only deal half threat compared to any other healers. This is a property inherited from actual classic, where blizzard was afraid righteous fury + healing threat would be too strong.

3. Blessing of Light for a sizeable increase to healing done. since the effect however is static, it only scales with spellcrit and in the cast of holy light slightly with haste

But the conclusion remains correct. The distinguishing features paladin healer has, become less relevant as gear improves.

The only actual upsides a paladin healer can currently provide in high end raids are:
- a longer lasting manapool to speedclear trash
- a semi permanent ~500 hp for the main heal target thanks to daybreak
- dispell of most type of debuffs from a single target in one gcd
- the ability to play melee healer meme to support your raid with nightfall / dark iron sunderer for dps optimisations.

While paladin remains a class of many strengths, as a pure healer,he starts strong, but gets overtaken by other healers and their traits that are much more useful in difficault raid scenarios.

Off the top of my head, i dont think a gcd reduction really solves the issue. In fact paladin is the single worst healer scaling with haste even if it impacts gcd.
This is because haste is based on the base casttime of spells. Paladin hasno castspeed talent appart from the fast goly light after judgement.

The best ways for a pala healer would likely be a way to benefit from his crits without having to let the tank drop to a unhealthy degree everytime you wanna taje adventage of a crit (albeit flash has so low base amounts of healing that this is not q big issue)

And more crucially allowing him to throw more of his vast manapool out to actually heal by giving him a new healspell that is horrendously inefficient but allows you to actually convert the manasavings into hps while having little impact on the powerlevel where healers are still ooming.

Blessed strikes alone imo can not be the answer, a spell that doesnt cost mana should not be the bread and butter healspell it is becomong in aoe fights.especially if it pulls you in the direction of a support healer with tactical weapons, but then has absolutely crazy scaling with addheal. A large chunk of which comes from the weaponslot specifically
Wow, great response! I agree with basically everything here.

subject: Re: The Holy Paladin Problem
content_md:
I feel the problem comes from which other roles the class has.
Every other healer has a caster DPS build, granting them a base toolkit to do things from far besides healing.
Pala is in a weird space, having tank, melee and healer. In Vanilla holy pala felt super boring in PVE because as a healer you were supposed to stand at the distance and your distance toolkit was very limited.
Pala's other builds would offer the class a cool toolkit from melee range if a proper melee-ranged healer would be made possible.
TWOW tried it via CC2 but honestly, failed if we check the lategame.
If I had the option, I'd push for a viable melee-healer for holy pala.
Would be unique mongst the healers and would open up a bunch of abilities for the pala during fights (like occassional stun on a trash).

Healing output-wise I'd rather nerf healing numbers and mana elsewhere.

I miss the times where thinking about spell downgrades or not using quick heals to save mana really mattered.
content_html:
I feel the problem comes from which other roles the class has.
Every other healer has a caster DPS build, granting them a base toolkit to do things from far besides healing.
Pala is in a weird space, having tank, melee and healer. In Vanilla holy pala felt super boring in PVE because as a healer you were supposed to stand at the distance and your distance toolkit was very limited.
Pala's other builds would offer the class a cool toolkit from melee range if a proper melee-ranged healer would be made possible.
TWOW tried it via CC2 but honestly, failed if we check the lategame.
If I had the option, I'd push for a viable melee-healer for holy pala.
Would be unique mongst the healers and would open up a bunch of abilities for the pala during fights (like occassional stun on a trash).

Healing output-wise I'd rather nerf healing numbers and mana elsewhere.

I'm aware of the differences between macros and addons. The actual functional code of my rogue's macro is written in raw lua (specifically so it could be shared with people with 0 addon dependencies), the point was that i had enough space to spare even after that to fit in #showtooltip and /startattack after the fact, and that was just to make it look nice on my hotbar and to kick off autoattacking.

For reference, here is an entire assassination rogue's rotation in raw lua that fits in one macro without any #showtooltip or /startattack:

/run c=CastSpellByName p=GetComboPoints() g=GetPlayerBuff t=GetPlayerBuffTexture s=strfind if p==5 then c("Rupture")end
/run i=0 m=0 while not (g(i)==-1) do if (s(t(g(i)),"INV_Sword_31")) then m=1 end i=i+1 end if m==0 then if p<5 then c("Envenom")end end
/run i=0 m=0 while not (g(i)==-1) do if (s(t(g(i)),"Ability_Rogue_SliceDice")) then m=1 end i=i+1 end if m==0 then if p<5 then c("Slice and Dice")end end
/run c("Noxious Assault")
/run if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end

A better way to track CS/HS would be by actually checking the buff duration remaining. If there's less than 6 seconds left on holy strength, use holy strike, otherwise use crusader strike. If you're in prot, then just check if zeal is at 3 stacks, if it's not use CS, if it is check if it has less than 6 seconds left, in which case refresh it, otherwise just use HS

You're assuming that melee healing Paladins are strictly for "noobs," but that's a narrow take. The melee healing archetype isn’t inherently bad—it just has a higher execution requirement and demands proper encounter design and team synergy. Yes, they take more damage and face more interrupts, but they also bring powerful utility to the frontline: instant spot healing, blessings, and the ability to weave in melee attacks for mana sustain or proc effects.

The idea that ranged Paladins are the only "pro" option ignores the fact that some top players have optimized melee healing builds and found success in coordinated groups where positioning, interrupts, and utility management are tightly controlled. Not every healer should be a turret at 40 yards spamming heals.

As for gear—yes, the Kara 40 set seems built with the melee-healing playstyle in mind, but that doesn't mean it's "for noobs." It simply supports an alternative build path. And frankly, diversity in viable builds is good for the game. A ranged-only healing meta creates stagnation. Giving Paladins both a melee and ranged option isn’t just catering to skill level—it’s offering playstyle choice. And the best players will make either work depending on comp, fight mechanics, and strategy.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Melee Holy Paladin - Boss Fights
content_md:
Blessed strikes indeed incentivizes you to stand in melee range, but there are a few limiting factors.

The range on the Holy Strike healing is melee only. Depending on how many targets are in closeproximity to the mob, you might put yourself in harms way for no extra healing. Especially in dungeons where shield slams, silences or fears are being cast, thats a gamble that can backfire spectacularly.

Blessed strikes is mainy for raidhealing.

There it is vital that you know the bosses, as it is really good in some fights and trolling in others.

Bosses where you should usually avoid it:
MC: Gehennas, Garr(boss is ok, never stand close to adds), Shazzrah, Sulfuron Herald (ae stun), Majodormo (the firenovas hurt you more than you gain), Ragnaros (he targets manaclasses with an aoe knockback that tends to kill a lot of melees if it hits someone close to them)
BWL:razorgore(melee cc abilities), lashlayer (knockback), Chromaggus (the only target taking dmg is the tank anyway),  Nefarian (Fear)
Aq: Bug Trio(fights too chaotic you loose too much time moving), Sartura, Twins(can mess the tanks up and can get you killed if you dont know the fight in and out), Cthun (chance to kill melees on chaining)

Tldr: know the boss mechanics and only go in if you know for certain its an upsidd because while it is better to have the option to use blessed strikes, if you do it in the wrong fights you kill yourself AND others

So I'm not a "professional Ret Leveler" but I've leveled them many times. These are what my talents might look like at 30 & 50:
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... FoAAVCIAAI](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin?points=--FoAAVCIAAI)
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... oAAVCYYFIF](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin?points=F--FoAAVCYYFIF)

Useful tip to know is that Sanctity is -not- worth it until 60. Improved Retribution Aura helps you deal more damage overall since you don't have enough big numbers on Holy Damage, even on single-target mobs.

As for CS & HS: If you're able to keep your killing streak going, it's great to have 3 stacks of CS, then keep using HS. CS will do more damage than HS will but as you mentioned, drains mana. Just do CS once in a while to keep it up.
If you feel like you run out of mana during it, don't sit down and drink. Pop Seal of Wisdom and spend time on one mob to get your mana back, then carry on. I also recommend using "Blessing of Wisdom" as that will keep you going between fights.

If you can obtain the ring from Gilneas City that adds a "+3 Nature Damage" attack, great! That thing is considered it's own attack, meaning if you cast Judgement of Wisdom, you now have an extra proc chance on the Wisdom - and the proc chance on that judgement is very high.

When I use Crusader I am oom after 2 or 3 mobs, with Holy Strike, whilst TTK is slower, I never have to sit down and drink so I feel my overall speed is much better with HS instead of CS.

Curious to know why people still spam CS oder HS.
So I'm not a "professional Ret Leveler" but I've leveled them many times. These are what my talents might look like at 30 & 50:
https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... FoAAVCIAAI
https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/paladin? ... oAAVCYYFIF

Useful tip to know is that Sanctity is -not- worth it until 60. Improved Retribution Aura helps you deal more damage overall since you don't have enough big numbers on Holy Damage, even on single-target mobs.

As for CS & HS: If you're able to keep your killing streak going, it's great to have 3 stacks of CS, then keep using HS. CS will do more damage than HS will but as you mentioned, drains mana. Just do CS once in a while to keep it up.
If you feel like you run out of mana during it, don't sit down and drink. Pop Seal of Wisdom and spend time on one mob to get your mana back, then carry on. I also recommend using "Blessing of Wisdom" as that will keep you going between fights.

If you can obtain the ring from Gilneas City that adds a "+3 Nature Damage" attack, great! That thing is considered it's own attack, meaning if you cast Judgement of Wisdom, you now have an extra proc chance on the Wisdom - and the proc chance on that judgement is very high.

The issue regarding the Paladin's Improved Seal of Righteousness (SoR) talent is that the additional holy damage of the spell effect in terms of melee attacks do not increase, and only the Judgement of SoR's damage increases.

author: Tankmeister
subject: Feedback on holy and prot paladin after leveling to 60
content_md:
(*this post was formatted using AI for better readability)*

I’ve played Paladin since retail Vanilla, through Wrath, and into Cataclysm. First, I want to commend the Turtle WoW team - this is by far the most fun version of Paladin I’ve experienced in WoW. After leveling to max and spending a lot of time in dungeons (and a few raids), here’s my feedback:

Protection

 **Positives**

Seals and Judgements finally feel impactful. Choosing the right seal/judgement in the moment feels somewhat strategical.

The Reckoning redesign is fantastic. Having it proc immediately, and on block, makes sense thematically and feels rewarding.

Having a taunt is just good.

Converting some blessings into hand spells is a welcome quality-of-life change.

 **Mixed Feelings**

Bulwark of the Righteous is a great addition with both offensive and defensive utility. That said, a 5-minute cooldown feels like a lot. I’d personally prefer a slightly weaker version that could be used more often.

Holy Strike and Crusader Strike are excellent concepts but currently feel underutilized. Right now, I just use Crusader Strike to keep Zeal up, and otherwise Holy Strike. I’d love to see more meaningful choice regarding these two abilities:

Holy Strike: a supportive option - perhaps by providing a short party buff (e.g. a 6-second damage boost). Or just significantly increasing the healing done.

Crusader Strike: a survival tool, enhancing my defenses (also for 6 seconds).

Right now, the Holy Strike heal is simply too weak to matter and Crusader Strike just feels like a chore you have to keep doing.

 **Negatives**

Eye for an Eye should be available to Prot again. It was the only real tool against casters in PvP, and it fit the Paladin fantasy very well.

Holy

I’ve never really played as a healer in WoW before. Standing at the back spamming heals never appealed to me. But Turtle’s melee-healer design tempted me to try Holy, and I’m surprised by how much I enjoy it.

 **Positives**

The melee healing playstyle is fun and engaging. Even if I’m not dealing huge damage, being in the fight and seeing damage numbers alongside heals just feels better.

 **Mixed Feelings**

The interplay between Holy Strike and Crusader Strike works better here than in Prot. Timing Crusader Strike to refresh Holy Shock vs. using Holy Strike for healing/mana management feels meaningful. But again, Holy Strike’s heal (even with Blessed Strikes) is far too weak. I’d prefer if Holy Strike had a more impactful heal, and compensating with lowering healing from other spells. That would add a conscious choice between “healing one vs. healing many” to the gameplay.

 **Negatives**

Daybreak feels underwhelming and uninteresting. It could be much more engaging if it were an activated ability. For example, alongside its current effect, it could make your next heal a guaranteed crit. This would also synergize nicely with Holy Strike, since the only time it feels impactful is when it crits and procs Daybreak.

Closing Thoughts

Overall, I think Paladin on Turtle WoW has had a lot of great improvements. Fun, unique, and closer to what I always wished the class had been in retail. However, it leaves a lot more to be desired and improved upon, and I hope the dev team continues to realize this hidden potential.

I'm ok with the amount of healing I get out of it especially once healing gear has been stacked.

author: Dogfight
subject: Paladin evolution suggestions
content_md:
Paladin on Twow is in a good state imo. All specs are viable and enjoyable to play, Twow has done a great job here. However, class balance is always ongoing and classes are still evolving. So here are some suggestions for paladins.

 **1. Ranged Pull**
I know, I know, we do have gimmicky items, dynamites, our BFF hunter to pull for us etc, and we make do. But most of the items and dynamites have a 1min cd minimum, which is too long cd when you're chain pulling, and/or shares cooldown with other items you'd want to use in combination with the pull (Sappers i.e). And when you have a milisecond to pull that patrol before it is too late, then it's too late to ask the hunter. It would be convenient to have our own ranged pull. So if Twow decides to give us a ranged pull, here are a couple of suggestions:

 **a) Mark of the Crusader**
 30yd range, 10 sec CD, puts you in combat and generates a tiny amount of threat.
Puts Mark of the Crusader on the target for 10 sec, increasing Holy damage taken by up to 140.

 - CD reduced by 1/2 seconds with Imp Judgement talent
 - Holy damage bonus increased with current Imp SotC talent

Remove Seal of the Crusader and remake Judgement of the Crusader into Mark of the Crusader as a ranged pull. Seal of the Crusader isn't being used very much imo. Judgement of the Crusader on the other hand, is very much used in dungeons, raids and perhaps even by some levelers. Unless you're leveling weapon skill on a target dummy, then I'd say most of us won't miss not having SotC.

 **b) Mark of Justice**
 30yd range, 10 sec CD, puts you in combat and generates a tiny amount of threat.
Puts a Mark of Justice on the target for 10 sec, preventing the enemy from fleeing.

 - CD reduced by 1/2 seconds with Imp Judgement talent

Judgement of Justice is seeing little use and is very niche. Seal of Justice is also niche, but has a clear usecase against casters. So I see this as a bigger sacrifice than losing SotC. You could perhaps make JoJ a 30yd range, but then you'd have Judgement on cd for your threat opener - which is not ideal. All in all a worse alternative than Mark of the Crusader.

 **2. Hand of Sacrifice remake**
Hand of Sacrifice was mostly used for breaking CC in PvP and PvE. Now that it doesn't work anymore it is more or less useless. Suggestions for a remake:

a) Let the damage transfer scale with healing power and reduce the duration to 10 sec. Possibly cap the damage transfer at XX % of the paladins health. Could be a useful tool for holy, prot and SP/Hybrid rets.

b) Remake it into an Argent Defender type of spell. The next attack within 5 seconds that brings the target below 35% health will have 30% of its damage transfered to the paladin instead, up to a maximum of 50% of the paladins health. Or just not have a maximum damage transfered at all for some light comedy when someone actually sacrifices themselves and dies to save others. Numbers as an example and it would need a fairly long cd. Possibly 30min so you have something to do while waiting for LoH to come off cooldown again, right?

c) Possibly let HoS reduce the duration of CC effects by XX %? Doesn't really fit namewise, but it is what we mostly used it for - preventing CC. Could be a standalone effect or in combination with alternative a). Not sure if I like this personally, but throwing it out there.

 **3. Gap closer and better mobility?**
Mobility is obviously a weakness of paladins. Not saying we must do something about this, because classes should be unique, but here is an idea anyways.
In TBC we had 15% run speed increase through PoJ to function as a gap closer and improved mobility for us. How about if Guardian's Favor reduced the CD of Hand of Freedom, but also increased run speed of the target by 4/8% for the duation. Stacking with other run speed increasing effects ofc.
That would make it a utility spell both for ourselves and others.

Let me hear your thoughts.

author: Azcron
subject: Re: What are the stats priority for leveling paladin
content_md:
Prot pally is really all about stamina and strength. Once you hit level 20 and pick up Seal of Wisdom, mana just isn’t the issue people make it out to be. You’ll regen enough through SoW that you don’t need to stack Spirit. If it’s on a piece you’re already using, that’s fine, but it’s not something you should go out of your way to hunt down.

What actually pays off is stamina for survivability and strength for threat and block value. Some folks like going heavier into intellect for a bigger mana pool, and that’s not wrong, but it’s more of a comfort choice than a necessity. By design, your kit already handles your mana problems, so what really matters is staying alive and holding aggro.

And if you happen to come across gear with spell damage, that’s worth considering too. It’ll give your threat output a nice boost, which makes life easier for you and your group.

It directly boosts the effectiveness of several key spells that form  your threat generation and utility. Consecration, for example, scales with Spell Power, making it far more potent for AoE tanking and holding packs. Holy Shield benefits as well, not just by increasing your block chance, but by amplifying the reflective damage you deal every time you block, which translates into passive threat. Holy Strike is another important ability that scales with Spell Power, offering reliable single-target burst and synergizing well with a caster-oriented tank setup. Seal/Judgement of Righteousness also scale with Spell Power, which is especially valuable since Prot Paladins don’t rely heavily on weapon damage. While Crusader Strike does have some Spell Power scaling, I wouldn’t recommend using it in a Prot build as it's a mana waste and doesn’t offer the same threat or utility as the other abilities mentioned.

Doesn't matter at all during leveling.

Just take whatever piece of equipment you can find that provides a lot of stats and armor.

The impact of stats is marginal especially early on. You'll waste more time trying to "optimize" yourself playing a very easy game, even more so as a paladin, than you would by just sticking to killing mobs/questing/xping.

If you just want to tank, just stack armor and stamina, and that's about it. Paladins are already god-tier at holding aggro, no one will ever compete with you inside a consecration. You don't need to optimize for it.

That’s not completely true. While it’s right that your main aggro tools (SoR, Judgement, Consecration) scale with spell damage, strength still has an indirect impact. It increases your block damage, and block damage directly boosts the damage from Holy Shield.

I tested this swapping between strength-heavy gear and gear without it, and you can see the difference, every block with Holy Shield hits harder when your block value is higher. Since that’s holy damage, it benefits from Righteous Fury as well, which means more reliable threat when you’re tanking packs.

So no, strength isn’t on the same level as spell damage for raw threat scaling, but it’s not useless either. It helps with Holy Shield, which is a big part of holding aggro as a prot pally.

content_html:
What actually pays off is stamina for survivability and strength for threat and block value
Strenght wont improve your threat in the slightest. All your aggro comes from holy damage. None of your aggro generating spells/attacks scale with strenght
That’s not completely true. While it’s right that your main aggro tools (SoR, Judgement, Consecration) scale with spell damage, strength still has an indirect impact. It increases your block damage, and block damage directly boosts the damage from Holy Shield.

I tested this swapping between strength-heavy gear and gear without it, and you can see the difference, every block with Holy Shield hits harder when your block value is higher. Since that’s holy damage, it benefits from Righteous Fury as well, which means more reliable threat when you’re tanking packs.

So no, strength isn’t on the same level as spell damage for raw threat scaling, but it’s not useless either. It helps with Holy Shield, which is a big part of holding aggro as a prot pally.

author: Schlaechter
subject: Re: What are the stats priority for leveling paladin
content_md:
Go Mail/later Plate with Stam, most of the time you will got Strengh, sometimes there are "...of the Eagle" Greens with Stam/Int, take them. But Stamina and high Armor is all you need. Later you will find Items with +Defense or +Avoidance (Parry/Dodge/Block).
Later on Plate there is +Spelldamage and in the late 60s Dungeons you will finally find Items with Stamina + Intelligence + Spelldamage + Defense.

Untill then just run for Plate with Stam/Def-Stats: Survivability is more important than Threat.

With no Int you will have a poor Manapool, so Regeneration through Seal and Judgement of Wisdom is important. Therefore allways use fast weapons (with +spelldam as a nice to have)! Weapon Damage is not important for threat, only Crusader Strike scales with weapon damage. But try to keep Zeal up! Faster hitting=more Mana! Thats why +attack speed is also a nice stat. And try to keep at least one item on you with "adds +dmg to your attack"(<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=16615> or <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=7711>). This extra damage on attack triggers Judgement of wisdom! Game changing!

Another notable thing is <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17774> and other "when struck" items. You got hit a lot.

Hi friend, I haven't yet entered dungeons, as I said I am speaking solely for the leveling experience (which is a big element of vanilla wow hence I feel servers that are vanilla-esque ought to pay attention to its wellbeing) - for that leveling experience, I feel like Crusader Strike is too much as it is.
Judgement of Righteousness at level 10 deals about 25 holy damage. It is a very good nuke at 10 seconds cooldown.
Plagued by the fact that is the only on demand nuke of the class for long (or forever for Ret) and that casting it means abolishing your combat system (your seals). Furthermore you can't even cast it if someone decides to constantly dispel your combat system (your seals).

Undoubtedly paladins needed some improvement and the careful introduction of an extra on demand damaging ability was long overdue.

Holy strike deals about the same damage as judgement while being on a 6s cooldown, it is in melee range but it is independent and doesn't require an active seal, neither does it consume one. Even if it were on a 10s cooldown (like judgement) it would effectively mean double the amount of damage and on demand strikes.

A definite improvement right? The numbers are quite clear.
Now taking it to 6s right off the bat is kind of questionable but borderline swallow-able. But enter Crusader Strike doing 31+35% weapon damage, so about 35-38, is kind of too much. It makes me considering not using it while leveling even. That on top of a great passive buff it gives.

 **Imo to preserve the leveling experience:**
- Crusader Strike + Holy Strike should start on an 8/10s cooldown.

- Crusader Strike should be 100-110% weapon damage always plus its zeal effect.

- Both Strikes through their respective tree 5 pointer boooster should receive 0.4/0.8s cooldown reduction (taking them back to 6s with the 5 talents).

- Through the same talents receive as much of a damage boost as necessary to preserve end game DPS to what it is now or what is always necessary for the specs to be viable (as you said it's fine)

From my experience in dungeons so far, we don't stand out from the DPS table. Even in early dungeons like WC and Deadmine. We're good, don't get me wrong, but other classes do well too, and we're just fine as we are now.
Hi friend, I haven't yet entered dungeons, as I said I am speaking solely for the leveling experience (which is a big element of vanilla wow hence I feel servers that are vanilla-esque ought to pay attention to its wellbeing) - for that leveling experience, I feel like Crusader Strike is too much as it is.
Judgement of Righteousness at level 10 deals about 25 holy damage. It is a very good nuke at 10 seconds cooldown.
Plagued by the fact that is the only on demand nuke of the class for long (or forever for Ret) and that casting it means abolishing your combat system (your seals). Furthermore you can't even cast it if someone decides to constantly dispel your combat system (your seals).

Undoubtedly paladins needed some improvement and the careful introduction of an extra on demand damaging ability was long overdue.

Holy strike deals about the same damage as judgement while being on a 6s cooldown, it is in melee range but it is independent and doesn't require an active seal, neither does it consume one. Even if it were on a 10s cooldown (like judgement) it would effectively mean double the amount of damage and on demand strikes.

A definite improvement right? The numbers are quite clear.
Now taking it to 6s right off the bat is kind of questionable but borderline swallow-able. But enter Crusader Strike doing 31+35% weapon damage, so about 35-38, is kind of too much. It makes me considering not using it while leveling even. That on top of a great passive buff it gives.

Imo to preserve the leveling experience:
  • Crusader Strike + Holy Strike should start on an 8/10s cooldown.
  • Crusader Strike should be 100-110% weapon damage always plus its zeal effect.
  • Both Strikes through their respective tree 5 pointer boooster should receive 0.4/0.8s cooldown reduction (taking them back to 6s with the 5 talents).
  • Through the same talents receive as much of a damage boost as necessary to preserve end game DPS to what it is now or what is always necessary for the specs to be viable (as you said it's fine)
You speak from one perspective, ignoring any others. Open world leveling maybe important, so are other aspect of the game.

For instance, HS at 6s is perfect to keep aggro on the main target as a prot, even at low level. 8s/10s would mean no ways to maintain aggro. Clearly not good. We already struggle on packs until level 20 when we get consecration. Now you suggest that we shouldn't tank whatsoever before 20.

Level up a bit more, play other classes, then you'll get a better idea where pallys stand.
But how would you preserver the leveling experience then?
Currently I am playing a class that was auto attack heavy and now a warrior is more auto attack heavy than me while leveling, while I also have my heals and blessings and seals.

You have to also remember that free instant strikes like Mortal Strike, Whirlwind and Crsuader Strike, the Warrior only starts getting at level 36. I use the warrior as the example of the prime Melee class and I don't think a Paladin should so violently shortcut into it.

People do care, which is why these spells had to be coded to not proc extra effects. A big reason for this is burst damage. Paladin is already one of the burstiest classes as is.

Currently, Auto Attack + SoC procc + Crusader Strike can already almost kill questmobs with a bit of critluck in one go. If you add another Proc to it there is a good chance your questing, farming and pvp encounter end in the first second you get into melee. This is exasturbated once you  get swing increases such as wings of the timelord, hoj or other similar effects. Especially with WF in the mix. That might be fun for a few hours as a milestone to reach, but it considerably dulls gameplay down afterwards.

To give you an example of how much (by current balance figures unnecessary-) power that is:
You could increase the damage of ret paladins seals by 50%(!) and it would still be less strong.

On hit modifiers such as wf & seals dont mix well with instant attacks. Which is why shaman and pala are nightmares to balance, and always will be.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Another Paladin fanfic talents rework
content_md:
Lets start with the ideas i like.

Evil is a point of view is a great talent both flavorwise and gameplaywise if you ask me. As it taps into the more sinister aspects of blind faith, befitting a ret paladin.
It should however be limited to damaging abilities. Paladin should not gain access to a widely useable fear spell. Particularly not in conjunction with any other of the massive buffs that you intend for the class.

Consecration being useful as a healspell would be a great addition to healpaladin, as they struggle from not having enough buttons to press. Making consecration be useful for them would be great. However it definitely needs some tweaking. As "all friendly targets" in some fights can mean upwards of 1k hps per paladin.
Id rather have it say "up to x friendly targets inside the area get healed for half that amount". Keeping its usefulnes while limiting the abuse potential of just stacking the raid in a ball and dropping some consecrations. (Especially since tank and retpalas can come and pick the talent uo with very little downsides).
Or simply limit it to the paladins group.

Searing light might be fun to enable a more spellcaster type paladin. But with the numbers given, it is undoubtably a meme. Which i think is good. Paladin has some playstiles. He doesnt need to be good at range too.
Hereim just worrying about tankshaman syndrome where over time it will get buffed to an unreasonable degree because people adore a meme spec. Creating a lot of problems in the future in other game areas (particularly pvp as was the case with shaman and pala in the past)

Now for the stuff i dont like at all
Bullwark of the righteous
Is hitting people with your shield cool as hell? of course!
Is it also brutal and slightly dirty and undoubtably a warrior ability? Also yes!
With the current threat and dps numbers, tank paladin does not need to pilfer the one cool thing prot warrior has in his arsenal.

Northshire abbey training replacing precision and the removal of imp hand of reckoning leave paladin with wanting 17% spellhit for their taunt. Warrior and Druids both have secondary taunt effects (aoe taunt/mocking blow) in a pinch if their taunt misses. Paladin (and Shaman) dont have that. They need their taunt to be more reliable. And the respective spellhit talents are vital for them being reliable at taunting.

Radiance & the change to divine shield i am absolutely not a fan of. It gives tank paladin access to the single hardest hitting aoe ability in the game.
And at the same time it takes away ita debuff cleansing properties. The best thing abour current divine shield!

Then there is the mess that is conviction into holy cleave into vengeance.
Why am i forced by prerequisite talent to improve them both? These abilities are sharing cd. If they have separate talents, I should have the option to invest in one and not the other!

It also is a 15 pt chain that you basically have to take towards the end of the tree. Ensuring you have to invest far more than 31 points and overinvest into the tree (something that has sadly become all too common with the reworked talent trees)

Another one that ruffles my feather is the buff to imp. Hammer of justice. Base cd is 60 seconds. With the talent it goes to 40. With the pvp setbonus a further 10 seconds and libram of the justicar nabs another 5 seconds.

As 25 second cd 20y ranged stun that lasts 6 seconds... No thanks
When suggesting talents please ensure you are aware of what interactions that are already in the game you are impacting.

author: Maxe71
subject: Suggestion: Seals & Blessings Are Too Easily Dispelled (Need a Talent-Based Solution)
content_md:
Hi fellow Paladins and Turtle WoW team,

I’d like to bring up an issue that many Retribution and Holy Paladins feel very strongly about, especially in PvP:
our Seals and Blessings are extremely easy to dispel, and this leaves the class unable to function during combat.
Paladins are heavily dependent on both Blessings and Seals to do anything — pressure, utility, mobility, damage, healing flow, you name it.

But right now:
One single dispel can remove Blessing of Freedom, Blessing of Protection, or Blessing of Sacrifice instantly.
Seals are removed just as easily, shutting down core abilities like Judgement, burst windows, or defensive play.
Classes with strong dispel tools can lock a Paladin out of almost everything with very little effort.
Because of this, Paladins often end up in situations where they simply cannot play their class, despite using their tools correctly.

Proposed Solution: A Talent That Protects Seals & Blessings
My suggestion is to introduce a new talent or position in one of the Paladin trees that:
Makes the Paladin’s own Seals and Blessings immune to dispel,
OR
Gives them a very high chance to resist dispels (e.g., 50–75%),
OR
Applies a buff that temporarily prevents dispel effects after casting a Seal or Blessing.
This would give Paladins a fair chance to actually use their toolkit without being shut down completely by a single dispel spam.
It wouldn’t make us overpowered — it would simply let us function.

Final Thoughts

Just my two cents to improve class balance and gameplay feel.
I love the server and appreciate all the work the creators have done.
Thanks for reading, and I’d be glad to hear the thoughts of other Paladins and the dev team.

content_md:
I understand the point about dispels being the counter to buffs, just like kicks counter casts.
But there’s an important difference here:

A Paladin without seals or blessings doesn’t just get “countered”—he loses his entire kit.
Other classes don’t become “unplayable” when you remove a single component of their rotation.

A Priest doesn’t just stand still spamming dispel—he applies DoTs, Mana Burn, SW:D pressure, so while he dispels my seal, I’m also rotting at the same time.

Same with Shamans: even if purge now has a CD, they still keep massive burst windows (WF + shocks + CL) that a Paladin has no tools to smooth out, except bubble—which is purely defensive, and cuts our offense in half while it’s active.

My point was never that “counters shouldn’t exist,” but that no other class becomes completely neutered by a dispel the way Paladins do. Something that gives partial resistance, or reduced dispel success, or a talent that stabilizes at least one core seal, would prevent the class from collapsing the moment a dispeller is present.

Just my 2 cents, fellow Paladins—and devs.
